### `found-24-sep/task-edits-narrower-than-clickup` — **closed** (behaviour, medium; found closing the linked-docs item, researched)

**Only a task's creator, an assignee or a manager may change it; in ClickUp, anybody with "edit" on its location may**

*Evidence (code read):* `assertTaskWriteAccess` (tasks.service) refuses every change to a task by a member who neither made it nor is on it: "Only assignees, creators, managers, and workspace admins can edit this task". That covers the title, status, fields, links, labels and attachments. The space's own level is asked after that (`assertSpaceAllowsTaskWrite`), so a member with "edit" on a space still cannot change a colleague's task in it.

*ClickUp's rule* (help.clickup.com "Intro to permissions", "Permissions in detail", "Default user role permissions", search snippets; the pages cannot be fetched here): a member invited to a workspace has full edit on every public location and item by default, and a location's level can be narrowed. "Edit" lets them edit every task and subtask there, including status, assignees, title, attachments, archiving, moving, merging and duplicating. "Full edit" adds creating and deleting. "Comment" allows comments, and on a task assigned to them a change of status or assignees. "View" allows nothing.

*To close:* decide it as ClickUp does. A change to a task asks the level the person holds where the task lives (`resolveSpaceLevel`, a grant winning over the default), not whether they made it or are on it; deleting asks for full edit. This widens who may write, so first measure every suite that relies on the narrower rule (`task-boundaries`, `task-space-levels`, the `workspace-read-access` link half and others that expect a 403 for a member's colleague's task), then change the rule once, in `assertTaskWriteAccess`, with a suite that sets the three levels side by side on a colleague's task.

*Measured, lane 5, on HEAD:* in a space the member may edit, they were refused every change to a colleague's task: its title and status, its assignees, archiving and deleting (403 each, the rows unchanged), with "Only assignees, creators, managers, and workspace admins can edit this task". The comment-only and view-only spaces and a private list's task refused them as they should.

ClickUp (help centre, search snippets): "Edit" lets a person edit all tasks and subtasks in the location, "status, assignee, title of the task, any ClickApps", remove attachments, archive, move, merge and duplicate; "Full edit" adds deleting and creating. Members hold full edit on public locations by default. "Comment" is comments, and "comment with task assigned" a change of status on a task assigned to them; "View" nothing.

*Closed, 25 September:* a change to a task asks the level its space gives the person (`assertSpaceAllowsTaskWrite`, as before), not whether they made it or are on it. First the read rule (`readableTask`): a task in a private list, project or folder they are not in is refused as it is to every read (404), whatever the space lets them do. That had been implied by the creator-or-assignee rule, and no longer is. Guests are unchanged: they edit no task (their edit on a task shared with them is `found-25-sep/guests-edit-no-shared-task`, below).

Rundesk's "edit" is the space default and already makes tasks, as ClickUp's default full edit does, so it is read that way here, deleting included. A space narrowed to ClickUp's "Edit", which archives and does not delete, has no level of its own here.

The new suite `task-edit-levels`, 5 checks: in an edit space, a colleague's task's title, status, assignees, archive and delete; a comment-only space, a colleague's task and one assigned to the member; a view-only space; a private list's task in an edit space, beside the admin's change; and what a refusal says. Each change is read back by SQL.

- Before (HEAD, lane 5): 3 of 5. The comment-only, view-only and private-list checks passed, as they must after the change too.
- After: 5/5.

`tel-1..4`, each compiled: creators and assignees only, writes that skip the read rule, the space's level not asked, and everybody taken for an assignee. Break run, lane 1 (`ddbd509`): 4 of 4 reddened, on a green baseline (5/5); `tel-1`, `-3` and `-4` were re-aimed the same day at the call that passes the task's chain (`project-roles-narrow-nothing`). Regression on lanes 2 to 5, the 64 suites that change a task through the API: 60 passed in the sweep. Two read a member refused a colleague's task as one who "may only read" it, in a space the member may edit, and are pointed at a task they may only read now: `linked-docs-access`'s space is comment-only (5/5), and `task-boundaries`' watcher checks use a task in its view-only space (45/45). `task-depth` and `addressability-live` failed in the sweep and passed on their own, 91/91 and 28/28 (`found-24-sep/three-suites-fail-under-a-full-sweep`). In CI (178).

*Found beside it:*
- A project's members' roles narrow nothing for a member: the Members sheet sets a member to View or Comment on a project, and every rule asks the space (`found-25-sep/project-roles-narrow-nothing`).
- The task sheet offers every edit to anybody who can open the task, and a comment-only or view-only reader is refused each one (`found-25-sep/task-sheet-offers-refused-edits`).

### `found-25-sep/project-roles-narrow-nothing` — **closed** (security, medium; found closing `task-edits-narrower-than-clickup`)

**A project's members' roles narrow nothing for a member**

*Evidence, measured on lane 5:* the admin made a space (edit, the default), a project, a list and a task, and put a member on the project as View (`POST /projects/:id/members`, 201; the Members sheet lists them as View). The member then changed the admin's task (200) and made a task in the list (201). Every rule a member meets asks the space: `resolveSpaceLevel` reads a project's grants for a guest (`within`) and not for a member. So the role the Members sheet sets for a member on a project is recorded and read by nothing. With `task-edits-narrower-than-clickup` closed, that View member may change any task in the project, where before only their own.

*ClickUp's rule* (help centre, search snippets): a location's permission can be set per Space, Folder and List, and the most specific one decides.

*To close:* a member's grant on the project (and on the list, where a list has members) decides before the space's level, as a guest's share does. Pass the chain from the task's writes, the task and list create gates and the container rules. Measure every suite that sets a project member's role.

*Measured, lane 5, on `ddbd509`:* the new suite below, 0 of 5. A member given View on a project changed the admin's task (200) and made a task (201) there; given Comment, they changed its title (200); given Edit on a project in a view-only space, they could change nothing (403). Only the list's rename was refused, by the list's own maker rule.

ClickUp (help centre, search snippets): permissions set on a Folder or List override the Space's, and the most specific decides ("full edit on the List but edit on the Folder"), in either direction.

*Closed, 25 September:* `resolveSpaceLevel` reads a member's grants on the item and the containers above it (`within`) before the space, as it read a guest's: their role on the project, and a share on the task, list, project or folder. The most specific decides, either way. A project's maker is seeded as its admin member, added by themselves, and that row is not a grant: making something is no exception to its space's level, as `assertCanManageContainer` already has it for a list's maker. The chain is passed from a task's writes, the container rule (a project's and a list's rename, archive and delete, and the project page's capabilities), and the status rule. The task and list create gates already passed it, for guests. A refusal by a project's grant says so ("Your access to this project is …").

The new suite `project-member-levels`, 5 checks: View on a project in an ordinary space (the task, a new task, the list, beside a project with no grant); Comment; Edit on a project in a view-only space (beside a project with no grant); the maker's seed row, then the same row given by the admin; and what the refusal says. Every change is read back by SQL.

- Before: 0 of 5.
- After: 5/5.

`pml-1..5`, each compiled: the member's grants unread, the maker's seed taken for a grant, the task's writes and the list's rule asking the space alone, and the refusal naming the space. Re-aimed at the new lines: `tel-1`, `-3` and `-4`, `tsl-2`, `sdp-2`, `sdp-5`, `swa-2`, `ppc-6`, and `gsl-3` and `gsl-6` (a member's grants have a loop of their own now; these are the guest's). In CI (179).

*Break run, lane 1 (`72c5bb7`):* `pml-1`, `-2`, `-3` and `-5` reddened, on a green baseline (5/5). `pml-4` (the list rule asking the space alone) left the suite green: its list was the admin's, and the maker rule refuses a member that rename whatever the project says, so the check could not tell. The check renames a list the member made now, planted by SQL, beside one in the project with no grant. ### `found-25-sep/lane-databases-drift-from-the-migrations` — **closed** (test tooling, small; found closing `project-roles-narrow-nothing`)

**Lanes 2 to 4's databases lacked four unique indexes and a dropped default; lanes 6 to 10 lacked two migrations**

*Evidence, measured:* `folder-create` failed on lane 4 ("the database accepted it") and passed on lane 5. Comparing each lane's indexes and columns with lane 5's: `rundesk_v2`, `v3` and `v4` had no `uq_folders_space_name_active` (0157), `uq_lists_project_name_active` (0147), `uq_saved_searches_user_ws_name` (0040) or `uq_task_calendar_links_task_provider_user` (0021), and `user_dock_configs.pinned_links` still defaulted to `'[]'`, which 0163 drops. That is the default the dock bug came from, so `dock-defaults` would have read a different product there. `rundesk_v6` to `v10` had neither 0160 nor 0162. `fleet-restart.sh`'s witness checks the newest migration that adds a column or a table, and a missing index or default is neither.

*Repaired by hand, 25 September:* the four constraints (no duplicates on any lane) and the default on lanes 2 to 4, and 0160 and 0162 on lanes 6 to 10. Every lane database now matches lane 5's and the pristine database's indexes, columns and defaults.

*To close:* a gate before a lane is used (`fleet-restart.sh`, and `verify.sh`'s staleness refusal) that compares the lane's indexes, constraints, columns and defaults with the pristine database, and refuses one that differs. Show that it catches a dropped index.

*Closed, 28 September.* Measured first: the pristine database was not a sound reference. It lacked 0164's default (`spaces.default_permission` `'edit'`, where the source and 0164 say `'admin'`), and so did lanes 6 to 10, which were restored from it. Lanes 2 and 4 had lost two foreign keys (`skill_connections.connection_id`, `workspace_member_custom_roles.workspace_member_id`).

The reference is `rundesk_schema_ref` instead: the pristine dump with the current schema source pushed onto it. That is what `fleet-sync.sh` does to a lane, and how CI builds its database. It is rebuilt, under a lock, when the schema source or the migrations change (16s).

`lane_schema_drift` (`lane-env.sh`) compares a database with the reference, line by line:
- columns (type, nullability, default), indexes, constraints and enums;
- leaving out index and constraint names, since push's `…_fk` and a migration's `…_fkey` are the same key.

It prints each `missing:` / `extra:` line. The gate is used in three places:
- `verify.sh` refuses a drifted lane with exit 9, naming what differs.
- `fleet-restart.sh` refuses to start one.
- The sweep's summary and the README list the new exit code.

Repaired on 28 September:
- lanes 2 and 4: the two foreign keys (no orphans);
- pristine and lanes 8 to 10: 0164 applied;
- lanes 6 and 7: the default (their rows' 0164 update waited for the suites running on them).

All eleven databases then read as no drift, and `pristine.dump` was re-dumped.

`schema-drift-selfcheck.sh`, in preflight: 6/6 on copies of the reference.
- The copy itself: no drift.
- A dropped `uq_folders_space_name_active`: named as missing.
- `pinned_links`'s `'[]'` default put back: named as extra.
- A foreign key dropped: named as missing.
- The same key renamed: not drift.
- A database that cannot be read: exit 2, not a pass. The first run of the self-check found the gate reading such a database as "everything missing", because `psql` was piped straight into `sort`. It reads psql's own status now.

End to end, the case this item was found by: with `uq_folders_space_name_active` dropped on lane 10, `verify.sh folder-create 10` refused with exit 9, naming the index, before the suite ran. The index was put back and lane 10 reads as no drift again.

### `found-28-sep/folders-changed-by-any-reader` — **closed** (security, HIGH; found by the deletion research for `role-editor-offers-unenforced-permissions`)

**Any reader of a space renamed, made private and deleted its folders, whoever made them and whatever the space's level**

*Evidence, measured on lane 1 (the build of `818f919`), probe then suite:* folders are changed through `spaces/:spaceId/folders`, guarded by `ResourceMemberGuard` (can read the space) and `space.create`, which every member holds. `FoldersService.update` took no actor, and `remove` asked no rule. So a member of a view-only space renamed an admin's folder, made it private and deleted it (200 each). A member in a space at Full edit did the same to folders an admin made. Only moving a folder asked the container rule ("This space's default permission is "View only"…", "Only the creator or a workspace admin can modify this folder"). Making a folder private hides its projects from everyone not named on it, so a reader could hide an admin's work from the rest of the workspace.

ClickUp (help centre "Permissions FAQ", "Set permissions on individual locations", search snippets): View changes nothing, Edit changes a location, Full edit deletes it.

*Fixed, 28 September:* `update` and `remove` ask the container rule as `move` did (`assertMayChange`). That is Edit to change a folder and Full edit to delete it; a grant on the folder decides before the space; the creator rule and managers' own spaces apply as for projects and lists. The route passes the actor.

`folder-change-rule`, 4 checks:
- Before: 2 of 4 on lane 1. The member's changes in the view-only space and to an admin's folder at Full edit were all 200.
- Unit tests: `folders.service.test.ts` 5/5. The delete test now asserts that the rule is asked at its delete level; update and remove refused by the rule write and audit nothing.

### `found-28-sep/doc-archive-and-delete-at-two-levels` — **closed** (permissions, small; found by the deletion research)

**A doc reaches the Trash at Edit through one route and at Full edit through the other**

*Evidence, read not run:* `PATCH /docs/:id {isArchived: true}` is allowed at Edit (`doc-update-fields.ts:29`, `docs.service.ts:595-616`) and lands the doc in the Trash (`trash.service.ts:171`). `DELETE /docs/:id` asks Full edit for the same result. ClickUp's snippets put archiving and deleting a Doc at Edit ("Anyone, including guests, with Edit permissions can archive and unarchive Docs"; "Guests with edit permissions can edit and delete Docs and pages").

*To close:* one level for both. Measure both routes at Edit and at Full edit, before and after.

*Closed, 28 September.* ClickUp (help centre "Archive and unarchive a Doc", from search snippets): "Anyone, including guests, with Edit permissions can archive and unarchive Docs", and "Guests with edit permissions can edit and delete Docs and pages". Docs are the exception to the location rule, where Edit changes and Full edit deletes. `full-edit-enforced-nowhere` had put a doc's delete at Full edit with the rest; this corrects it for docs.

Measured on lane 7 at `ad97e31`, `doc-trash-level` passed 2 of 5. The two that passed pin what stays: a Comment share neither deletes nor archives, and unarchiving at Edit works. The three failures:
- A member with an Edit share was refused deleting the doc (403, "that takes Full edit"), while archiving it through the doc was allowed.
- Archiving through the doc (`PATCH {isArchived: true}`) wrote the flag alone, with no date and no archiver. The doc sat in the Trash as nobody's, out of the archiver's own Trash and past their restore.
- A guest with an Edit share was refused deleting it.

Now:
- `DELETE /docs/:id` asks Edit, as archiving does. The "takes Full edit" refusal is gone with its only caller.
- Archiving through the doc records who and when, as deleting does, and unarchiving clears both.
- The share dialog explains a doc's Edit as "can change it, archive it and delete it", in the four locales.
- `full-edit-levels`' doc check is rewritten for the rule: a doc shared at Edit is renamed and deleted. `fel-11`, which made deleting ask Edit, is re-aimed to restore Full edit, and `dwl-7` onto the new line.

`doc-trash-level`, 5 checks:
- Before: 2 of 5 on lane 7.
- After: 5/5 on lane 7.
- Patches `dtl-1..5` each reddened the check they name (lane 1, at `96305b3`, baseline 5/5). The re-aimed `fel-11` reddened `full-edit-levels`' doc check and `dwl-7` `doc-write-levels`' (lane 2, baselines 8/8 and 5/5).

### `found-28-sep/docs-offer-no-archive-or-delete` — **closed** (feature, small; found closing `doc-archive-and-delete-at-two-levels`)

**The docs panel has an Archived scope and no control that archives or deletes a doc**

*Evidence (reading, 28 September):* `docs-panel.tsx` lists "Archived" docs in its rail and offers nothing that sends a doc there: no Archive or Delete in the doc's header, the rail or a menu. The API has both routes, at Edit. ClickUp archives a Doc "from Docs Hub, the Home Sidebar and Spaces Sidebar, Doc views, or from Docs Home".

*To close:* an Archive (and Delete) in the doc's menu, offered at Edit — which needs the caller's level on the doc in its payload — and Unarchive on an archived one. Measure a member at Edit and at Comment.

*Closed, 29 September,* with `doc-editor-open-to-readers` below. The level comes from the doc's capabilities (`GET /docs/:id/capabilities`, the checks its routes ask, which the share button already read), one query for the page and the button. The doc's header has a menu, drawn when there is something in it: Archive at Edit (the doc then opens in the Archived bucket, where the menu offers Unarchive, which brings it back to All), and Delete at Edit on a live doc, which sends it to the Trash and opens the next doc. Both land the doc in the Trash of whoever did it (`doc-archive-and-delete-at-two-levels`), so an archived doc is not offered Delete, which would change nothing. Four locales.

Measured on lane 2 at `f8a799d` before: a member with an Edit share was offered no menu at all, and nothing on the page archived or deleted a doc. After: the Edit share's menu offers Archive and Delete; Archive archives it as the editor's doing and Unarchive restores it; Delete puts it in the editor's own Trash; View and Comment shares get no menu. Checks 3–5 of `doc-level-controls` (below); patches `dlc-5..9`, `dlc-11`.

### `found-28-sep/doc-editor-open-to-readers` — **closed** (mirror, small; found closing `doc-archive-and-delete-at-two-levels`)

**The doc editor takes typing from someone who may only read or comment, and a refused save says nothing**

*Evidence (reading, 28 September):* the docs panel knows nothing of the caller's level: the editor is editable for everyone who can open the doc. `saveDoc`'s `onError` speaks only for a 409 (a teammate's edit); the 403 a View or Comment share gets is dropped, so the typing looks saved until the doc reloads.

*To close:* the caller's level in the doc payload, a read-only editor below Edit, and a refused save said. Measure a View share typing.

*Closed, 29 September.* Measured on lane 2 at `f8a799d` before: a View share and a Comment share were each shown an editable editor that took their typing, with Save and the formatting tools; and when an Edit share was lowered to View while the doc was open, Save answered 403 and the page said nothing. ClickUp: View and Comment read a Doc; Edit changes it.

The editor starts read only and is made editable only when the doc's capabilities say Edit; below Edit the formatting tools, the AI tools and Save are not drawn, and a "Read only" pill says why. A save refused for any reason but a teammate's edit (409, as before) is said with the API's own sentence ("Your access to this doc does not allow changing it"), and the level is asked again, so the page turns read only. Four locales.

`doc-level-controls`, 7 checks, a View, a Comment and an Edit share on one doc:
- Before: 1/7 on lane 2 (the API's capabilities, which were right).
- After: 7/7 on lane 2.
- Patches `dlc-1..11`, one or more per check: all eleven redden (lane 3, at `0911c6e`, baseline 7/7).
- In CI (229).
- Regression on lanes 1, 2, 3 and 7 at once, 49 suites: every suite that opens a doc, reads announcements, flags, the home page or the planner's What's new, and the 19 of `three-suites-fail-under-a-full-sweep`: 49/49.
- 29 September, under a four-lane sweep: the Edit member's check read the editor before the doc's capabilities had answered (`contenteditable` still "false", though the typing then took). The editor is read only until they answer, and says nothing meanwhile, which outlasted the network lull the suite waited for. It now waits until the read-only pill is drawn or the editor is editable (15 s at most), and fails in its own words if neither comes.

### `found-28-sep/announcement-views-counted-per-click` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found by the announcement research)

**An announcement's views count every call, and paused or expired ones accept views and dismissals**

ClickUp has no workspace banner (its nearest is a Chat post), so the rule is the product's own: a view is a person.

- A view is a row per person, `announcement_views` (migration `0165`, unique on the announcement and the person, as `announcement_dismissals` already was), and the count moves only when the row is new. The counts recorded before are kept.
- `view` and `dismiss` take a live announcement only (published, not paused, not expired), else 404, as for somebody who was never shown it; a dismissal is a view too, and both are written with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so two at once are one rather than the unique index's 500.

### `found-29-sep/platform-flag-switches-apply-nowhere` — **closed** (facade, small; found closing `role-flags-read-the-account-role`)

**The platform console's feature switches applied in no workspace, and each one added a row**

*Evidence, measured on lane 5 at `c55a088`:* the console switches a feature for the whole platform (`PUT /feature-flags/:flag`, `scope: 'global'`, no workspace). Turning Forms off answered 200, and a workspace went on resolving Forms on and serving its routes: a workspace read loaded only that workspace's rows (`resolveFromDb`), so a row with no workspace was never read. And the unique key ran over nullable columns with NULLs distinct, so the upsert never matched a platform row: each switch inserted another, and which one a read applied was the table's order. Forms had nine platform rows on lane 5.

*Closed:* a workspace read loads the platform's rows and the workspace's, and applies them platform first, then the workspace's, a role's, a person's — the more specific wins. A switch updates its own row, found with NULLs equal, under a lock per flag, and makes one only when there is none. Migration `0166` keeps the newest of each duplicate and makes the key NULLS NOT DISTINCT. The drizzle schema cannot say NULLS NOT DISTINCT: drizzle-kit 0.31 does not read it back, and tried to rebuild the key, asking about the table's rows, on every lane push, which failed without a terminal. So the rule is kept in code, and a database built by `drizzle-kit push` (CI's) holds one row too.

The seeded platform rows are all on (the default-enabled flags), so applying them changes nothing by itself; a feature the console had switched off would now be off in every workspace that says nothing of its own. Three checks in `flag-resolution` (above); patches `flr-1`, `flr-2`, `flr-4`.

### `found-29-sep/stub-mutants-time-out-unnamed` — **closed** (test tooling, small; found by the preflight for `commit-log/log-b7ee313-1`)

**Under load, a stub gate's mutant run could fail without saying why, and the gate called it "proves nothing"**

*Evidence, 29 September:* in a full preflight beside two agents' runs (load ~10), `check-s3-stub.mjs --mutate` reported "the list is empty whatever is in the bucket — it exited non-zero but named no case"; a second run with the model-stub gate beside it reported two others the same way; alone, 22 of 22 bite. Each mutant re-runs the whole gate: it waits 15 s for its stub to announce itself and is given 180 s in all, and a run ended by either limit exits non-zero with no case named, which the gate cannot tell from a harness fault.

*Closed, 29 September:* both stub gates (`check-s3-stub.mjs`, `check-model-stub.mjs`) wait 60 s for a stub to announce itself and give a mutant's run 300 s. A run ended by the timeout says so ("its run was ended after 300 s (SIGTERM): a loaded machine, not the rule"; shown with the limit set to 2 s), and one that exits unnamed prints its last two lines, so the next one names its cause rather than leaving it to be guessed. Both still count as not biting.
- The next preflight caught the cause. The run printed "(it said: at ChildProcess._handle.onexit …)": the mutant's stub had exited on EADDRINUSE. The gates drew their ports from their pid, `9300 + pid % 400` and `9500 + pid % 300`. Those ranges overlap each other, and stubs left by ended mutant runs were still listening in them (`found-29-sep/killed-mutants-outlive-their-run`). Both gates now take a port the OS chose (`scripts/lib/free-port.mjs`).
- `STUB_GATE_MUTANT_TIMEOUT_MS` sets the limit for a slower machine.
- After: the two gates together, 22 of 22 and 11 of 11, at load ~10.

### `found-30-sep/status-zero-passes-status-only-checks` — **closed** (test tooling, medium; found closing `suite-hygiene/apiAs-duplicated-62`)

**When nothing answers, the one client answers status 0, and 137 conditions in 57 suites compare the status with no lower bound**

*Evidence, 30 September (the agent's count):* the 105 suites whose copies answered 0 when nothing answered keep that answer, now the one client's default. Their checks compare a status below 300 or 400 with no lower bound 137 times. Most are ANDed with a read-back that a dead API would also fail. But a check that rests on the status alone passes with nothing answering: `dependency-read-access:111` and `related-task-access:95` would say "the member could open the hidden blocker" about a dead API. The 80 suites bound with `noAnswer: 'throw'` hold 165 more such comparisons, which the option keeps harmless.

*Closed, 30 September.* Measured first, at `8c1b727`: the suites' code held 389 status comparisons with an upper bound. In the 112 suites that bind the client the default way, 168 had no lower bound, in 61 suites: 162 in a check's condition, 4 in guards that throw (the two above among them), 1 in a helper a check calls and 1 in an `if`. The ledger's 137 were these lines on the older tree; the rest are in three suites added or moved since, and in a status held under a name of its own. The throw binding did not cover all of its own either: 26 more, in 12 suites bound to throw, read a hand-made `{ status: 0 }` (a step never taken, standing in for its answer, or a rejection caught into one) or a helper's own 0. `ai-value` caught the put-back's rejection into `{ status: 0 }` and passed "the workspace's own benchmark is put back" on it.

- `search-read-access`, the API gone at the admin's rebuild: 4 of 4 passed, and it exited 0.
- `lookup-read-access`, gone at the member's first open favourite: "…while they favourite the open ones" passed on five 0s.
- `dependency-read-access`, gone at its guard: it threw "the member could open the hidden blocker (0 … no answer)".

All 194 now read `ok`, which is what `status < 300` meant:
- 187 as `x.ok`;
- the four guards as `if (gate.ok) throw`;
- `flag-resolution`'s restore as `healed?.ok === true`, and `task-ai-bar`'s `< 400` as `ok`;
- `project-page-controls`' two bare numbers keep a floor.

Three answers a suite builds itself (`publishAs`, `makes`, `download`) carry an `ok` of their own. No suite was bound with `noAnswer: 'throw'` instead: none had more than seven, `ok` changes only the condition, and the binding would reject in each suite's `finally` too while leaving a placeholder's 0. No check sentence and no `EXPECTED_CHECKS` changed. `lib/fixture.mjs` is unchanged, so only the 73 edited suites' break logs drift.

Checks:
- `scripts/check-suite-status-floor.mjs --mutate`, in preflight and CI's verify job beside the api-clients gate, refuses a status compared with an upper bound alone where it can be 0: in a suite binding the client without `noAnswer: 'throw'`, or read from a name bound to a hand-made `status: 0` or to a helper that hands one back. It reads every comparison in code, not only a check's condition (the two examples above are guards), and never a check's message. A lower bound is another conjunct of the same `&&`: `>= 200`, `> 0`, `!== 0`, the status itself, or the answer's `ok`. A line is exempted only by `// status-floor: not-a-client | zero-fails`, and none is. At `8c1b727` (and `eff8b9c`) it finds the 194 sites in 73 suites; now none. 32/32 cases pass, and 32 of 32 mutations bite.

The gate passes on the merged tree, 32 of 32 mutations biting.

of its root's NAME anywhere in the suite holds `status: 0`. 8 of the 20 PLACEHOLDER guards this rule found are a

parameter to its callers' arguments), with a planted case each way and mutations that bite.

*Triage, 5 October:* reproduced on a lane. *Closed, 7 October*. The gate reads a status's name where it is compared. It resolves the name to the nearest function around the comparison that declares it or takes it as a parameter, else to the file's top level. A declared name is bound to what is written to it in that scope; a parameter is bound to what its callers pass in its place, each followed the same way, up to four calls deep. A name nothing declares, and a parameter whose function is never called by name (a callback handed on), are read file-wide, as before. Blocks inside one function are not told apart. One rule says what a value as written can hold (`zeroText`), and the file-wide reading and the scoped one both ask it.

- Over the 270 suites, the tallies are the same before and after: 207 comparisons with an upper bound, 163 of them on a status that cannot be 0; 200 guards and 37 notes, 218 on a status that cannot be 0. ### `found-30-sep/client-address-behind-nginx` — **closed** (security, small; found closing `found-30-sep/public-routes-unthrottled`)

**Behind nginx, every visitor may be one address, so each per-address limit is the whole site's**

*Evidence, 30 September, read and not measured:* production runs the API behind nginx (`deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml` binds it to loopback). Neither that file nor `deploy/env.production.template` sets `TRUST_PROXY`, and `main.ts` reads the client's address from `X-Forwarded-For` only when it is `true`. Unset, `req.ip` is nginx's for everyone: sign-in's ten a minute, and the public routes' 120 and 1,200, are one budget for the whole site. Set, `trustProxy: true` trusts every hop, and nginx appends to the client's own header (`$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`), so a client chooses its address.

*To close:* trust exactly one hop, nginx (`trustProxy: 1` or its address), and set it in the production compose. Check it through nginx with a forged `X-Forwarded-For`.

*Closed, 30 September* (by an agent on lane 3; merged and measured again here). The API now trusts exactly the hops it has. `TRUST_PROXY` is the number of proxies in front (`trustProxyFrom`, `apps/api/src/common/http/trust-proxy.ts`), and it is handed to Fastify as a number. Fastify's reference defines that as "Trust the nth hop from the front-facing proxy server as the client". nginx's `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` is "the 'X-Forwarded-For' client request header field with the `$remote_addr` variable appended to it". So behind nginx, `1` makes `req.ip` the entry nginx appended, never one the client wrote.

The other values:
- `true` is read as 1. It was Fastify's `true`, which trusts every hop and answers the first entry, the client's own.
- Unset or `false` means no proxy.
- Anything else stops the API at boot, naming the variable, and the boot log says which setting it runs with.

It is not an address list. Behind Docker the socket is the bridge gateway (docker-proxy relays the loopback port), not nginx's 127.0.0.1. A range wide enough to cover it would also trust a client on a private network.

Where it is set:
- `deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml` sets `TRUST_PROXY: ${TRUST_PROXY:-1}`, and `env.production.template` says 1.
- `deploy/README.md` explains it, with a check through nginx using a forged header.
- The vhost's comment names the hop the API trusts.
- The lanes run the API as production does (`lane_proxy_env`, in all four launchers), and so does CI's API step.

The same address feeds more than the limiter. The workspace IP allowlist and the security settings' `currentIp` saw Docker's gateway for everyone in production, so the allowlist could not tell one visitor from another either.

Checks:
- `auth-route-limits` (new) puts a proxy of its own in front of the lane's API. It forwards from 127.0.0.5 and appends the address it saw, as nginx does. Three checks:
  - the API reads a client's address as the proxy saw it, not the one it wrote (`currentIp`);
  - a client naming a different address on each of 11 sign-ins is still held to sign-in's ten;
  - a second client behind the same proxy has a budget of its own.

  Before (lane 3 on HEAD's API, which ignores `1`): the API read 127.0.0.5 for everybody, the counter was `127.0.0.5 | 12`, and the second client was refused with 429. After: all three hold; the counters are `127.0.0.3 | 11` and `127.0.0.4 | 1`, and no forged address appears.
- `trust-proxy.test.ts` (new, 5 tests) drives a real Fastify at nginx's socket for each value, including `true` and a CDN's second hop.
- Break patches: `arl-1` (every hop trusted again) reddens four checks: the API read the forged `198.51.100.23` as the client, and the forged-header burst was answered 11 of 11. `arl-2` (no hop trusted) reddens two: the API read `127.0.0.5`, and the second client was refused. `arl-13` and `arl-14` redden their unit tests.

### `found-30-sep/register-unthrottled` — **closed** (security, small; found closing `found-30-sep/public-routes-unthrottled`)

**The old `POST /auth/register` makes accounts with no limit, beside signup's ten a minute**

*Evidence, 30 September, read:* `AuthController.register` is deprecated but routed, and carries no `@RateLimit`. Each call makes an account and a workspace. The invitation routes (`claim`, `decline`, `preview`) and `sso/lookup` have none either.

*To close:* limit or retire `register`, decide the invitation and SSO routes' budgets, and check a burst on each.

*Closed, 30 September* (by an agent on lane 3; merged and measured again here). ClickUp documents limits for its API alone: "The ClickUp API applies rate limits per token", 100 a minute on Free Forever, Unlimited and Business, and 429 past it. Of invitations it says only that they "never expire, but the link in the email is only valid for a short time". Its help centre says nothing of limits on signing up, on invitations or on SSO (read through search results; the sites are blocked here). So the safe rule: per address, far above one person and far below a flood, and no route that makes an account without a limit.

`register` is limited, not retired. The web's `/register` page still calls it, though nothing links to it, and eleven suites make their people with it. The budgets are `AUTH_ROUTE_LIMITS`, beside the guard:
- **Ten a minute**: register, with sign-up's own policy object, and an invitation's claim (which makes an account or signs one in) and its decline.
- **A page's 120** (`PUBLIC_ROUTE_LIMITS.page`): opening an invitation's link.
- **60**: the SSO lookup, asked while an email is typed. Unlimited, it enumerated which workspace signs in with SSO for any domain.
- **30**: SSO's start and both callbacks. There is no password to guess through them, but each costs a discovery fetch, a code exchange or a signature check against every enabled SAML connection.

Past each, 429 with a Retry-After. The invitation sender's routes and SSO's settings are not counted. The eleven suites call `registerApi` (`lib/signin.mjs`), which waits out a 429 as `signUpApi` does and says so.

  - A burst one past each budget, in one fresh minute, is refused with 429 and a Retry-After.
  - Another address still registers.
  - After the window every route answers the same address again.
  - Before, on lane 3: every burst was answered whole, 3/17 in all. After: 17/17, three times.
- `auth-route-limits.test.ts` (new, 14 tests): each route carries its budget behind the guard, register's is sign-up's own object, the 11th registration from one address is refused, and the routes with a session are never counted.

### `found-30-sep/public-pages-read-429-as-gone` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found closing `found-30-sep/public-routes-unthrottled`)

**A public page refused for too many requests says its link is gone**

*Evidence, 30 September, read:* `clip-link-page.tsx` shows "This clip is not available" ("the clip may have been deleted") for any failure but a 401. `portal.$token.tsx` shows its not-found page for any failure. `custom-domain.ts` drops the branding without a word. The 429 says when to come back (`Retry-After`, and `retryAfter` in the body).

*To close:* on a 429, say that there were too many requests and when to try again. Check it by answering the page's request with a 429 in the browser.

*Closed, 30 September.* ClickUp documents nothing about its public pages being refused. HTTP defines 429 as "the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time", whose answer "MAY include a Retry-After header indicating how long to wait before making a new request" (RFC 6585 §4). So the page says the second part and then does it.

Measured first, on lane 5, with the refusal answered in the browser:
- the clip page said "This clip is not available";
- the client portal said "Portal unavailable";
- the public doc page said it could not be loaded, and none of them asked again.
- The portal also asks again every 45 seconds. When one of those asks was refused, or failed for any reason, the portal already on screen was replaced by "Portal unavailable": `isError` stays true beside the data it had.

The fix:
- `retryAfterSeconds` in `lib/api.ts` reads a 429's wait from the envelope's `details.retryAfter`, the rate limiter's; a 429 with none waits five seconds. The doc page reads its `Retry-After` header.
- `useRetryAfter` counts the wait down a second at a time and asks once when it runs out.
- `PublicBusy` says "Too many requests", "It will try again in N seconds", and offers "Try again now". It is used on the three pages, in four locales.
- The portal draws an error page only when nothing was ever drawn. A 404 says the portal is unavailable, and any other failure says it could not be loaded.
- A custom domain's branding, refused, is asked again once after a wait of a minute or less, rather than being dropped for the whole visit (`lib/branding-retry.ts`).

Checks:
- `public-pages-busy` is new, with 10 checks, registered in CI (249 in `postgres-harnesses`). Its refusals are answered in the browser, since a real 429 would spend the lane's budget for a minute. It covers the doc, the clip and the portal: each refused says so and in how many seconds, and asks again by itself once the wait is over; "Try again now" asks at once. A portal already drawn stays drawn when its 45-second refresh is refused (the page's clock is jumped 46 seconds). A 500 says the portal could not be loaded, and an unknown link says it is unavailable. Before, 1/10 on lane 5: every check failed but the last. After, 10/10.
- `branding-retry.test.ts` is new, with 5 tests.
- `pbz-1..10` are new: 8 aimed at the suite and 2 unit claims. The break runner measured the eight at 8c1b727 (lane 1): each reddens against a 10/10 baseline, `pbz-1` four checks, `pbz-2` and `pbz-3` three, the other five one each.
- Regression on lanes 5 and 7, the pages that read the public routes and two that boot the app: all green, 104 checks (public-doc-page 12, clip-links 20, hook-portal-access 11, stable-images 6, stale-chunk-recovery 27, addressability-live 28); `public-pages-busy` 10/10 on both lanes.

### `found-30-sep/attachments-unordered` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found closing `found-30-sep/task-attachments-flaky`)

**A task's attachments come back in whatever order Postgres finds them**

*Evidence, 30 September, lane 4:*
- `listAttachments` and `getTask`'s attachments select from `task_attachments` with no ORDER BY, and the table has no index on `task_id`. Both are a sequential scan in heap order.
- Each pooled connection inserts into its own target page. So once autovacuum has freed space, three files linked in a row land on three pages.
- 9 seedings of three links in 15 came back out of order, for example file-1, file-2, file-0 from heap (0,3), (5,35), (8,5).
- The panel shows them in that order, so a new file can land first or in the middle.

*To close:* find out which order ClickUp lists a task's attachments in and give both reads that order. Check it with files written out of heap order.

*Closed, 30 September* (by an agent on lane 4; merged and measured again here). ClickUp's help centre does not say what order the Attachments section lists files in. Its feedback board says there is no sort: "ClickUp provides no option to sort attachments within tasks or spaces" ("Add Sorting Options for Attachments (by Date and File Type)"), and "a massive list of attachments without the ability to sort (beyond the date modified)". So by date. The direction is not said, and this follows the ledger, which expected a new file to land last: the order they were attached, oldest first. A file attached later then moves no card already drawn.
- `listAttachments` and `getTask`'s attachments sort by `created_at, id`, one constant for both. The id breaks a tie between rows written in one transaction.
- 0170 indexes `task_attachments` on `task_id`, in the migration and the schema: every read of a task's files, and the cascade when a task is deleted, read the whole table. On the task alone, not with the date, because an index in date order would hand rows back sorted to a read that forgot its ORDER BY. The schema pushed onto the pristine dump differs from the shared reference by that index alone, and lane 4 with 0170 applied read as no drift against it.

Checks: `task-attachments` attaches file-1, file-2 and file-0 in that order, then rewrites their rows into the heap as file-2, file-0, file-1 and reads their `ctid` back. "the list hands the files back in the order they were attached, oldest first — not in the order the heap holds them", "and the task itself carries its files in the same order" and "the panel draws the files in the order they were attached".
- Before, all three failed in three runs of three: [file-2, file-0, file-1], the heap's order. After, all pass.
- `tasks-attachments-read.test.ts` is new, 5 tests: 0/5 against the old service, 5/5 after.
- `ato-1` (the list unsorted) reddens the list's and the panel's order (21/23), on a lane that has the index; `ato-2` (the task's rows unsorted) the task's (22/23); `ato-3` (newest first) all three (20/23). `ato-4` and `ato-5` redden their unit tests. Measured again by the break runner at 8c1b727 (lane 1): 21, 22 and 20 of 23. And at `de24716` (lane 1, 26 checks): 24, 25 and 21 of 26, each failing what it names.
- After the merge every lane database needs 0170 before `fleet-restart.sh` will start its API.

### `found-30-sep/killed-suites-leave-members-behind` — **closed** (test tooling, small; found closing `ledger-rows/row-1874`)

**A suite killed mid-run leaves the people it joined to the shared workspace**

*Evidence, 30 September:* `template-center` joins two people to the shared workspace for a run. A run killed with SIGKILL leaves them as members, as it already left its templates, since the `finally` cannot run. The break runner kills runs that overrun, so this happens.

*To close:* tag the people a suite makes (as its templates are tagged) and sweep tagged leftovers at the start of the next run, and check that a killed run's people are gone after the next one.


*Closed, 30 September.* Measured first on lane 6 at `f532edc`: `template-center` SIGKILLed three seconds after its setup left its two people members of Main, with their organizations and workspaces, and its ten templates. The next clean run left them all there.
- The tag is the journal `made.mjs` writes, not a name: `<suite>.<pid>.<started>.jsonl`, appended before each call that makes something returns. A name pattern cannot tell a killed run's rows from the same suite running now from another worktree; a process that is gone is not running.
- The first registration of any later run on the same database sweeps every journal whose process is gone (and whose number, if reused, no longer runs that suite) before it makes anything, and says what it removed.
- After, four times (the last on `bac7eae` with the final library): killed the same way, the run's journal named its 2 accounts and 10 templates. The next run removed them with their organizations and workspaces, then its own. From before the kill to after it, no account, organization, workspace, member of Main or template was added. `check-made-sweep.mjs` does the same with a probe process on every CI run.
- Merged here onto `2d38c0e` (one clash: `request-access` had moved onto `signUpApi` in the batch before, which now registers each person, so that side was kept). The gate names none over the 262 suites, and 19 of 19 mutations bite; it and its cases run in preflight too. Run again on lanes 2, 4, 5 and 7: the 25 suites this changed and `sign-in-and-password`, all green, 456 checks, and the four named suites it changed through `signUpApi` alone (`project-template-key`, `like-literal`, `role-permissions-web`, `space-default-permission`) 5, 5, 5 and 36, all green. `check-made-sweep.mjs` against lane 6: 24 cases hold, and 21 of 21 mutations bite (a first run cut off by a 15-minute limit of mine left one mutant file beside its subject, removed).

### `found-30-sep/suite-cleanup-leaves-stored-objects` — **closed** (test tooling, small; found closing `found-30-sep/suite-runs-leave-accounts-behind`) · reproduced 5 October

**What a suite uploads stays in the lane's store after the sweep deletes its rows**

*Evidence, 30 September:* after `stable-images` ran on lane 6 with the new cleanup, the store stub (bucket `rundesk-v6`, listed with `ListObjectsV2`) held `avatars/8cd8d0e3-…png` and `workspace-logos/d3cdb4de-…png`, whose user and workspace no longer exist. The sweeper deletes rows by SQL. `WorkspacesService.deleteForGood` purges a workspace's keys and prefixes; nothing purges an avatar. The stub keeps objects in memory for its lifetime, and `lane_store_up` keeps a running one.

*To close:* have the sweeper remove the objects a swept workspace or account names (the prefixes `storedKeysOf` lists, and `avatars/<userId>-`) through the stub's S3 API, and check by listing that a run that uploads leaves no object.

*Triage, 5 October:* reproduced on a lane. A suite's uploads stay in the lane's object store after the sweep deletes their rows: stable-images on lane 1 left an avatar and a workspace logo whose user and workspace no longer exist. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*Closed, 6 October* (lane 2). The sweep removes what the store held for the workspaces and accounts it removes (`made-sweep.mjs`). It reads them before their rows go, as `WorkspacesService.storedKeysOf` reads a workspace deleted for good: for each workspace, registered or in an organization the sweep removes, the keys its rows name (task files and covers, chat files and emoji, call recordings) and the prefixes it owns (`workspaces/<id>/`, `calls/<id>/`, `chat/<id>/`, `workspace-logos/<id>-`); for each account, `avatars/<id>-`. It deletes them once the rows are gone, through the store's S3 API, and lists them again: an object still there is left behind, as a row is. Only a stub's objects are removed. The store is the lane's (port 91<k>, bucket `rundesk-v<k>`, for the database `rundesk_v<k>`) or the one `E2E_STORE_PORT` and `E2E_STORE_BUCKET` name (CI's Postgres job now names its bucket too), and it must answer as the stub does; any other store is said and left.

Measured on lane 2 with `stable-images`, the store listed before and after the run. Before, on the build these fixes went onto, the run left `avatars/2af802a4-…png` and `workspace-logos/840f809e-…png`, whose account and workspace SQL no longer found (32 objects before the run, 34 after). After, the run's sweep said "removed what this run made: 1 account, 1 organization with 1 workspace, 2 stored objects", and the store held 34 objects before the run and 34 after; 6 of 6 again in the regression sweep, on lane 7.

Checks:
- `check-made-sweep.mjs` 24 → 26 cases, on a store stub of its own: a run that ends leaves nothing the store held for its account and the workspace only it owns (the avatar, the logo, a task's file, a call's recording, an emoji); and it keeps the outsider's avatar and the shared workspace's logo and clip, and says how many objects it removed. Its `--mutate` list gains four mutations, each of which makes a case fail (run by hand): the store left as it was, the avatars left, the workspace's objects left, and every avatar taken.

- Lane 4: 1,964 accounts, 1,929 organizations, 1,543 archived workspaces, 345 archived spaces, 164 archived lists; then 14 organizations, 205 workspaces, 409 spaces, 624 lists.

### `found-30-sep/suite-leftovers-unmeasured` — **closed** (test tooling, medium; found closing `found-30-sep/suite-runs-leave-accounts-behind`) · reproduced 5 October

**What a run leaves was measured for 36 of 259 suites**

*Evidence, 30 September:* the six named suites, the 21 converted and nine more were run with every table counted before and after, and nine of them turned out to leave rows the first cleanup did not see (a form, invitations, lists, docs, tasks, time blocks, notifications, an account made through a page; all fixed). The library covers accounts from `signUpApi` or a registered route, and workspaces, spaces, lists and invitations made through `apiAs`. It does not see what is made through the page or by other routes (an account made so is at least named at the run's end): Main held archived spaces named `Folders e2e-fd-…`, `AI e2e-cma-…`, `treefind-*-…`, `Views swv-…`, `Attach e2e-aoc-…`, `Control capg-…`, and live `Space-list check …`, `Space e2e-hdrstatus-…`, `Space e2e-fieldcreate-…`; 26 suites insert rows by SQL.

*To close:* run every suite once on a lane with every table counted before and after (the scratch `run.sh`/`content.sh` do it), register what each leaves (`madeRow`), and add a check that a run adds no row outside the admin's sessions, rate-limit counters and Main's audit trail.

*Triage, 5 October:* reproduced on a lane. Suites still leave rows the cleanup library never sees (task-provenance leaves a form and three tasks in Main on every run), and nothing counts every table to catch it. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*Closed, 7 October* (lanes 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7). Measured first, in the ninth batch's sweep, the lanes brought to pristine's hierarchy: the 268 suites left 559 rows in 43 tables, from 53 suites (`person-panel` 138, `task-depth` 73, `task-merge` 48, `chat-message-actions` 28 first). Most were tasks: a suite made them through `apiAs`, which registered workspaces, spaces, lists and invitations alone, and deleted them through the product, which only bins them.

What now registers, and removes, what a run makes:
- `apiAs` registers what more routes make (`MADE_BY_POST`, `lib/fixture.mjs`): tasks, projects, comments, checklists, channels and direct messages, messages, docs and imported docs, labels, support tickets, meetings, calls, forms, bookmarks, announcements, AI chats, canvases, custom fields, reminders, list email addresses, list views and filter presets. A workspace comes with its organization: the admin is in none, so a workspace the admin makes brings one of its own, which nothing registered. A call that ends names the meeting it filed. What `ensureSweepFixture` and `ensureShared` make is registered too, and goes when the run ends: they kept it from run to run for a suite beside, and no suite runs beside another on a database now.
- Every browser a suite launches through `resolveChromium` registers what its pages make, from the same routes (`watchMade`); a suite that launches one itself watches it so. The AI dock's threads, the space wizard's space, the meeting form's meeting and the list's add row's task were made so, and left.
- The sweep (`made-sweep.mjs`) removes what a registered row filed elsewhere: a call's meeting, a form's submitted tasks, the tags a task made by name, the project the server made for a list made under a space alone, the mail in and out of a task or a list, the mail refused that names neither but is still the run's (sent to a list's address once it was cut, or naming a task in its address's plus tag, or from one of the run's own accounts), the notifications about any of it (by `target.entityId` or along `target.url`), what the AI index held of it, what was opened of it from a search, and the files and cover of a task removed from a workspace that stays. It keeps a registered row older than the run, as it kept an older account: a route that answers with a row it already had (a direct message found again) registers that row, and it stays; so does an older organization, tag or project.
- The end of every suite's run is read: a suite is armed as it starts (`made.mjs`), whether it registers anything or not, and when its journal is swept, every row made since it began fails it, named by table (`leftSince`). A row's time of making is its `created_at`, or, in a table without one, the time set as it is written (`received_at`, `joined_at`…). Not counted: sessions, rate-limit counters, AI calls (the AI hourly limit's own counter, which reads the last hour), the audit trails, what was opened from a search, a notification with no actor of a kind only the API's schedules write (a reminder, the overdue notice, the briefing, the workload alert), and the built-in templates an API writes as it starts. A journal swept by hand is not read so.
- `lane-leftovers.mjs` also removes what runs left inside pristine's own containers: every other table's rows pristine lacks, but those using the product makes and the API's own templates.

Suites changed for what they did themselves:
- `calendar-accounts` no longer deletes its colleague by SQL: that took the owner's membership with the account, and the organization sign-up made stayed with its workspace every run.
- `ai-model-picker` registers the preference row it made when there was none (there is no DELETE route, and putting the default back kept a row).
- `flag-resolution` registers the platform's Forms switch when its run made it (the `PUT` answers with nothing), and leaves the one it found, switched back on.
- `panel-collapse` registers the test notification it sends to the admin's inbox in Main: the route answers with no id, and the notification has no actor.
- `list-address-readers` registers the mail it sends by message id: mail to a task's address cut from its task names no task, no list and no list's address.
- `create-ai-results` makes its workspace through the client; `settings-depth` and `task-depth` watch the browsers they launch.

Measured:
- Step by step on the same lanes: of the 53 suites that left rows, 32 left nothing once `apiAs` registered more; 14 of the other 21 once the pages were watched, what rows file elsewhere was taken, and the lanes were cleared of what earlier runs left; the last 8 after their own fixes.
- Then all 270 suites, twice, the lanes brought to pristine before each. The first regression failed `flag-resolution` (the platform switch's row, which its `PUT` makes and does not name), `private-object-urls` (its own API wrote the built-in templates the cleanup had taken) and `task-menu` (a list's email address, which its `DELETE` only turns off); each was fixed, and left nothing run again. The second, with each table's own time of making read, failed `email-reply-routing`, `list-address-readers` and `mail-comments-by-level` on refused mail, every check of theirs passing: 266 of 270 suites green at once, 4,224 of 4,225 checks (`task-menu`'s "the task menu opens", green run again). With the mail rules above, each of the three left nothing run again.
- The lanes compared with pristine after it held, inside pristine's own containers, the API's own overdue notice on each, the AI index of pristine's own tasks on lane 4 (use, which no run removes), and a test notification `panel-collapse` left in the admin's inbox on lane 2, which the check passed for having no actor: it is registered now, and a notification with no actor counts unless it is of a kind only the schedules write. `panel-collapse` (57 of 57) and `inbox-scope` (23 of 23), run again, left nothing.
- On lane 7, `calendar-accounts` failed once the lanes held pristine's rows, its planner's "Meet with" box never drawn: lane 7's admin held a rail without it, from an earlier run (`found-7-oct/shared-rows-keep-what-runs-changed`). Put back, 37 of 37.

Checks:
- `check-made-sweep.mjs` 26 → 39 cases. New: the notifications about a registered row go with it (by id, along the address), a notification about something else stays; a registered row and a registered organization older than the run stay; what a registered row filed elsewhere goes with it, and an older tag or project stays, not even taken up as the run's; the mail in and out of a task and a list that go goes with them, and so does mail refused at the list's cut address or naming the task in its own; the mail in from an account the run made, filed nowhere, and out to it goes with the account, and an older account's stays; what was opened of a task from a search goes with it; a run that leaves a row it never registered fails and names the table, and so does one that leaves a row of a table with no `created_at`, or a notification with no actor of a kind no schedule writes; one that leaves only a sign-in, an AI call and a scheduled notification passes; a suite that registers nothing is read when it ends. Mutations 25 → 50 (the registry 8 → 10, the sweep 17 → 40), each caught: a full run caught 44 of the first 45 and found the line of the 45th moved; re-aimed, it, the five added after and the two re-aimed with them were each caught on their own.

### `found-30-sep/legacy-break-patches-directory` — **closed** (test tooling, small; found closing `ledger-rows/row-1874`)

**`test/e2e/break-patches/` holds old copies of patches that no gate reads, some of which no longer apply**

### `found-30-sep/templates-null-array-field-values` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found closing `ledger-rows/row-1060`)

**A task template stores a list- or people-valued custom field as `null` on every write**

*Evidence, 30 September, measured on lane 3 by the agent that built row-1060:* `TaskTemplatesService.normalisePayload` keeps a `customFieldValues[].value` only if it is a string, number or boolean, and turns anything else into `null`. But the schema widened `value` to `string[]` (`packages/db/src/schema/task-templates.ts:73-77`) precisely so that a template would not silently drop a task's people field. It runs on create, on save-from-task and on every PATCH that carries a payload. A template created with `[{fieldName:'People', value:['u1','u2']},{fieldName:'Budget', value:5}]` is stored as `People: null, Budget: 5`. So Update existing template keeps scalar custom-field values and cannot keep an array one, and its panel promises only checklists and subtasks.

*To close:* keep an array of strings in `normalisePayload`, with a unit test each way and a patch that reddens it. Then the Update panel may promise custom fields too.

*Closed, 30 September* (built by an agent on lane 6; merged and measured again here). ClickUp's help centre ("Use task templates", read through search excerpts; the site is blocked here): a task template saved with Import everything "will include all task properties, fields, and settings", and of its custom fields only one kind is named as left out: "Custom Fields: Include Custom Fields (Note: Formula Fields are not included)".

Measured first, on lane 6 at `f499cf6`:
- A template made with a People list (two members) and a Labels list (two options) read back both as null.
- So did a task with both fields set, saved as a template.
- The task made from that template got both fields as null.
- The Update panel read "its checklists and subtasks are kept".

- `normalisePayload` keeps a list of texts (`templateFieldValue`). An object, or a list holding anything else, is still null. Create, save from a task and every PATCH with a payload go through it.
- A list kept in a template reaches the task made from it. On the way it is checked as the field's own route checks it, because this write goes round that route:
  - people who are members of the workspace now, options the target field defines, and tasks in the workspace, each once;
  - a list with nothing left is not written;
  - a list never goes into a one-value field (`fitTemplateValue`);
  - only id-shaped ids are asked of Postgres.
- A template never takes or writes a Voting or Files value. A vote is its voter's own (the route toggles only the caller's), and a Files value names the source task's attachments.
- The Update panel says "its checklists, subtasks and custom-field values are kept". Four locales.

Checks:
- `create-modal-templates` had 15 checks and has 20. The new ones:
  - a template made through the API keeps both lists;
  - Update keeps them as lists;
  - the panel says so before it is pressed;
  - a task saved as a template keeps them;
  - a task made from it carries both, read by SQL.
- One sentence changed from "custom-field value" to "custom-field values", since the template it compares now holds three.
- Before, 15/20 on lane 6 (the five new checks red). After, 20/20, and again on `cb21d14` and `6db885c`.
- `create-modal-templates-16..20` are new, each reddening the check it claims on lane 6. The break runner measured them at 8c1b727 (lane 1): 18, 19, 16, 18 and 19 of 20 against 20/20. `create-modal-templates-3` claims the renamed sentence and reddens it.
- `ttv-1..5` are unit claims, each reddening its test in `task-templates.service.test.ts` (11 tests new). The API's unit tests: 1785/1785.
- Regression on lane 6: `template-center` 81, `project-template-key` 5, `space-wizard` 23, `space-create-menu` 32, `space-default-permission` 36, `like-literal` 5, `sidebar-sections` 25, `role-permissions-web` 5, all green.

Found while building it: `found-30-sep/template-values-written-unchecked`, `found-30-sep/duplicate-copies-votes-and-files`, `found-30-sep/save-as-template-words-promise-every-field` and `found-30-sep/suite-runs-leave-accounts-behind`.
- Merged here and run again: on lane 5 `create-modal-templates` 20/20, and on lane 7 `template-center` 81/81, `project-template-key` 5/5, space-wizard 23, like-literal 5, role-permissions-web 5 and space-default-permission 36, all green.

### `found-30-sep/template-submit-ignores-the-form` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found closing `ledger-rows/row-1060`)

**With a template chosen, Create task ignores everything else typed in the form, and nothing says so**

*Evidence, 30 September:* the submit sends `{ listId, titleOverride }` to instantiate. Priority, description, dates, estimate, tags, task type and assignees typed into the same form are not applied, although the route already accepts `assigneeIds`. `docs/clickup-research.md` §9 records this as a defect and proposes letting the fields the person touched win over the template. It was kept as it is by row-1060's brief.

*To close:* research how ClickUp applies a template to a form that already holds values, then apply what was typed (or say, before Create, which fields the template will replace), and check it with a suite.


*Closed, 30 September* (built by an agent on lane 2). ClickUp's help centre, read through search excerpts (the site and its feedback board are blocked here):
- the task creation modal can "load a task template" ("Create a task");
- templates "are merged when applied to an existing task" ("Intro to templates");
- in a merge, the target "will keep its tags, priorities, dates, recurrence, time tracked, Custom Fields, and estimated time", the other's "description is added to the bottom" of the target's, and its "assignees are added" ("Merge tasks");
- the feedback board's "Choose where in description to append a task template": "When you append a template that adds to the description, it gets added to the end of the description".

So the form is the task, and the template is merged into it.

Measured first on lane 2 at `f335b89`, three runs. A template with a checklist, a subtask and priority Low. In the modal: priority High, an assignee, a tag, a due date and a description; Create. The page sent instantiate `{ listId, titleOverride }`. The task came out Low, with the template's description alone, no due date, nobody assigned and the template's tag alone: all five dropped.

- What the person set wins over the template's one values: priority, task type, start and due dates, estimate.
- A typed description comes first, and the template's follows it after a blank line.
- Tags and assignees are the template's and the form's, each once.
- What was left alone is the template's, and its checklists, subtasks and custom-field values come as before (`templateWithForm`).
- The form sends only what was set (`setInForm`, which the plain create sends too). Every field starts empty but the priority, which starts on Normal, so whether it was chosen is kept apart.
- The route's body is a DTO (`InstantiateTemplateDto`), with `POST /tasks`'s rules field for field, and no estimate below nothing. The type, the people and the labels are asked by `createTask`, as for `POST /tasks`. The body was an untyped shape, and nothing in it was checked.
- Before Create, beside the chosen template, the modal says:
  - that the template brings its checklists, subtasks and custom-field values;
  - that what is set here wins over the template, naming what was set ("Priority · Due");
  - that a typed description comes first;
  - that tags and assignees are added to the template's.

  It is said, not loaded into the form. The template's tags and description are added to what the form holds, so in its boxes they would read as the person's own. Four locales.
- Create instantly is unchanged: the list and the title only.

Checks:
- `create-modal-templates` had 26 checks and has 33.
  - Before: 26/32 three times at `f335b89` (the six merge checks red), and 26/33 three times at `2f7670e` (the seven new checks red).
  - After: 33/33 three times in a row at each, and again at `de24716`.
  - One check reads the request as well as the task. A field left alone is the template's on the old build too, so what is checked is that only what was set is sent, and the template's estimate and start date stand for the rest.
- `create-modal-templates-21..27` are new. Each reddens only the check it claims on lane 2 (32/33). The break runner measured them at `cdc2105` (lane 2): each fails exactly the check it names, 32/33 against 33/33.
- `tsf-1..4` are unit claims. Each reddens only its test in `task-templates.service.test.ts` (4 tests new; before, 29/33 with the four red).
- `create-modal-templates-5`, `td-create-1`, `time-estimate-4` and `v1f-3` were anchored on the create body, which moved into `setInForm`. They are re-anchored, and each still reddens its claim on lane 2. The break runner measured `create-modal-templates-5` at `cdc2105` (lane 2): 26/33 against 33/33, failing the check it names and the six that make a task from a template.
- Regression on lane 2 (by the agent): the 23 suites that open the create modal or its templates, all green, 609 checks. Among them: template-center 81, project-template-key 5, task-depth 92, video1-fast-items 92, custom-field-progress 60, space-create-menu 32, custom-field-types 32, folder-dialog 29, create-menu-ai 24, space-wizard 23 and time-estimate 13.
- Merged here and run again on lanes 2 and 5: `create-modal-templates` 33/33, `template-center` 81, `project-template-key` 5, `custom-field-progress` 60, `task-depth` 92, `space-create-menu` 32, `folder-dialog` 29, `time-estimate` 13 and `create-menu-ai` 24, all green, 369 checks. The API and the web typecheck.

### `found-30-sep/refused-create-leaves-tags` — **closed** (small; found closing `found-30-sep/template-submit-ignores-the-form`)

**A refused create leaves the tags it made behind**

*Evidence, 30 September, measured on lane 2 by the agent:* making a task from a template makes the template's missing labels (`resolveLabelIds`) before `createTask` asks about the list, the type, the people and the labels. A create refused for its task type (400) made no task, and left the template's label in the workspace.

Read, not measured: the create modal makes each typed tag (`POST /workspaces/:ws/labels`) before the task. So a refused create, plain or from a template, leaves those tags too. Before this fix, every tag typed beside a template was left so, attached to nothing.

*To close:* make the labels only once the task is made, or in the same transaction, and check that a refused create adds no label.


*Closed, 30 September* (built by an agent on lane 5). ClickUp makes a tag from the task creation window ("Search or
create new", type the name, Enter), as part of the task being made; OWASP's Business Logic Security Cheat Sheet: a
half-finished step leaves "exploitable inconsistencies", and the fix is "a database transaction". Measured first on
lane 5 at `6f8e02c`, a probe three times: a task from a template holding a tag the workspace lacked, refused for its
task type (400), made no task and left the tag. Read: the create modal made each typed tag before the task.

- `createTask` takes tags by name (`labelsByName`): each is found in the task's workspace whatever its case, after
  every question has been answered, and the rest are made in the same transaction as the task, its people and its
  tag rows. The template's route hands its tags over by name and makes none itself; its match was exact-case, so a
  template's "urgent" beside the workspace's "Urgent" made a second tag. A duplicate carries the original's tags by
  id. A guest's name for a tag that does not exist is left off, as the tags route refuses a guest a new tag.
- The create modal sends the typed tags by name, on `POST /tasks` and on the template's route, and no longer makes
  them first; a typed tag the task came back without is said with the other extras.

Checks:
- `create-modal-templates` had 33 checks and has 37. Before: 32/37 three times at `6f8e02c` (the four new checks
  red, and "Create sends the template’s route what was set …", which now expects `labelsByName`). After: 37/37
  three times in a row there, and again at `bac7eae`.
- `create-modal-templates-28..31` are new, each reddening only the check it claims on lane 5.
- `twr-5`, `twr-6`, `twr-8`, `twr-12` and `twr-13` are unit claims, each reddening its test.
- `create-modal-templates-12`, `-23` and `tsf-3` were anchored on lines this moved; re-anchored, each reddens its
  claim.
- Merged here onto `f44b647` with the other three builders' batches (one clash: `create-modal-templates` took checks from two of them, 33 → 45, and a `T5_ID` both had declared; three of the fields batch's unit tests scripted one read fewer than the task-writes batch now makes, and do now) and run again on lanes 2, 4, 5 and 7, 26 suites, all green, 552 checks: among them `create-modal-templates` 45, `task-values` 21, `task-creation-access` 6, `time-estimate` 13, `task-depth` 92.

### `found-30-sep/spreadsheet-import-skips-task-rules` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found closing `found-30-sep/a-task-starts-after-it-is-due`) · reproduced 5 October

**The spreadsheet import makes a second tag that differs only in case**

*Evidence, 30 September, measured on lane 5 at `bac7eae` with this work's build (`probe-import.mjs`):* a sheet row
"Start Date 2026-10-10, Due Date 2026-10-03, Tags urgent-X", imported into a workspace that holds the tag "Urgent-X",
answered 201. The task was stored starting on the 10th and due on the 3rd, and the workspace then held two tags,
"Urgent-X" and "urgent-X". The import writes its rows straight into `tasks` (`spreadsheet-import.service.ts`, the
insert and the "merge" update), not through `TasksService.createTask`, so it asks none of `task-values.ts`; and its
`ensureLabel` finds a tag by its exact name, where `POST /workspaces/:ws/labels` and a create's `labelsByName` find
one whatever its case.

*5 October:* since the owner's decision of 1 October every route takes a start after the due date again
(`found-30-sep/a-task-starts-after-it-is-due`, reverted), so the import's dates now match the product; only the tag
half stands.

*To close:* find a tag by name whatever its case (`ensureLabel`), as the tags route and `labelsByName` do, and check
it with the `imports` suite, by SQL.

*Triage, 5 October, after the revert:* partly reproduced on a lane. The spreadsheet import, and the ClickUp CSV import, still make a second tag that differs only in case ('urgent-X' beside 'Urgent-X') where the tags route finds the existing one. Its start-after-due write is no longer a defect, since every route now takes one. The ClickUp CSV import makes the same second tag (its `ensureLabel` matches exact case too). The skeptic reproduced the tag half by the merge path, and found two more defects in the same code, now counted: `found-5-oct/import-writes-into-another-workspace` and `found-5-oct/import-merge-resets-fields-the-file-lacks`. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*Closed, 5 October (the tag half; the date half is no defect since the owner's decision of 1 October).* ClickUp holds no two tags that differ only in case: "Tags of tasks are currently forced to be lowercase, no matter what you write or rename it to" (feedback board, "Allow Tags to use capital letters", through a search excerpt). Rundesk's tags route and a task's `labelsByName` already find a tag whatever its case, and both importers' `ensureLabel` now do too: `lower(name) = lower(given)`, for the lookup and for the re-read after a conflicting insert.

Measured on lane 4 (`probe-tags-merge.mjs`): before, with the workspace's "Urgent-X" (POST labels "urgent-x" answered with it), a sheet row tagged "urgent-X" made a second tag and a ClickUp row tagged "URGENT-x" a third, each tagging its task with its own; after, both rows are tagged "Urgent-X", no tag is made (labelsCreated 0) and the workspace holds one.

Checks:
- `imports` +2, one per importer, by SQL: red on HEAD's product code, green after (33/33 three times).
- One test each in `spreadsheet-import.service.test.ts` and `clickup-import.service.test.ts`, reading the SQL the lookup sends.
- `imports-25` and `-26` redden exactly their checks; `iss-7` and `ics-3` redden their tests.

*Review fix, 6 October* (lane 4):
- The ClickUp import made a tag cut to 60 characters but looked it up by the whole name. A 70-character tag imported again in another case made a twin differing only in case; imported again in the same case, it hit the twin's conflict and the tag was dropped (labelsCreated 1|1|0, the third task untagged). It now looks a tag up by the name in the file and by the name it is stored under, for the lookup and the re-read after a conflict. After: 1|0|0, one tag, all three tasks tagged.
- A tag a running spreadsheet import makes is committed with its row, so the tags route finds it while the import goes on (when the run was briefly one transaction, it made "racetag-…" beside "RaceTag-…").
Checks: `imports` +2 (a 70-character ClickUp tag; a tag asked for during a running import). Patches `imports-35`, `imports-43` (42/43 each); `imports-26` and `ics-3` re-aimed; unit claim `ics-4`.

### `found-30-sep/menus-drop-a-press-while-closing` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found closing `ledger-rows/row-1060`)

**A dropdown pressed while the last one is still closing opens and shuts again at once**

*Evidence, 30 September, measured on lane 3 by the agent:* a closed `DropdownMenu` stays mounted through its exit animation. A press on the trigger in that window opens the new menu, and 3 ms later the leaving layer takes it as a press outside and closes it. In a scratch loop under load: 2 of 6 rounds, with the old menu still mounted 355 ms after closing; 0 of 10 once the loop waited for it to go. Measured on the create modal's Templates menu only. It comes from the shared `@rundesk/ui` dropdown's exit animation, so other menus on it presumably share it. `create-modal-templates` waits for the old menu to leave before pressing.

*To close:* measure it on two other menus, then make a closing layer ignore presses on a trigger (or drop the exit animation's outside-press handling), and check that a press during the exit opens the menu and it stays open.

*Closed, 30 September* (built by an agent on lane 6, merged and measured again here). ClickUp's help centre ("Task settings menu", "List, Folder, and Space settings", read through search results):
- "In the upper-right corner, click the ellipsis ... icon to open the task settings menu";
- a List's settings open from "the ellipsis (...) icon to the right of a List".

A press on a menu's button opens its menu. Nothing there depends on how recently the menu closed.

Measured first, on lane 6, on four menus of the shared dropdown: the task's ⋯, the sidebar's ⋯ on a list, the sidebar's + on a space and the top bar's user menu. A press during the exit re-opened the menu 4–16 ms after the press. In the same millisecond the leaving layer took the press as a press outside (`pointerDownOutside`), and the menu was shut 3–8 ms later. Focus-outside played no part: a modal Radix menu refuses it. It was every menu drawn by `DropdownMenuContent`, not the Templates menu alone.

- `DropdownMenuContent` now draws `ReopenableContent`, which refuses the outside press of a layer that was already closing when the press began. The button's own toggle decides.
- "Was closing" is read in the capture phase, before the button's handler re-opens the menu.
- The caller's `onPointerDownOutside` runs first. An open menu is dismissed by a press outside it as before, and the exit animation is unchanged.
- One line of `DropdownMenuContent` changed, so `swc-7`'s anchor still holds.

### `found-30-sep/menu-items-take-a-press-while-closing` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found closing `found-30-sep/menus-drop-a-press-while-closing`)
