### `found-24-sep/one-suite-two-lanes-share-a-results-file` — **closed** (found planning the `wra-8..40` runs)

**Two break sets of the same suite on two lanes write, and truncate, one results file; neither the runner nor the dispatcher stops it**

*Evidence, read not run:* `wt-break.sh` locks the LANE (`/tmp/claude-0/wt<lane>.lock`), but its results go to `/tmp/claude-0/break-<suite>.txt`, one file per SUITE. It truncates that file once it holds the lane lock (`: > "$OUT"`), and archives it on exit. `run-plan.sh` removes that same file before launching each set, and hands the next plan line to any free lane without asking whether that suite is already running elsewhere. Its header describes this very accident (`ui-sweep` ran on lanes 2 and 3 into one file) and says a single dispatcher cannot race. That holds for one plan line; two lines for one suite still run at once. A set split across lanes by hand has the same problem, and the second set's truncation erases the first set's results mid-run. The generated plans put one line per suite, which is why it has not bitten. The `wra-8..40` runs were kept to one set on one lane for this reason.

*Closed:* `break_locks_take <lane> <suite>` (lane-env.sh) takes the lane lock, then a suite lock (`break-<suite>.lock`). It refuses with exit 3 and says which one was held; on a busy suite it gives the lane back. `wt-break.sh` takes the pair and drops both on exit. `run-plan.sh` no longer takes the next line: a free lane gets the first untaken line whose suite is neither running on another of its lanes (whose child may not have taken the lock yet) nor locked by another run. So a busy suite is passed over, not handed out and refused, which would burn the entry. The waiting message and the give-up count follow.

Held to that twice. `check-locks.sh` has three new cases for the pair (both free; busy lane, suite untouched; busy suite, lane given back and holder untouched) and two mutations: the lane lock alone, and the lane kept on refusal. That makes 6 of 6 mutations caught. The new `check-run-plan.sh` dispatches a five-line plan to a stand-in runner that takes the real locks and traces its hold: three sets of one suite, two others, and one suite held by another run for two seconds. It requires that no two sets of a suite overlap, that the others ran beside them, that the held suite waited, that nothing was refused and that the plan drained 5 of 5. Its three mutations are each caught for their own reason (a second set of the running suite refused; the held suite handed out and refused; plan order losing three sets). Both run in preflight and CI.

### `found-24-sep/model-patches-measured-without-a-model` — **closed** (test tooling; found judging the second drifted plan)

**Two patches that only a model can redden ran on lanes with none and read as reddening nothing, and the suite's no-model branch printed the model's sentence**

*Evidence (the second drifted plan's logs, read by `check-break-reddened`):* `wra-11` and `wra-12` each say in their header "Reddens only where a model answers". The plan ran on lanes 3 and 4, started without `RUNDESK_LANE_MODEL`, so the API had no model and `workspace-read-access` built no prompt. Both came back 0 failed and were listed with the patches that prove nothing. Nothing in the runner read the header; whether a lane had a model was up to whoever started the run. And the suite's branch for a lane with no model printed "the prompt a model is sent names, for a member, no space they are refused — the admin’s names it" after checking only that the chat answered 503. The log said a prompt rule had been measured when no prompt existed.

*Closed:* the break runner asks every patch in a set (`patches_needing_model`, lane-env.sh). When one needs a model, the lane gets one for the whole set, baseline included (`lane_model_add`), and the log says so on a `-- model:` line that no log reader takes for a patch header. The runner's stamp of what a lane serves now carries the model (`lane_serving_id`). A lane serving the right revision without one is re-synced for a set that needs one, and back again for a set that does not. So `create-menu-ai`, which is about the refusal, never inherits a model. The no-model branch has its own sentence, which says the prompt rule is measured only where a model answers. The new `check-model-lanes.sh` holds the header, the lane list (added to, not replaced; `all` left be), the stamp and the runner's wiring, and catches 5 of 5 mutations; before the change it failed on the runner. In preflight and CI. `wra-11` and `wra-12` were re-run with it on lane 2. The log says `-- model: on — needed by wra-11… wra-12…`, the baseline was 30/30 with a model, and each patch reddened the prompt check.

### `found-23-sep/lane-store-refused-the-apis-own-uploads` — **closed** (found giving the store a copy for `clip-create-task-persists-24h-url`)

**Under `--strict`, the lane store refused every PUT the API sends itself, as unsigned**

*Evidence:* `s3-stub.mjs` counted a PUT as signed only if its QUERY carried `X-Amz-Signature`, which is a presigned upload's shape. The SDK signs a request it sends directly in the `Authorization` header, so `putObject` (inbound email attachments) and any copy were answered 403 "the PUT carried no X-Amz-Signature" wherever the stub runs strict, which is how CI runs it. `check-s3-stub.mjs` never sent one, so nothing noticed. A mutation restoring the old rule reddens 5 cases of the new contract.

*Closed:* a signature in either place counts, and an unsigned PUT is still refused. The stub also serves CopyObject (the source's bytes, the requested type under `REPLACE`, `NoSuchKey` for a missing source, the source noted in the request log), which `check-s3-stub` drives through the real `R2Service`: 23/23 cases, 19/19 mutations.

### `found-24-sep/drifted-plan-three-patches-unaimed` — **closed**, re-runs pending (test tooling; found judging today's drifted break plan)

**The plan that re-measured today's drift (106 sets, 580 patches, lanes 3 and 4) left three patches that prove nothing, and one check that could not fail on this date**

*Evidence (the plan's logs, read by `check-break-reddened`):*
- `prail-3-finished-work-is-still-assigned` reddened nothing (0 failed). It removed the planner rail's own "open work" filter, and the member endpoint the rail reads has returned open work only since `ecd6bb0`. So the client filter restates the server's rule, and removing it changes nothing.
- `pv-2-the-arrows-always-move-a-week` reddened nothing. Its check, "next in Month view moves to a different month", pressed next once and compared labels. On 24 September a week's step also lands in October, so the check passed with the arrow moving a week. It could only fail in the first three weeks of a month.
- `lwb-1-noorder` was unproven: a check failed, not the one it claimed. Without an ORDER BY the database answers in whatever order it holds the rows, so which order-dependent check falls is the database's choice. On 23 September it was the rename check, today the token's binding.
- The plan's other 103 sets ran; `task-cover`'s and `calendar-accounts`' baselines were refused, the second a real defect (`found-24-sep/zoom-row-not-connected-while-loading`, closed) and the first a run under load (42/42 on lanes 1 and 2 since, 20 of 20 patches reddened).

*Closed:* `prail-3` takes the rule out where it lives, the member endpoint's closed filter. `planner-views` presses next twice and needs three different months: two week-long steps cannot cross two month boundaries, and two month-long steps always do. `lwb-1` claims both order-dependent checks. The re-runs are on lane 2, with `calendar-accounts`' own set in the second drifted plan (76 sets, 657 patches, started on lanes 3 and 4 after today's fixes drifted them).

*Re-run on lane 2:* `pv-2` reddened, and `lwb-1` reddened its claim. `prail-3` reddened nothing again. With the server's rule gone, the page's own copy still left the closed task out. Each copy of the rule covered for the other, so neither could be tested. The page's copy is gone now (with `product-siblings/workload-csv-dates-shifted-east-of-utc`'s batch), and the server's is the only one. `prail-2`, which read the page's copy, is re-aimed at the list it now reads. `planner-rail` passes 10/10 without the page's copy, in the 24-suite sweep above. Re-run on lane 2: `prail-2` and `prail-3` each reddened. `prail-3` now proves the server's rule. `sidebar-reorder-2`, re-aimed at the tree drawing the server's order, reddened as well.

### `suite-hygiene/hand-rolled-chains` — **closed** (test tooling, large)

**103 literal check(false, …) calls in 15 suites, plus 5 other hand-rolled chains, instead of lib/chain.mjs**

### `suite-hygiene/apiAs-duplicated-62` — **closed**, medium

**62 suites hand-roll an API client in 5 variants beside lib/fixture.mjs apiClient**

*Evidence:* `^const apiAs = ` appears in 62 suites. Hashing the whole function bodies gives 5 variants: 54 copies (activity-rail…), 5 copies (addressability-live…) that always send `authorization: Bearer ${token}`, so an anonymous call sends 'Bearer null'; 1 in task-ai-bar that adds a `message` field; 1 GET-only in malformed-ids; and 1 multi-line in chat-message-actions. lib/fixture.mjs:28-46 apiClient differs again: it parses text and keeps `raw`. syncup-live has a third shape, api(token, method, path, body). The ledger extracted chain.mjs (docs/video2-reaudit.md:4076-4078) for two copies and claim-match.mjs (4071-4075) for two.

*To close:* Export apiAs(base)(token) from lib/fixture.mjs with the null-token rule and the message field, move suites onto it, and have the one copy expose `ok` and a `must(res, what)` helper, which would also remove most of finding unguarded-derefs.

*Closed, 30 September.* By then it was 172 suites, not 62, because the suites added since had copied the copy. With comments and spacing set aside, the 172 were 21 variants. Thirteen more suites had the same client under another name: ten `call`s, an `A`, an `asMember`, file-exports' `api`, and syncup-live's `api(token, method, path, body)`. They differed where a caller does not look:
- 87 sent `Bearer null` for a null token;
- 67 rejected when nothing answered, and 105 answered 0;
- some parsed the body as text and kept it, one kept the whole body as `data`, and four sent `{}` on a write with no body.

`lib/fixture.mjs` now exports the one client, `apiAs(base)(token)`:
- it answers `{ status, ok, data, error, message, text, type }` for every status;
- it sends no Authorization header for a null token;
- it carries `task-ai-bar`'s `message` as one string.

Beside it, `must(res, what)` hands back `data` on a 2xx and otherwise throws "could not make the workspace: answered 403 …". `apiClient` is the same client and still rejects when nothing answers. `ensureShared` uses `must`.

Each suite binds the client where its copy stood (`const apiAs = apiAsAt(API)`), so no call site moved. Where a suite's checks stood on its copy's behaviour, that behaviour is an option at the binding, with its reason:

The 239 suites held 1,544 `.catch(() => {})` (a grep finds 1,549; five are in comments). 158 were on an API client, in 133 suites: 136 on a client call, 11 on a closure or loop that calls one (six `cleanup.reverse()` runners, three `restore?.()`, one `cleanup?.()`, one `platformOn()`), and 11 on a raw `fetch` to the API. 111 of the 158 were one copied line, the teardown `DELETE` of the suite's own workspace. A restore of shared state is a counted check, one in each of ten suites (`panel-collapse`, `person-panel`, `settings-depth`, `video-regression`, `video1-acceptance`, `task-provenance`, `ai-value`, `flag-resolution`, `planner-default-list`, `comment-recording`), each suite's `EXPECTED_CHECKS` one higher. - `lib/fixture.mjs` `ensureShared` reads every write and closes its task with the list's own closed status, not `done`.
- Found doing it, and fixed: 67 suites closed their proxy before the teardown `DELETE`, which goes through that proxy, so those workspaces were never archived (ECONNREFUSED, swallowed); `stack.close()` now comes after it. Five teardowns in four suites answered 400, because their clients sent `content-type: application/json` on a bodyless `DELETE`; they send it only with a body now. `replies-inline-thread` sent `{ userId }` where the route reads `userIds[]`, so its peer was never added (2xx, `added: 0`); it sends the list and requires `added === 1`.
- Demonstrated: a teardown pointed at a wrong workspace printed `cleanup left behind: DELETE /workspaces/… answered 400` above `1 passed, 0 failed`.
- `scripts/check-suite-api-catches.mjs --mutate` (preflight, and CI's verify job) keeps it so. It reads each suite as code (comments, strings, regex literals and template text blanked), resolves the names the file binds to an API client (factories, aliases, fetch-calling helpers, `.as` properties, curried calls), and refuses an empty handler on a client call, on a closure or loop that calls one, or on a raw `fetch`, and a null handler whose result nothing reads. It found 158 at `d86220d` (136 direct, 11 wrapped, 11 fetch), line for line what the scanner found, and 0 now. 24 of 24 mutations bite, over 24 planted cases (18 it must catch, 6 it must pass: Playwright, SQL, teardown, a handler that does something, the shape inside a comment, string or regex, and `waitUntil`).
- It also caught the three suites added since that base (`audit-log-settings`, `routes-with-readers`, `assign-with-ai-picker`), which had the old teardown and closed their proxy first. `routes-with-readers` put the admin's digest setting back through the closed proxy too, so the restore never happened (lane 7's admin was left on a weekly digest); it now restores before closing and treats no answer as a failed restore, and lane 7's setting is back to the default.
- `docs/e2e-shared-state-audit.md` §3 and its table, and `docs/video2-resume.md` §3, carry the measured split instead of 292.
- The 133 suites on lane 6 at the agent's tree: each `N passed, 0 failed` at its `EXPECTED_CHECKS`. At this tree, with the text-read and stale-doc changes merged in, on lanes 1, 3, 5 and 7 at once: 137 of 138 (the changed suites and `a39-dm-tabs`, whose fixture changed). `doc-level-controls` read its editor before the doc's capabilities had answered under that load; it now waits for them (see `doc-editor-open-to-readers`), then 7/7.

**email.service send() still has no replyTo, cc or messageId, and task_comments still has no channel column**

*Evidence:* apps/api/src/modules/email/email.service.ts:584-611: send(opts: {to, subject, html, attachments}) calls transport.sendMail({from, to, subject, html, attachments}). I searched apps/api/src for an outbound composed-body route (`@Post(...email...)`, `this.email.send*` callers in task and comment modules): the only senders are notification templates (notifications.service.ts:1179, 1203, 1213).

Add migration 0161: task_comments.channel ('comment'|'email', default 'comment') plus email metadata (to, cc, subject, message_id). A comment notification's Message-ID is kept where `resolveReplyContext` finds it. Its Reply-To is the task's address when the list has an alias; none is minted. - Every mail about a task is sent with a thread: a Message-ID kept with the task, and the task's own address as its Reply-To where its list takes email (`sendEmail`, `notifications.service.ts`; `replyThread` as before). The mail that tells somebody they were mentioned, that a task is theirs, due, overdue or changed, that their comment was resolved, and any other mail whose target is a task, as the comment notification already was. Whether a mail is about a task is read from its target, not its type: a mention in chat is a `task_mentioned` about a message, and carries none.
- Each sender of such a mail takes the thread and hands it to the transport (`ReplyThread`, `email.service.ts`); the comment notification's own two fields are that type now.

Measured on lane 4 with the extended `email-reply-routing` suite: before, on the build of `a936b69`, somebody mentioned in a comment, who did not watch the task, and the watcher given the task were each kept nothing (no row in `outbound_email_messages` for them), so their replies had nothing to name and reached no task (4 of 6, the two new checks red, two runs alike). Checks:
- `email-reply-routing` 4 → 6: "the mail that tells somebody they were mentioned is sent with a Message-ID the server keeps and the task’s own Reply-To, and a reply naming it lands on the task as their comment"; "and the mail that tells somebody the task is theirs is answered on the task the same way".
- `notifications.service.test.ts` +1: each type of mail about a task is sent with the thread kept for it, the resolved comment and a type no case names among them, and a mention in chat with none. `email.service.test.ts` +1: each of the seven senders hands the transport the Message-ID and the Reply-To it is given.

### `harness/model-lane-routing-unbuilt` — **closed** (test tooling, medium)

**No suite can be routed to a lane with or without a model; the model stub is wired but no suite exercises it**

*Evidence:* lane-env.sh:126-132 says 'Wiring that choice into the dispatcher is the next piece of this work and is NOT done'. Confirmed open. run-plan.sh:47-68 hands a set to any lane that is free and unlocked, and it never sources lane-env.sh or calls lane_has_model. No suite declares a lane need: a git grep for RUNDESK_LANE_MODEL, needsModel, 'Lane:' and LANE_NEEDS finds only two comments, at ai-create-containers.mjs:343 and ai-answer-rendering.mjs:532. wt-break.sh applies lane_model_env only inside restart() (:105 and :116), and restart runs only on a sync or an API patch. So a lane keeps whatever model configuration its last launcher had. create-menu-ai.mjs:193,323,489 and task-ai-bar.mjs:95,126,245 assert 'not configured' and would red their baseline on a model lane (wt-break exit 5). No suite drives the model stub's /__control seam: the only __control users in test/e2e are the storage stub in attach-on-create.mjs:321 and task-cover.mjs:512,598. So the modelConfigured===true branches in ai-create-containers and ai-answer-rendering have never been measured. Stale around it: fleet-restart.sh:120-121 says 'Off unless RUNDESK_LANE_MODEL=1 ... the six suites'. =1 now means lane 1 only (lane-env.sh:156-160), and there are four suites. lane-env.sh:89-95 says all four flip, but its own :111-116 says two were converted. docs/video2-reaudit.md:6665-6674 says 'It is wired into no lane' and 'Six suites'.

*To close:* Smallest correct routing: (1) each suite declares its need in a greppable header, e.g. `// Lane: no-model` on create-menu-ai and task-ai-bar, and `// Lane: model` on any suite that stages __control/next. (2) run-plan.sh sources lane-env.sh and skips a lane whose lane_has_model answer differs from the suite's declared need. If no lane in $LANES matches, it refuses loudly with a new exit code, so the plan is never silently burned. (3) wt-break.sh, before the baseline, asks the lane's GET /api/v1/ai/status and refuses (new exit) when `available` differs from lane_has_model, or else restarts. (4) A checker asserts that every suite asserting 'not configured' in a chk declares no-model. Then write the model-path checks against model-stub's __control/next, since the frames-do-not-specify reason is no longer accepted.

*Partly fixed, 24 September (with `found-24-sep/model-patches-measured-without-a-model`):* the break runner now chooses for a SET. A set with a patch whose header says it reddens only where a model answers runs with one, baseline included. The runner's stamp of what a lane serves carries the model, so a lane is re-synced whenever its model differs from what the set asked for, and no longer keeps its last launcher's configuration. `check-model-lanes.sh`, 5 of 5 mutations. What is left is routing by SUITE: (1), (2) and (4) above, so that an invoker who puts every lane on a model (`RUNDESK_LANE_MODEL=all`) cannot send `create-menu-ai` or `task-ai-bar` to one. And the model-path checks against `__control/next`. ### `ledger-rows/row-850` — **closed**, small

**Add to a colleague's priorities — refused on purpose; the frame's prompt names the assignee, so ClickUp research should settle it**

*Evidence:* reaudit.md:850 (M, 'the write takes no :userId, deliberately'). people.controller.ts:100-119: PrioritiesController writes only the caller's own. Reading someone else's already exists at people.controller.ts:90-97 (GET /people/:userId/priorities). task-detail-sheet.tsx:2611-2635 shows the prompt only when `userId === currentUserId`.

*Researched, 29 September* (help centre, read through search excerpts; the hosts are not reachable from this environment). ClickUp settles it:
- "Members, Admins, and Owners can add tasks to other people's priorities" ("What are Personal Priorities?"; LineUp is now Personal Priorities). A guest cannot.
- A task's Priority field has "Add to Personal Priorities": pick a person's avatar. The task menu has Add to › Someone's Priorities.
- My Settings has "Ask to add task to priorities after assigning: Show a prompt asking if you'd like to add the task to the assigned member's priorities."
- The expanded view shows who added each task and when ("Added by", "Added at").
- A colleague's priorities are shown on their profile and in Teams Hub; a task the viewer cannot open reads "Private task".

*Closed, 29 September.* ClickUp settles it, so the refusal is gone. `POST /workspaces/:ws/people/:userId/priorities` adds a task to a colleague's list when:
- the caller is a member and not a guest (403);
- the colleague is a member (404);
- the body is a task, not a typed line (400);
- both of them can open the task, asked of each by `readableTask`: 404 for the caller, 403 for the colleague. ClickUp's sources do not say whether a task the colleague cannot open may be added, so the safe rule is taken.

A second add answers with the row that is there. Every row records who added it (`user_priorities.added_by_id`, migration 0167), and the list returns `addedBy`. Ticking, ordering and removing stay the owner's: the one who added a row gets 404.

Assigning a colleague now offers their priorities by name ("Add this task to <name>'s priorities?"). The offer follows the same "Don't ask again", is not made when the task is already open on their list, and is never made to a guest. The toast says whose list the task went on and opens their panel. The Planner rail and the person panel say "Added by" under a row somebody else added. Four locales.

- Regression on lanes 5–7 after the merge: 46 suites, each one that reads priorities, assignees, the Planner or the person panel, and `doc-import`. All 46 green, 1031 checks, among them `person-panel` 60/60 and `video-regression` 94/94 on the model lane.

Found while building it: `found-29-sep/priority-readd-answers-a-ticked-off-row`, `found-29-sep/priority-added-at-on-hover-only` and `found-29-sep/priority-field-adds-to-nobody-else`. The task menu's Add to › Someone's Priorities stays with `ledger-rows/row-845`; the route built here is the one it would call. The agent's note that the prompt could offer a colleague who cannot open the task does not hold: assigning refuses anybody who cannot see the task, judged as an assignee (`assertPersonCanSeeTask`), and the prompt follows only a successful assignment. So the write takes a person: a member, admin or owner may add a task they can see to anyone's priorities, and the prompt after assigning offers the assignee's. Not settled by the sources: whether a task the colleague cannot open may be added; the safe rule is to refuse it.

*Evidence, read:* the Meetings page's "Upcoming" reads the `meetings` table, which only calls and `POST /meetings` fill (`MeetingsService.upcoming`). The planner's grid draws `task_time_blocks`. The only reads of a person's calendar accounts are the picker's list and free/busy (`externalBusyWindows`, for the people panel). The inbound pull (`pullEvents`) turns the WORKSPACE connection's events into tasks, and nothing calls it on a schedule (`ledger-rows/row-1874`, the sync button). Nothing writes an event to the default account ("New events go here").

The sentences:
- Meetings: "Connect a calendar and your meetings will show up here." Corrected with the item above.
- Accounts page, `plannerAccounts.noneHint`: "Connect one and your events appear on the Planner, and your tasks can go the other way."
- Accounts page, `plannerAccounts.subtitle`: "One is where new events are created".

ClickUp (help centre, search snippets): the Planner "syncs with your connected Google or Outlook Calendar", two-way, and upcoming meetings come from it (the AI Notetaker joins the meetings on the connected calendar).

*To close:* read each connected account's events for a window (Google `events.list`, Graph `calendarView`), with the providers' base addresses overridable so a lane stub can answer, and draw them on the grid and in "Upcoming". Write a new event to the default account. Until then, correct the two Accounts page sentences.

*Triage, 5 October:* reproduced on a lane. The two Accounts-page sentences still promise that events appear on the Planner and that new events are created in one calendar. They are false, shown on lane 4 in four locales. Reading and writing connected calendars is unbuilt. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*Closed, 7 October* (lanes 4 and 2). ClickUp's help centre is blocked here; through search excerpts, its Planner shows a connected Google Calendar's events inside ClickUp, and time-blocking a task in it creates an event in the calendar. Rundesk's Accounts page said both, and now does both.

- A connected calendar's events are read for a window (`calendar-events.ts`: Google `events.list` with `singleEvents`, Graph `calendarView` in UTC), every page up to eight and the rest said, at the addresses the environment names (`GOOGLE_CALENDAR_API_URL`, `MS_GRAPH_API_URL`), so a lane's stub answers them. Which calendars: the ones the planner's picker has ticked (`countsAsBusy`, the column that already meant "this calendar is read"), each read on its own, and a failure costing only its own events and SAID, by address (`unread`): refused (the grant is gone) or failed. Only ever the caller's own accounts; a colleague is shown free/busy alone, as before.
- An access token is refreshed when it has expired, or is about to, and once more when the provider refuses it, at the token addresses (`GOOGLE_TOKEN_URL`, and `MICROSOFT_TOKEN_URL` as the workspace connection already read it); the new token is kept. Free/busy reads through the same refresh: it sent the token an account was connected with, which Google refuses an hour later.
- `GET /planner/:ws/events?from&to` (the blocks' range rule) answers them; an event that is one of the person's own written blocks is left out, so it is drawn once, as the block.
- The planner draws them: a timed event in its day's column, behind the blocks, an all-day one in the all-day row on every day it covers, each opening in its calendar; fetched only while an account calendar is ticked. A calendar that could not be read is named above the grid.
- Meetings' "Upcoming" lists the next week's timed events beside Rundesk's meetings, soonest first, ten at most, each with whose calendar it is and an Open link; a calendar that could not be read is named.
- A block made on the planner is written to the default calendar as an event (a task's block titled with the task); moving it moves the event and deleting it deletes it (`task_time_blocks.calendar_account_id`, `external_event_id`, migration 0173; set null when the account is disconnected). The block is saved whatever the calendar answers, and the answer says what it did (`calendar`); one not taken is toasted. A block made before any calendar was connected, or whose write failed, is written the next time it changes.
- The lanes run `scripts/e2e-lanes/calendar-stub.mjs` (port 94k, on every lane): Google's and Graph's calls and token addresses, a calendar per bearer token, a control seam to seed, read, fail and forget one. `check-calendar-stub.mjs` drives the product's own readers and writers against it, and each of its rules broken in turn reddens a case.

Measured on lane 4 with the new suite `connected-calendars` (a person of the run's own with three accounts — a Google default with events, a Microsoft one whose grant is gone, a Google one whose token has expired — and a colleague in their workspace): before, on the build of `a936b69` with the resume-8 change (no calendar code), 0 of 11 — `GET /planner/:ws/events` answered 404, nothing was read or refreshed, a block's answer said nothing of a calendar and none was written, and neither page drew an event or named a calendar. **Whether a subtask may be merged into its own parent is still an unanswered product question**

*Closed, 29 September, allowed.* ClickUp (help centre "Merge tasks", "Manage subtasks in a task window using the Bulk Action Toolbar" and "Work with subtasks from tasks", read through search summaries because the proxy refuses the pages): subtasks are merged into another task from the parent's own subtask toolbar, or from a subtask's menu, and nothing excludes the parent. ### `found-5-oct/guests-read-and-delete-every-clip` — **closed** (security, small; found by the triage beside `found-30-sep/guests-may-ask-for-clip-links`) · reproduced 5 October

**A guest lists, downloads and deletes every clip in the workspace's library**

*Evidence, reproduced 5 October on lane 1 by the triage's skeptic:* a guest of a throwaway workspace, an admin's clip in its library.
- As the guest, `GET /workspaces/:ws/clips` answered 200 with the admin's clip, and the signed URL in the listing downloaded its bytes (200).
- `DELETE /workspaces/:ws/clips {storageKey}` on the admin's clip answered 200. The admin's listing was then empty, and the clip's public link answered 404 "Clip not found".
- The guest can also add clips to the library (presign 201, PUT 200), and a member then lists them.
- In the browser, signed in as the guest, `/app/:ws/clips` drew the admin's card with its delete button; confirming the dialog deleted it.
- Control in the same run: the same guest's `GET …/canvases?type=whiteboard` answered `[]` after the admin made a board, as the closed `found-24-sep/guests-list-every-whiteboard` rule says (no share can name a canvas; none can name a clip either).

The cause: `clips.controller.ts` is guarded by `JwtAuthGuard` and `WorkspaceMemberGuard` alone. `ClipsService.list` returns every clip with a signed URL, and `remove` checks only the key's shape, with no role and no owner. Not measured: a member deleting another person's clip goes through the same route.

*To close:* research what ClickUp lets a guest do with a workspace's clips (see, delete, record), and what a member may do with another's clip. Then give the library's routes the guest read rule and an owner-or-manager rule for delete, and check both in a suite.

*ClickUp* (help.clickup.com, through search excerpts; the site is blocked here). "Clips feature availability and limits": guests, like members, can record Clips and Voice Clips, "use Clips Hub" and "view Clips shared with them"; only members and admins comment on them; "Clips Hub only displays Clips, Voice Clips, and SyncUps recorded by you". "Clips Hub": a clip's ellipsis menu there offers Rename, Download and Delete. "Manage your Workspace storage": storage is freed by deleting "Clip recordings from Clips Hub". Nothing found says whether an owner or admin may delete somebody else's clip.

*Measured before, lane 5, the triage's probe twice alike:* a guest was listed all 5 clips, and the admin's signed URL served its bytes (200). The guest's DELETE of the admin's clip answered 200 and the admin lost it. The guest recorded a clip (201/200) and a member listed it. A member deleted another member's clip (200), and the admin's (200). Search handed the guest the admin's clip and its storage key. With that key the guest got the clip's link (201; the anonymous watch 200). The first version of this fix left that open, and with it a share of the clip (public and to a member, 201) and a copy of it on a task shared with the guest to edit (201), which served the admin's bytes; measured on its build, twice alike. The guest's clips page drew the admin's card with Delete, and confirming deleted it. Control: the guest's whiteboards, 200 [].

*Closed, 5 October.* One rule, `modules/clips/clip-access.ts`. A clip's recorder is the id its object now carries (`recordedbyid`, written at presign), or, for a clip recorded before, its address (`recordedby`). A guest reads the clips they recorded, as ClickUp's hub shows a person what they recorded. A clip somebody shares with them (Share › Member mails them its link) is watched through that link and does not join their library. Anybody else in the workspace reads every clip, as before. A clip is deleted by its recorder or by somebody who manages the workspace (`isManagerRole`). Who is asking is read one way for every route that asks (`clip-reader.ts`): their address as the users table holds it, and their role as the workspace guards give it (a platform super admin is `super_admin`). It is asked in:
- the library: a guest's newest 200 of their own, looked for a page at a time; nothing is signed for a clip its reader may not see; each listed clip says `mayDelete`;
- delete: 403 "Only the person who recorded this clip, or a manager or admin of the workspace, can delete it"; a key naming no clip is 404 for anybody who would have to be its recorder; a manager's delete is not looked up;
- link, share (every mode) and a task's copy of a clip (`POST tasks/:id/attachments/from-clip`): 403 "Guests can share or attach only the clips they recorded"; a key naming no clip is still 404;
- search's clip branch: a guest finds only the clips they recorded, their matches looked up a page at a time (they were looked up one store round trip after another).
Recording stays everybody's, a guest's included (ClickUp: guests record Clips). The clips page offers Delete only where `mayDelete` is true. It says a refused delete in the dialog in the server's words (fallback `clips.deleteFailed`, four locales), and opens the dialog on the next clip without the last refusal. Whether a guest may make a public link at all, even of a clip they recorded, stays the owner's (`found-30-sep/guests-may-ask-for-clip-links`).

The new suite `clip-library-access`, 10 checks, against the lane's real store: the library as a guest and as a member; search; a guest's delete; members' and a manager's deletes; the page as the recorder and as the guest; a delete refused after the reader's role changed; the dialog on the next clip after a refusal; a guest's link, share and task copy of another's clip and of their own; and clips stored before clips carried their recorder's id, which are listed, found, linked and deleted by their recorder and by nobody else.
- Before: HEAD's API and bundle on lane 5, 0 of 10 (the tenth stops: at HEAD the upload names no recorder id); the first version of this fix, 9 of 10 (link, share and a task's copy open).
- After: 10/10, five runs. Measured again with the same probes, twice alike. The guest is listed only their own, is refused the admin's clip (403, the sentence; kept), and records and deletes their own. Their link, share and task copy of the admin's clip are refused (403, "Guests can share or attach only the clips they recorded"; nothing made), and of their own are made (201); a key naming nothing answers 404. Members are refused another's clip and the admin's (403; kept) and delete their own. The manager deletes a member's. Search finds the guest nothing of the admin's. The guest's page draws no card of the admin's and no Delete. The admin's Share › Member to the guest still mails the link (201), and it plays for them (200).

`clacc-1..9` and `clacc-21..26`, each reddening on lane 5 the check it names; unit claims `clacc-10..20` and `clacc-27..31`, each failing its test. Re-aimed where this moved their anchors: `clacc-2`, `clacc-20`, `clb-3`, `csl-17`, `csl-22`, each shown reddening again. Unit tests: clips 26 → 39, search.service 51 → 55; API 1962/1962, web 321/321; both typechecks clean. In CI. Regression on lane 5, 20/20 besides the new suite: `clip-links`, `clip-created-card`, `clip-library`, `object-key-boundaries`, `private-object-urls`, `public-route-limits`, `public-pages-busy`, `workspace-delete-for-good`, `settings-depth`, `search-index`, `search-read-access`, `guest-read-scope`, `guest-chat-scope`, `private-list-reach`, `private-folder-reach`, `search-sources`, `trending-sort`, `like-literal`, `video-regression`, and `clip-library-access` three times.

*Not changed, for the owner:* a member's library still lists every clip of the workspace, where ClickUp's hub lists only your own. Whether a guest may make a public link of a clip they recorded (`found-30-sep/guests-may-ask-for-clip-links`): their own is linked, shared and attached as before. Whose a clip is lives only in its object's metadata, so a guest's library, and a guest's search, still look up to every clip of the workspace (200 at a time) to find their own.

*Merged, 6 October,* into the main checkout with the batch's other two builders' work (fields, clips, sign-in and sockets), and run again there on lanes 2, 5 and 7: 47 suites, all green — `password-hash-time`, which compares timings, failed once at a load of 13 on four cores and passed 4/4 twice on a quiet lane — and the API's 1984 unit tests and the web's 320, both typechecks clean.

### `found-5-oct/readers-change-shared-views` — **closed** (security, small; found by the triage beside `found-25-sep/view-only-individual-permissions`) · reproduced 5 October

**A reader of a list renames, reconfigures, deletes and re-defaults the views everybody shares**

*Evidence, reproduced 5 October on lane 7 by the triage's skeptic:* a space whose default is View only, a list holding five views the admin made (visibility "everyone", one the default). A plain member, and a guest given the list at View. The same for both:
- `PATCH` an admin's view with a new name and config: 200; `DELETE` an admin's view: 200, gone.
- `POST` a view of their own: 201; `PATCH` it `{isDefault: true, isPinned: true}`: 200, and the list's default moved to it.
- On a list with no views, the member's first `POST /lists/:id/views` was saved with `isDefault` true and visibility "everyone", and the admin's list then opened on it.
- Control in the same run: the same member's `PATCH` of a task title on that list answered 403, "This space's default permission is "View only", which does not allow changing its tasks".

The cause: `views.service.ts` `create()` asks no level and makes the first view the default; `assertMayWrite` returns at once for a view whose visibility is "everyone". The list page's view menu offers Update, Rename, Make default and Delete on every view to everybody. The ledger's own line ("Saved views … made by any reader … change what the reader sees, not the list") does not hold: they change what everyone sees.

*To close:* research ClickUp's rule for who may create, change and delete a shared view, and who may set a list's default view (its view-only individual permission "create views" is off by default). Ask the location's level on every shared-view write, keep a reader's private views theirs, offer in the menu only what the reader may do, and check it in a suite.

*Closed, 5 October* (worktree off `68b89c1`, lane 6; reviewed, and fixed after review):

ClickUp (help centre, read through search excerpts; the help centre is not reachable from here):
- "Views feature availability and limits": "To create views, you must have Edit or Full edit permissions to the List, Subfolder, Folder, or Space where the view is created."
- "Manage individual permissions for view only users": view-only users and guests have four individual permissions, and "Add/remove tags and create views are deactivated by default."
- "Manage Custom Role permissions": the Create Views permission "permits users to create and edit views on locations", and "when toggled off, members can still create personal views".
- "Permissions in detail": Edit "Permits the person to make changes to a location or item … The person isn't able to delete the location or item". Comment is "to add and reply to comments"; View only gives "read-only access".
- "Delete a view": "Guests with Full access to a Folder, Subfolder, or List can delete views in it."
- "Protect a view" and "Create and share a private view": a person given Full edit on a view "can save changes, protect and unprotect, share, and delete the view"; Limited "can only view, duplicate, and favorite the view".
- "Set a default view": "On the Business Plan and above, owners and admins can set default views for everyone in specific Workspace locations"; "any guest, member, or admin can set their own personal default".
- "Pin a view": "Everyone, including guests with full edit permissions, can pin the views they have access to."

What changed:
- **Every write to a shared view asks the level on that view** (`views/view-write.ts`).
  - The chain is the one the view's share panel already read (`SharesService.locate`): a share on the view itself first, then the list, its project, its folder and the space. It is read through `resolveSpaceLevel`, as every write rule reads it (`WithinStep` takes `view`).
  - Changing a view (its name, layout, pin, position, who sees it) asks Edit.
  - Deleting one asks Full edit, as deleting a task or a location does here.
  - Making a view, making a private one shared, and changing the list's default ask the list's level, Edit.
  - A refusal is a 403 in the level's words: "This space's default permission is "View only", which does not allow changing its shared views" (… "deleting its shared views", … "adding a shared view", … "changing its default view"). For a share, it is the share's words: "What is shared with you here is "View only", …".
  - A protected view keeps its own rule on top: its maker and the workspace's managers.
- **A private view stays its maker's at any level.** They make, rename, reconfigure, pin and delete it. Making it shared asks the list's level, and it is never the list's default.
- **One default per list.**
  - Making a view and Make default each run in one transaction under a lock on the list (`lockListViews`).
  - The list's first shared view becomes its default; private views are not counted.
  - A private view that the old rule made a list's default gives the default up to that first shared view.
- **The page offers only what the reader may do.** `GET /lists/:id/views` gives each view `mayChange`, `mayDelete`, `mayMakeDefault`, `mayChangeVisibility` and `mayMakePrivate` (`viewOffers`, the write rule's answers). The list's capabilities give `views`.
  - The tab's ⋯ offers Update, Rename, Make default and Delete by those answers, with Delete only at Full edit. It is not drawn when it would offer nothing.
  - + View and Save view follow the list's answer or the view's.
  - The Customize panel draws Pin, Private, Protect and Set as default disabled where the reader may not use them, and Private disabled on the list's default. Autosave stays the reader's own.
  - Make default is no longer offered on a private view.
  - A refused write from the page says why, in the server's words.

*Measured* on lane 6 (probes adapted from the triage's `views-by-readers.mjs` and from the review's):
- Before (`68b89c1`), as on 5 October:
  - The view-only member and the guest renamed, reconfigured and deleted the admin's views, and made their own the default (200).
  - The member's first view on an empty list was saved shared and as the default.
  - The task-title control was refused (403). A member at Comment did the same as the readers.
- The review of the first build measured more:
  - A member held to View on one view by a share on it renamed and deleted it (200). One given Full edit on a view of a view-only list was refused (403). The share panel read both cases the other way.
  - A member at Edit, refused trashing a task (403), deleted the list's default view for good (200).
  - Six views made at once on an empty list left 4, 6 and 6 defaults; three Make defaults at once left up to 3.
  - The panel offered Private on the default view (400 when pressed).
  - A private default left by the old rule sat beside the first shared view as a second default.
- After:
  - The readers are refused every write (403, in the level's words), and the views are as the admin left them. Their own private views are theirs.
  - Comment is refused the same.
  - Edit makes, renames, pins and defaults, and is refused deleting (403); so is an Edit guest. Full edit deletes, for a member and a guest alike.
  - The View share refuses (403, in the share's words). The Full edit share renames and deletes that view (200) and does not choose the list's default (403).
  - The list keeps one default however many ask at once, and Private is not offered on the default.
  - The task-title control is unchanged.

The suite `view-writes-by-level` has 20 checks:
- the readers on the admin's views, and making one (read back by SQL);
- a reader's own private view; the empty list's default;
- Comment and Edit; deleting at Full edit, by a member and by a guest;
- what the API offers: the list's `views`, and each view's offers;
- a View share on one view; a Full edit share on one view; a workspace manager's offers and rename;
- six views made at once; Make default pressed at once; a private default giving way (its fixture written by SQL);
- the page: the view-only list (+ View, ⋯, Save view); the member's own private view's ⋯; the Customize panel for a reader; the Edit list's ⋯ (no Delete) and a rename from it; the panel on a view of their own, with Pin and Set as default saved; Private not offered once it is the default; and a rename refused in the server's words after the space drops to View only while the page is open.

Results:
- `68b89c1`'s API and web: 1/20. The one passing check guards against the panel locking for everybody.
- The first build: 10/20.
- Final: 20/20, four runs on lane 6.

Break patches. Each was measured on lane 6 against a 20/20 baseline and reddens exactly what it claims.
- e2e `vwl-1..18` and `vwl-28..42`:
  - re-aimed at moved lines: `vwl-1`, `-4`, `-5`, `-7`, `-9`, `-13`;
  - claims reworded to follow the reworded checks: `vwl-2`, `-6`, `-17`, `-18`.
- unit `vwl-19..27` and `vwl-43..50`, on `view-write.test.ts` (16 tests). Each reddens its test; re-aimed: `vwl-20`, `-26`, `-27`.
- `view-visibility-1..6`, re-run on the final rule: each reddens its claim.

Regression on lane 6, all green: `view-visibility` 23, `list-save-view` 7, `list-page-levels` 9, `list-customize` 37, `list-card-cover` 26, `list-view-controls` 50, `list-export` 33, `paywall-sites` 30, `space-features` 12, `task-depth` 92, `space-wizard` 23, `team-view` 13, `ui-sweep` 107, `video-regression` 94.
- API unit tests 1961/1961; web 321/321; both typechecks clean.
- In CI: the postgres-harnesses comment counts 258 after the merge (257 in the worktree).

*Not changed, recorded (the owner's to decide):*
- **Who sets a list's default for everyone.**
  - ClickUp: owners and admins, on the Business Plan and above, with a personal default for everybody else. "Setting a default view for everyone will also make that view required."
  - Here, Make default is the only default and asks Edit on the view and on the list.
  - Personal defaults, required views and plan gating are unbuilt.
  - The workspace dashboard's default asks `dashboard.workspace_default.manage`, an admin's by default.
- **Pin.** ClickUp's text says everyone can pin the views they can open, and guests with Full edit. Here a pin is one flag that reorders every reader's strip, so it asks Edit on the view: a view-only member is refused, and an Edit guest pins.
- **Whether + View should offer a reader a private view.** ClickUp lets members make personal views without the Create Views permission. Here a reader makes, renames and deletes their own private views through the API, but the page offers them none.
- **A guest's individual "create views" switch** (`found-25-sep/view-only-individual-permissions`). A guest at Edit makes shared views by the location's level.
- **A colleague's private view answers 404 "View not found".**
  - An id naming nothing answers 404 "Resource not found", so the 404 does not hide that the view exists.
  - The owner's 1 October rule is 403 with its reason.
  - Changing it reverses four `view-visibility` checks.
- **A share on a view does not reach every rule.** It gives nothing on a protected view to somebody who is not its maker or a manager, gives no protect or unprotect (those are its maker's and the managers'), and does not open a private view. ClickUp's Full edit on a view does all three.
- **Required views.** ClickUp: "You can't delete a required view." Here the list's default can be deleted at Full edit, which leaves the list with no default.

The line in `found-25-sep/list-page-offers-refused-edits` ("Saved views … change what the reader sees, not the list") now holds only for saved filters and private views.

### `found-5-oct/default-list-files-into-an-archived-list` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found by the triage beside `found-24-sep/planner-default-list-read-by-nothing`) · reproduced 5 October

**A task made by /task, a chat message or the AI lands in an archived Default list, where nobody can find it**

*Evidence, reproduced 5 October on lane 7 by the triage's skeptic:* a member chose a list as their planner Default list (`PATCH /planner/:ws/settings`, 200). Message-to-task and `/task` then filed into it (201), as they should. The admin archived that list (`DELETE /lists/:id`, 200, `is_archived` true). `/task` afterwards still answered 201 and filed the task into the archived list, while the settings still named it; `GET /projects/:id/lists` no longer lists it. A direct `POST /tasks` into the archived list answered 201 too.

The cause: in `tasks.service.ts` `defaultListFor`, the chosen list is asked only for its workspace and `canCreateTaskIn`; the fallback alone filters out archived lists. The create gate (`common/permissions/task-create.ts`) never asks whether a list is archived.

*To close:* research what ClickUp does when a Default list is archived (fall back to the personal list, or refuse and say so) and whether a task can be made in an archived list at all. Then do the same in `defaultListFor` and the create gate, and check it in a suite.

*Closed, 6 October* (lane 6). ClickUp files a task made with no location in the person's Personal List ("Your Personal List is the default location for new tasks…"; help centre, "Create and add tasks to your Personal List", through search excerpts). Rundesk has no Personal List. A deleted List "moves to the Trash" with its tasks ("Restore items from the Trash"). An archived one leaves the sidebar but is "preserved and searchable" ("Archive or restore Folders, Subfolders, and Lists"). Nothing was found on what becomes of a deleted Default list, or on making a task in a deleted List. Rundesk's `DELETE /lists/:id` puts the list in the trash, so where ClickUp does not settle it, the person is refused with the reason rather than sent to a fallback.

- The create gate (`assertCanCreateTaskIn`) refuses a list in the trash with 409 "This list is in the trash. Restore it from Trash before adding tasks to it." (`ListInTrashException`). Since the review fix, what it advises follows the Trash's rule (below).
  - It is asked after the read rule, so somebody who may not open the list is still told "List not found" and learns nothing of the trash. It is asked before the space's level.
  - Every way of making a task through `createTask` asks it: `POST /tasks`, chat, the AI, templates, a meeting's action items. Mail and inbound hooks do not go through `createTask`; the review fix (below) covers them.
- `defaultListFor` asks the gate of the chosen list. When the refusal is the trash, `/task`, a chat message made into a task and the AI's "Create task from this" are refused with 409 'Your "Default list for new tasks" is in the trash. Restore it from Trash, or choose another in Calendar settings → Time blocking.' Since the review fix, those are the words a workspace admin, or whoever deleted the list, is given; anybody else is told to ask them (below).
  - Any other refusal still passes the choice over to the oldest list the person may add to, as before.
  - The three flows already show a refusal in the server's words. No new strings.

Measured on lane 6 (`probe-default-list.mjs`, the skeptic's route, three runs alike):
- Before: a member chose a list (200) and `/task` filed into it (201). The admin deleted it (200). `is_archived` was true and the settings still named it; `GET /lists/project/:id` no longer listed it. Then `/task`, message-to-task and the AI's create-task each answered 201 into the deleted list, and `POST /tasks` into it answered 201 for the member and for the admin.
- After: the three answer 409 in the Default list's words and make nothing anywhere. `POST /tasks` into the list answers 409 in the list's words, nothing made. Restored from Trash, the list takes a task again (201).

Checks:

*Review fix, 6 October* (lane 6). The review found the rule unasked wherever a task reaches a list without createTask, and the refusal's advice untrue for most members.

### `found-5-oct/xlsx-read-as-text` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found by the triage beside `commit-log/log-601eacc-2` and `ledger-rows/row-816`) · reproduced 5 October

**An .xlsx put into the spreadsheet import is read as text, offered for import, and fails leaving an empty space behind**

*Evidence, reproduced 5 October on lane 1 by two of the triage's skeptics:* the page says ".xlsx is not read — re-save the sheet as CSV first", and its file input says `accept=".csv,.tsv,.txt"`. That is only a hint to the picker: the dialog's "All files", or a drop, puts an .xlsx in. The page took it ("triage-board.xlsx (1.5 KB)"). Preview answered 201 with one column named by the zip's bytes (`PK\u0003\u0004…[Content_Types].xml…`) and drew them as column names. Mapping that column to Title enabled "Start import (1 task)". Pressing it, the panel said "Import failed / unsupported Unicode escape sequence"; the job ended failed with 0 tasks made, and left a new space, project and an empty "Imported Tasks" list behind.

The cause: `workspace-import-page.tsx` `onFileChange` reads any file with `readAsText` and checks neither its name nor its content; `spreadsheet-import.service.ts` parses any string as delimited text, makes the space and project outside a transaction, and writes an error holding a NUL into the job's jsonb, which Postgres refuses. Its own comment says the UI asks for CSV "rather than accepting an .xlsx it would then fail to read". The document import refuses a .docx by its name.

*To close:* refuse a file that is not delimited text, by its name and by its first bytes (a zip begins `PK`), before anything is made, in the words the page already uses; make a failed import leave nothing behind; check both in a suite. Reading .xlsx is the separate feature in `ledger-rows/row-816`.

*Closed, 5 October.* ClickUp's Spreadsheets Importer reads .xls, .xlsx, .csv, .xml, .json, .tsv and .txt (help centre, through search excerpts); Rundesk reads delimited text only, and reading .xlsx stays the feature `ledger-rows/row-816`. What is closed is the defect: a file that is not delimited text is refused before anything is made, and a failed import leaves nothing.

- The page (`isSheetFile`, `lib/sheet-file.ts`) checks a chosen file's name, which must be one of the server's `acceptedExtensions`, and its first eight bytes, which must not be a zip's signature (.xlsx, .ods) or a legacy .xls's compound-file signature (D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1). It checks both before reading the file. It refuses in the two sentences already under the picker and keeps no name, content or preview. Only the last file chosen is read into the page (`createPickTurns`): a read still in progress when another file is chosen, refused or not, is dropped. No new strings.
- The spreadsheet routes receive content only. Preview and start therefore check its first bytes: a zip (`isZipContent`), or a first line holding a NUL, which no header row of delimited text has (`headerHoldsNul`). Either is answered 400 in the page's words before parsing. Content that is not a string goes on to the parser and gets 400 'The file has no header row.', as it did before.
- Nothing written to the job row holds a NUL (`storable` writes each one as U+FFFD). A NUL in one row's title used to reach the job's jsonb inside that row's error, and the whole run failed on its last write with the raw message 'unsupported Unicode escape sequence'. That row now fails alone, like any row the database refuses.
- A run that fails takes away what it made (`undoRun`): its project, and by the foreign keys every list, status and task in it; its space when it made one; and the tags it made that label nothing. A merge into a task that was already there stays and is counted. Each list, and each row with its people and tags, is written in its own transaction that waits only on its own writes. A row that fails leaves nothing half-written, and the rest of the file goes on. The run is not one transaction: that design was tried first and measured on lane 4. It held one pooled connection for the whole run while each progress write waited for another. Twelve imports at once held all ten connections, and no route answered until the API was restarted (none of the 7,200 tasks committed). A merged task stayed locked until the run ended: a PATCH waited 5.4 s, and nine PATCHes stopped the API. A tag the run made could not be seen until then, so the tags route made a second tag in another case.

Measured on lane 4 (`probe-xlsx-ui.mjs`, `probe-xlsx-api.mjs`, the triage's .xlsx):
- before: the page took an .xlsx and an .xlsx renamed .csv ("triage-board.xlsx (1.5 KB)"), Preview enabled, and drew one column of zip bytes over 3 rows; over the API preview and import answered 201, and the job failed "unsupported Unicode escape sequence", leaving a space, a project and an empty "Imported Tasks" list; a CSV with a NUL in its second row failed with its first row imported, leaving space, project, list and task.
- after: the page refuses both in those words, Preview disabled, no request sent; preview and import answer 400 in the same words, no job row; the NUL file's job fails with created 0 and nothing left.

Checks:
- `imports` +5: the page by name (an .xlsx, and an .xls, which is no zip), the page by first bytes (an .xlsx renamed .csv), the server, a failed import leaving nothing, and a row Postgres refuses still failing alone (a year-0 date; green before as after: it guards the savepoints). On HEAD's product code the first four were red.
- `sheet-file.test.ts` (4) is new; `spreadsheet-import.util.test.ts` +2; `spreadsheet-import.service.test.ts` 4.
- `imports-29..33` redden exactly their checks; `isu-1`, `isu-2`, `iss-1`, `iss-2`, `iss-4`, `iss-5` and `sfl-1..4` redden their tests. `imports-10`, `-11` and `-13` were anchored on lines the transaction re-indented; re-aimed, each reddens its claim.

Run on lane 4 with the four import items: `imports` 33/33 three times, `data-transfer-keys` 7/7, `doc-import` 16/16, `sidebar-sections` 25/25, `space-create-menu` 32/32.

*Review fix, 6 October* (lane 4). The first build ran each import in one transaction; the review measured what that cost, and the fixer replaced it with the design above. Measured:
- Before, on the batch as first built (lane 4): a real legacy .xls renamed .csv was accepted by the page, previewed as 5 columns of binary, and imported (201) to a job that failed with 'unsupported Unicode escape sequence'. A 20 MB CSV replaced 5 ms later by a refused zip left Preview enabled, and Preview sent the 21 MB file (3 runs of 3). A NUL in one title failed the whole run and took its good rows with it. A preview with content 123 answered 500. Twelve imports at once and a merge with nine edits stopped the API, as above.
- After: the .xls is refused by the page and by both routes (400, no job row, no space). The superseded read is dropped (Preview disabled, 3 of 3). The NUL row fails alone (completed, created 2). Content 123 gets 400. Twelve imports of 600 rows complete (7,200 tasks) while /health answers in 4–7 ms. An edit of a merged task answers in 33 ms during the run.

Checks: imports goes 20 → 33 (builder) → 43. This item's checks:
- by name (the .xls fixture is now text named .xls);
- an .xlsx renamed .csv;
- a legacy .xls renamed .csv;
- a superseded slow read;
- the server refusing the .xlsx and the .xls;
- a number as content;
- a NUL row failing alone;
- a run whose last write the database refuses ends failed and leaves nothing (a trigger on clickup_import_jobs for the run's workspace refuses its 'completed');
- a refused date row failing alone;
- twelve imports at once;
- an edit during a merge.
On the builder's product code, the 10 new checks were red and the last-write check was green. After, 43/43 three times.
Units: sheet-file.test.ts 6; spreadsheet-import.util.test.ts 24; spreadsheet-import.service.test.ts 12 (its stand-in now models transactions, deletes and the pool).
Patches: imports-29..33 and imports-36..42 each redden their own check (-30 also reddens the slow-read check, -31 the .xls server check, -33 the NUL-row check). imports-41 stops the lane's API, which must be restarted after it. imports-10, -11 and -13 were re-aimed again. Unit claims isu-1..8, iss-1..12, sfl-1..6.

Found beside it: `found-6-oct/clickup-import-leaves-a-failed-run-behind`, `found-6-oct/doc-import-answers-500-to-a-binary-file`, `found-6-oct/import-start-answers-500-to-non-text`, `found-6-oct/verify-timeout-ends-no-hung-suite`, `found-6-oct/verify-refuses-a-lane-restarted-in-its-builds-second`.

### `found-5-oct/timeline-press-moves-dates` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found by the triage beside `resume-defects/resume-5`) · reproduced 5 October

**A press on a timeline bar rewrites the task's dates, and the Gantt drag drops the times**

*Evidence, reproduced 5 October on lane 4 by the triage's skeptic* (screenshots in `/tmp/claude-0/triage/lane4-sk/` on that machine):
1. Workspace timeline, a UTC browser: a press and release on a bar, without moving, changed a task due 9 October 17:30 and starting 7 October 09:00 to midnight on both days. No task sheet opened. `workspace-timeline-page.tsx` saves `startOfDay` of each date on every mouseup, even when the bar did not move.
2. The same press in a Los Angeles browser on a date-only task, 12–14 October: it became 11 October 07:00Z – 13 October 07:00Z. One click moved it a day earlier.
3. The list's Gantt, a UTC browser: a one-day drag of a task 16 October 09:00 – 17 October 15:00 saved 17 and 18 October at midnight. `rescheduleTaskSpan` sends `yyyy-MM-dd`, the loss `lib/task-dates.ts` `withDatePart` exists to prevent.
4. The list's Gantt, a Los Angeles browser: a date-only task of 19–21 October is drawn as "Oct 18 – Oct 20", every date-only bar a day early, and a one-day drag saved nothing. `GanttView` reads a UTC-midnight day as local time.

Coverage: `list-page-levels.mjs` asserts only that the due date changed, in a UTC browser; no suite presses or drags a workspace-timeline bar.

*To close:* a press that does not move a bar saves nothing; a drag moves each date by whole days and keeps its time (`withDatePart`); a date-only day is drawn and moved as that day in any zone. Check each in a suite in UTC and in a zone west of it.

*Closed, 6 October* (built by an agent on lane 5). ClickUp (help centre, "Rescheduling dependencies", read through search excerpts): "To reschedule tasks from a Gantt view, you can drag and drop a task to an earlier or later date, or click and drag the right end of a task to adjust the due date." Measured first on lane 5 with a browser probe in UTC, Los Angeles and Karachi: a press on a workspace-timeline bar sent a PATCH and rewrote 7 Oct 09:00Z – 9 Oct 17:30Z to local midnight (00:00Z, 07:00Z, 19:00Z the day before), and in Los Angeles moved a date-only task of 12–14 October to 11–13 October (drawn from the 11th); a day's drag saved local midnight, gave a due-only task a start, and each handle dropped its date's time; the CSV export in Los Angeles dated that task the 11th to the 13th. The list's Gantt sent `yyyy-MM-dd` (a drag of 16 Oct 09:00 – 17 Oct 15:00 saved midnight in every zone), and in Los Angeles titled a task of 19–21 October "Oct 18 – Oct 20" and saved nothing on a day's drag. What changed: `lib/task-dates.ts` gains `shownDay` (the day a date is shown as, by the date-only rule) and `shiftByDays` (whole days, keeping the time; a date-only day stays date-only); the timeline draws, ranges and exports by them, saves nothing for a drag that ends where it began, moves only the dates a task has, and its handles keep their date's time; the list's Gantt draws by `shownDay` and sends `shiftByDays`. After, same probe, three zones: a press sends nothing; a day's drag saves 8 Oct 09:00Z / 10 Oct 17:30Z, a date-only task 13–15 October, a due-only task no start; the handles keep 09:00 and 17:30; the date-only bar starts on the 12th and the export says 12–14, three days; the Gantt saves 17 Oct 09:00 – 18 Oct 15:00 and draws 19–21 October as "Oct 19 – Oct 21", three days after the task of the 16th. Checks: `timeline-dates` (new, in ci.yml), 9 of its 12 checks, 0/9 on HEAD's bundle, 12/12 four times after; `task-dates.test.ts` 14 → 19. Break patches `timeline-dates-1` to `-8` (e2e) and `tpm-1` to `-4` (unit), each shown to redden its check on lane 5 and restored.

*Review, 6 October (lane 5).* A press whose mouse travelled a pixel or two still moved a bar: at Auto fit (3.03 px a day) 2 px of travel saved the task a day later. The timeline now treats travel within the list Gantt's own threshold as a press (`GANTT_DRAG_THRESHOLD`, 4 px, now in `lib/gantt.ts` and shared); after, 2 px sends nothing. The list's Calendar and Table read a date-only day as the local day of its UTC midnight: in Los Angeles a task due the 19th read 'Oct 18' in the Table and sat in the 18th's cell, while the Gantt drew the 19th. A Calendar drop sent `yyyy-MM-dd`, so a task due at 17:30 dropped on another day lost its time. The Calendar is now keyed by `toDateInput`, the drop writes `withDatePart`, and the Table, row, subtask and Board labels read `shownDay`. After, in UTC and Los Angeles, a date-only task is drawn and labelled on its own day, a drop keeps date-only days date-only, and a timed task keeps its hour. Checks: `timeline-dates` 9 → 12, two of the new checks this item's (a press with a tremor; the list's Calendar and Table); patches `timeline-dates-12`, `-13` and `-14` each redden exactly their check, and `-1` and `-2` now also claim the new checks they redden. Not built, for the owner: a drag across a clock change can land a timed date on UTC midnight (the has-time decision), and the handles of a task that starts after its due date move against the drag, as at HEAD.

### `found-5-oct/comment-links-not-links` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found by the triage beside `resume-defects/s4-clip-link`) · reproduced 5 October

**A web address in a one-line comment is drawn as plain text, not a link**

*Evidence, reproduced 5 October on lane 4 by the triage's skeptic:* two comments posted (201 each): "see https://example.com/triage-plain for the spec", and "notes" followed by a list holding the same kind of address. In the task sheet's Comments tab the first address is text with no link (0 anchors); the second, because the comment holds a list, is a link (1 anchor).

The cause: `mention-text.tsx` takes its plain path whenever the text has no block markdown, and draws every segment as a `<span>`; `markdown.tsx`'s bare-URL autolinker is reached only on the block path. The plain path's comment explains skipping emphasis, not links.

*To close:* research how ClickUp draws a pasted address in a comment (a link, opening in a new tab). Link bare addresses on the plain path too, safely (http and https only), and check both kinds of comment in a suite.

*Closed, 6 October* (lane 4). An address in a one-line comment is a link, as one in a comment holding a list already was: `splitAddresses` (`lib/link-addresses.ts`) splits the plain path's text into its `http:` and `https:` addresses and the text around them, the address without the full stop, comma or bracket that ends its sentence, and every other character as typed; each opens in a new tab (`noreferrer noopener`). A `javascript:` or `data:` address stays text. ClickUp detects an address typed or pasted into a comment and opens it in a new tab ("URL links in tasks", read through search excerpts).

Measured on lane 4 with the extended `comment-slash-commands` suite: before, on the build these fixes went onto, the one-line comment's two addresses were text (no anchor), while the one in the comment holding a list was a link (10 of 11, the new check red); after, both are links to exactly the address, without the full stop or the bracket, opening in a new tab, the `javascript:` one is text, and the comment reads as written (11 of 11 on lane 4, and again in the regression sweep).

Checks:

### `found-5-oct/calendar-push-ignores-who-may-read` — **closed** (security, medium; found by the triage beside `ledger-rows/row-1962`) · reproduced 5 October as far as a push can go here

**A task is pushed into the Google or Outlook calendar of a connection's owner who may not read it, and after they have left**

*Evidence, reproduced 5 October on lane 7 by the triage's skeptic:* a plain member granted `integrations.manage` through a custom role started the workspace's Google Calendar connection (201, `connectedById` is them). The admin made a private space with a dated task; the member's `GET /tasks/:id` answered 404. With that connection staged without a token (so nothing left the machine), the admin's push of the task answered 201 `{"pushed":[],"skipped":["gcal:No access token for gcal"]}`: the push chose the member's connection for a task they cannot read, and stopped only at the missing token. The admin then removed the member (200, no member row left); the connection stayed "connected", and the push chose it again.

The cause: `calendar-sync.service.ts` `pushTask` loops over every connection and `resolveTaskContext` asks nothing of `connectedById`; `upsertGoogleEvent` sends the title and description; `fireCalendarPush` runs on every task write; `removeMember` leaves the member's connections. The iCal feed was fixed for exactly this (it applies the container rule and resolves only while its owner is a member); the Google and Outlook push does neither. A real Google write could not be made here.

*To close:* push a task only into connections whose owner may read it now, and stop a connection when its owner leaves the workspace; check both in a suite with the store-and-stub harness (no real calendar). Which lists push at all is the Automations feature, `ledger-rows/row-1962`.

*Closed, 6 October* (lane 6). ClickUp's calendar integration belongs to whoever connected it: "The Google Calendar integration is private, and no one else in your Workspace can access your Google Calendar through this integration" (help centre, "Google Calendar integration", through search excerpts). "When you remove someone from your ClickUp Workspace, the person immediately loses access to all Workspace content" ("Remove someone from a Workspace"). Which locations push at all is the unbuilt Automations feature (`ledger-rows/row-1962`) and was not built.

`pushTask` asks `ownerMayRead` of each connection at every push: the route's, and `fireCalendarPush` on every task write. The answer is yes only when:
- the connection's `connected_by_id` is still a member of the task's workspace — the iCal feed's rule (`resolveIcalToken`), asked of a platform admin too;
- and the task read rule (`readableTask`) lets them in, asked with their account's role.

A connection nobody owns is nobody's. A connection whose owner has left keeps its row, status and tokens, as the feed's token does, and takes no task, and no meeting is made in it.

Measured on lane 6 (`probe-calendar-push.mjs`, the triage's route, three runs alike). Every connection was staged without a token, so nothing left the machine.
- Before: a plain member granted `integrations.manage` (OAuth start 201) was refused a private space's task (403 "This space or project is private"). The admin's push of that task answered 201 `{"pushed":[],"skipped":["gcal:No access token for gcal"]}`, so the member's connection was chosen. After the member was removed (200, no member row, the connection still connected), their connection was chosen again for the open task and for the private one.
- After: the private task's push skips nothing (`{"skipped":[]}`); the member's connection is not tried. An open task they may read is tried in their calendar. Once they have left, neither task is tried. The connection is kept, connected.

Checks:
- `calendar-push-reach` is new (3 checks, registered in ci.yml): the private task goes only to the admin's Outlook; an open task goes to both calendars; after the removal, the open task goes to the admin's alone and the connection is kept. On HEAD's product code it scored 1/3; after, 3/3 four times.
- `calendar-sync.service.test.ts` +5 (14 tests).
- `cpr-1`, `cpr-2` and `cpr-3` each redden exactly their check (`cpr-2`'s first draft, with an empty id, answered 400 and was re-aimed). Unit claims `cps-1..5` each redden their test.
- Run on lane 6: `task-rows-by-id` 6/6, `calendar-pull-access` 3/3, `calendar-accounts` 37/37, `private-list-reach` 13/13, `workspace-read-access` 30/30.

For the owner (recorded, not built):
- The Calendar pull still uses a connection whose owner has left, and the integrations list says it is connected and healthy: counted as `found-6-oct/calendar-pull-uses-a-leavers-connection`. How such a connection is shown is open.
- Events already in the calendar of an owner who may no longer read a task, or has left: `deleteEverywhere` still deletes them through that connection when the task loses its date or is binned, and an update now leaves them as they were. Whether to delete them or leave them is open. ClickUp leaves them after a disconnect: "After you delete the integration, tasks synced from ClickUp must be manually removed from your Google Calendar".

*Review fix, 6 October* (lane 6). The task's Google Meet and Zoom buttons (`POST /tasks/:id/meeting`) make the meeting in the workspace's connected Google Calendar or Zoom under the task's title. They asked nothing of whose account that was.
- Measured with `probe-meet-zoom.mjs`. For that probe only, lane 6 ran with `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_API_URL` and `ZOOM_API_URL` at a local stub, then went back to the standard environment. Three runs alike.
- Before: the admin's Google Meet and Zoom on the private space's task the keeper is refused (403) were made with the keeper's tokens and the task's title (201, link stored). After the keeper's removal, the same on a new task.
- Now `createTaskMeeting` asks `CalendarSyncService.ownerMayRead` (shared) of that connection, before its token and before anything is sent.
- After: 400 'The Google Calendar connected to this workspace belongs to somebody who cannot open this task, so no meeting is made in it.' (or 'The Zoom account …'), nothing sent, no link. On a task the keeper may open, still made, 201.
- The task sheet says it in the server's words; it said 'Could not create the meeting'.
- ClickUp's Zoom is a personal connection: 'the data in your external app account will not be available to anyone else through ClickUp' (help centre, 'Connect an app', search excerpts).
- The membership half of `ownerMayRead` is now pinned by an e2e check. A platform admin, plain member of a signed-up owner's workspace with a calendar connected, takes its task while a member and nothing once removed. The read rule alone lets a super_admin in anywhere, and the review's mutant left the suite green.

Checks:
- `calendar-push-reach` 3 → 7: the Meet, Zoom, task sheet (browser) and platform-admin checks. The suite now takes `--dist apps/web/dist` in ci.yml.
- On the builder's product code 4/7: Meet, Zoom and sheet red; the platform-admin check green because it pins the builder's own line, and red with `cpr-7`. After, 7/7 three times.
- `external-links.test.ts` +3.

Patches:
- `cpr-4` (Meet; also the sheet check), `cpr-5` (Zoom), `cpr-6` (the sheet's words, web), `cpr-7` (the membership line alone).
- Re-claimed: `cpr-1` (1, 4, 5, 6), `cpr-2` (2, 4, 5) and `cpr-3` (3, 4, 5, 7).
- Unit claims `els-1..3`.

The comments that said every connected calendar now name the rule.
For the owner, added: a meeting on a task its connection's owner may open is still made in that owner's account, whoever presses. ClickUp makes it in the presser's own personal connection. Not built.
