### `found-13-oct/a-refused-chat-turn-never-ends` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found by batch 40b's break runs) · reproduced 13 October

**A chat turn refused by the hour's AI limit or the month's credits was never answered: a 201, no word, and the composer said Brain was answering until the client gave up**

*Evidence, 13 October:*
- The chat route opens its stream first (`openSseStream`, which hijacks the reply), to report what it reads. Only then does it call `chatStream`, which asked the hour's limits and the month's credits as its first act. A refusal there was thrown to a hijacked reply: no 429 or 402 was sent, no frame was written, and the response was never ended.
- So the request stood on a 201 until its client gave up: five minutes for the suites' fetch, read as "terminated" (`found-13-oct/bcd-stops-where-a-check-should-fail`), and in the composer, Brain answering.
- Lane 2's `ai_usage` shows the cycle: in every run the cap refused, a `chat` refusal, and a second one five minutes later.
- Without a model the route said "AI features are not configured" (503) to a workspace whose credits are spent. `assertAvailable` answers 402 for every other feature, the credits "whatever the server has". The streamed summary's route did the same; with a model it asks before its stream opens, so it was never left open.
- Measured with the checks below, on the lanes' trees before the fix: the chat turn on lane 2 (with a model, `77eb42e`), "201 (left open: The operation was aborted due to timeout)", and on lane 3 (without one, `6848104`), "503 {"error":"AI features are not configured"}"; the streamed summary on lane 3 (at `0e01918`), the same 503.

*Closed, 13 October.* The chat route asks the hour's limits and the month's credits before its stream opens, before the 503, so a refusal is a 429 or a 402 in words, which the composer already shows (`ai.controller.ts`). `chatStream` asks them itself only where it opens its own stream. Past the open, whatever throws is said down the stream, and the stream is ended (`endSseWithError`). The streamed summary asks the credits before its 503 too.
- `ai-credits.mjs`: "and a chat turn is refused the same way, before anything streams and whatever the server has — not left open (402)", and "and so is a summary streamed, whatever the server has (402)". After: 17 of 17 on lane 2 with a model and on lane 3 without one, before the summary's check; with it, 18 of 18 on lane 2 (at `a72c501`, which the summary's change leaves alone with a model) and on lane 3 (at `33f61ce`).
- Unit `chat-trace.test.ts`: refused past the hour's limit, and in a spent workspace, before the reply is hijacked; a read that throws past the open ends the stream with an error frame. On the old route all three failed.
- Patches:
  - `acr-16` (asked inside `chatStream` again): 16 of 17 on lane 2 with a model ("201 data: {"step":"workspace"}") and on lane 3 without one ("503").
  - `acr-17` (asked after the 503) and `acr-18` (the summary's credits asked only where a model answers), each only where no model answers: 17 of 18 on lane 3 at `33f61ce`, each on its own check ("503").
  - `acr-u4` reddened both refusal tests, `acr-u5` the stream's end.
- `acc-11` and `bep-17` anchored on the route's lines as they read before; re-aimed, the refusal and the read they take away are the same. At `7578782`: `acc-11` 32 of 33 on lane 3 without a model (baseline 33 of 33), `bep-17` 19 of 20 on lane 2 with one (baseline 20 of 20), each on the check it names.
- Regression on lane 2 with a model at `33f61ce`, the nine other suites that use the chat or the streamed summary, all green: `brain-comments-and-decks` 29, `ai-answer-rendering` 52, `ai-assign` 24, `ai-create-containers` 33, `ai-task-reads` 4, `brain-entry-points` 20, `private-list-reach` 13, `workspace-read-access` 30 and `video-regression` 94.

### `found-14-oct/agent-performance-carried-and-unbuilt` — **closed** (feature, medium; found reconciling the video-2 ledger) · reproduced 14 October

**My Agent Performance, the Credits tab's table of Super Agents, was carried to Super Agents and closed with them unbuilt**

*Evidence, 14 October:*
- Frame `19:00` draws the Credits Usage tab with **My Agent Performance** under the usage trend: Find agent · Edit benchmark, over a row per agent (`docs/clickup-research.md` §4).
- `commit-log/log-3943965-1` closed the Credits tab on 12 October and sent My Agent Performance to `ledger-rows/row-852` ("it goes with them"). `row-852` took it ("built with them") and closed on 13 October with the hub, the profile and Activity, and no word of it.
- Nothing in the tree draws it: no "Agent Performance" in `apps/web` or `apps/api`, nothing about agents in `ai-credits.tsx`, nothing about credits in `super-agents-hub.tsx`.
- Nor could anything. An agent's model calls are kept in `ai_usage` under the person it acted for (`agent.run`, `super-agents.runner.ts`), with nothing naming the agent or its run, and a run keeps no count of what it did. Neither its cost nor its actions can be told from anybody else's.

*To close:* ClickUp's Agent Performance table, as its help centre has it (through search excerpts, 14 October: "Track your Workspace's Brain AI usage", "How are AI Super Credits consumed?", "Super Agent privacy, security, and permissions"):
- a row per Super Agent with the actions it completed, the time they saved (each action times a per-action time benchmark), the value created (that time at an hourly rate), its cost, its ROI (value ÷ cost, as a multiple) and who made it;
- admins see every agent of the workspace, members the ones they made.

Record each run's credits and completed actions; then draw the table with Find agent and Edit benchmark, with a suite and break patches.

*Closed, 14 October* (lanes 2 and 3), as ClickUp's Agent Performance table has it (help centre through search excerpts, 14 October: "Track your Workspace's Brain AI usage", "How are AI Super Credits consumed?", "Super Agent privacy, security, and permissions"). Built so:
- **An agent's calls are its own.** Each model call of a Super Agent run is written with the run it was made in (`ai_usage.agent_run_id`, migration `0193`), its turn's calls and a refused turn's failure alike. A run keeps the actions of its turn that were carried out (`super_agent_runs.actions_completed`): a task made, a field set, and not one refused or skipped. They are kept even when the run then fails.
- **`GET /workspaces/:id/super-agents/performance`:** this month, a row per Super Agent:
  - its runs, not counting those refused before they began;
  - the actions it completed;
  - its credits, which are its own runs' calls;
  - the time saved, its actions at the minutes one action saves;
  - the value, that time at the hourly rate;
  - the cost, its credits at a tenth of a cent;
  - the return, value over cost, reckoned from the exact cost and none where it cost nothing.
  
  A workspace admin reads every agent of the workspace, a member the ones they made, and a guest is refused in words.
- **Edit benchmark:** the minutes one action saves (`workspaces.ai_minutes_saved_per_agent_action`, a whole number from 0 to 480, 6 until set) beside the hourly rate the value panel uses. A workspace admin sets it on the same route; the value panel's minutes per run stay its own.
- **The Credits tab and Settings → AI usage** draw My Agent Performance under the month's credits (`agent-performance.tsx`, four locales): Find agent, Edit benchmark for an admin, and a row per agent with who made it, its actions, time saved, value, cost and return (×).

Measured:
- Before (`c37c98a`, lane 3): `agent-performance` 0 of 15. The route answered 404, and the run's columns did not exist (`super_agent_runs.actions_completed`).
- After (`3a27eef`): 15 of 15 on lane 3 with no model, and 15 of 15 on lane 2 with one. With a model, a run that made a task counts that action and its calls' credits; without one, the refused run counts as a run that did nothing and cost nothing.
- Beside it at `3a27eef`: `super-agents` 39 of 39, `brain-comments-and-decks` 29 of 29, `ai-connected-apps` 11 of 11, `ai-credits` 18 of 18 and `ai-image-generation` 9 of 9, all with a model; `comment-email` 18 of 18.
- Patches `agp-1` to `agp-15` (the API) and `agp-w1` to `agp-w6` (the web) redden their checks:
  - 20 on lane 3 with no model, at `3a27eef`, each on the check it names and on the checks that stand on what it broke;
  - `agp-9`, which counts only where a model answers, and `agp-8` on lane 2 with a model (baseline 15 of 15).
- `agp-u1` and `agp-u2` redden their unit tests in `ai-value.test.ts`, which has six new tests: 17 of 17.
- Also green at batch 44: `ai-action-categories` 29, `ai-activity-filters` 34, `ai-button-relationship-fields` 17 and `ai-value` 23.

### `found-14-oct/clickup-workspace-import-and-people-unbuilt` — **closed** (feature, large; found reviewing what moving a team off ClickUp needs) · reproduced 14 October

**A team moving off ClickUp brings its work but not its people: nobody is invited, and a whole Workspace cannot be read at once**

*Evidence, 14 October:*
- The ClickUp tab imports ClickUp's CSV export, and reads its tasks' comments and files over the API when a token is given (`clickup-import.service.ts`). A person its rows name comes in only as a member already here: `applyAssigneesTagsFields` skips anybody else (`if (!uid) continue`), and nothing invites them.
- The Spreadsheet importer of `found-14-oct/imports-exports-branch-unmerged` invites the addresses a sheet names, but a person invited there is never put on the tasks they were named on ("assign them once they have joined"), and ClickUp's export names people by name, not address.
- Nothing reads a ClickUp Workspace as ClickUp holds it: its Spaces, Folders and Lists, each List's statuses, its members and their roles.

*To close:* as ClickUp's own importers work (help centre and developer docs through search excerpts, 14 October: "Import mapping … matching imported email addresses to users who have been invited"; a Workspace's members and their roles from `GET /team`, `role` 1 owner, 2 admin, 3 member, 4 guest; tasks 100 a page from page 0 until `last_page`, closed tasks and subtasks only when asked for):
- sign in to ClickUp by its personal API token and read a Workspace's Spaces whole over API v2;
- match its people to members by email, and invite the ones who are not here with ClickUp's role for them, by somebody who may invite, at no role above their own;
- hold their tasks for them and make them theirs when they accept, where the assignee route would put them on them.

*Closed, 14 October* (batch 45, `cdc5e44`, and what measuring it found):
- **Signed in by its token.** The ClickUp tab takes a personal API token ("Settings › Apps"), asks ClickUp whose it is, and keeps it sealed for the person who pasted it (`import_grants`, provider `clickup`). A token ClickUp refuses is said in the form, and nothing is kept.
- **Read whole** over API v2 (`clickup.ts`): a Workspace's Spaces, each with its Folders and Lists, and each List with its statuses (the List's own, else its Folder's, else its Space's), in ClickUp's order. Tasks are read 100 a page until `last_page`, closed ones and subtasks asked for. A subtask comes in under its task (one level here). A task keeps its description, dates, priority, estimate, tags, checklists, Custom Fields, comments (25 a page, newest first, each page asked from the oldest of the last), files, and links and dependencies as related tasks.
- **Its people.** Each is matched to a member by email. Anyone who is not here is offered an invitation with their ClickUp role (1 and 2 an admin, 3 a member, 4 a guest), and "Invite everyone who is not here" sets them all. The invitations go out as `POST /invitations` sends them: only by somebody with `members.invite`, at no role above their own, never twice to an address with one open. The tasks of the people invited are held for them (`import_pending_assignees`, migration `0195`) and become theirs when they accept, where the assignee route would put them on them. A guest is put on nothing that is not shared with them.
- **Found measuring it:**
  - the lanes' databases kept `import_grants`' old provider check, which `drizzle-kit push` does not rewrite, so a ClickUp sign-in failed on a constraint. 0195's check is applied to every lane, as `0191` and `0192` were; production's `migrate` applies it, and CI starts from an empty database;
  - the suite read a checklist column that does not exist (`is_completed`);
  - the suite looked for the invitation's token in a text part the email does not have.

Measured:
- `clickup-workspace-import` 14 of 14 on lane 3 at `83a6bc1`, 20 of 20 with batch 47 at `6efcf8c` and again at `93890fd`. `clickup.test.ts`: 7 unit tests, of 15 since batch 47.
- Patches `cwi-1` to `cwi-16`, 16 at `6efcf8c` on lane 3, baseline 20 of 20: each reddens a check it names. `cwi-9` was re-aimed at the claim's held-tasks line inside its block.
- Beside it: `importers-by-sign-in` 26 of 26 at `2f2a0bb`, and `isi-w2`, re-aimed at the wizard's people choice, reddens the check it names; `importers` 25 of 25 and `imports` 60 of 60 at `b2eed3f`.

### `found-14-oct/lane-tooling-misses-the-imports-package` — **closed** (harness, medium; found integrating `found-14-oct/imports-exports-branch-unmerged`) · reproduced 14 October

**The lanes and the worktree linker do not know `packages/imports`, so a change to it is served stale**

### `found-14-oct/automation-conditions-and-actions-unbuilt` — **closed** (feature, medium; found comparing the automations of the prototype in pull request #2 with the branch's) · reproduced 14 October

**An automation cannot ask anything of the task it runs on, and cannot comment, add a watcher, set a due date, fill an AI field or be tested**

*Evidence, 14 October:*
- A rule's trigger takes filters on the event — a project, a list, the field that changed, the status moved from or to (`AutomationsService.fire`) — and nothing of the task: "only if the priority is Urgent", "only if it has the tag Client" cannot be said. Whatever the event, every matching rule runs.
- Its actions are seven: change the status, set the priority, notify, make a subtask, assign, post to a channel, run a Super Agent. ClickUp's automations also add a comment, add a watcher, change the due date and fill AI fields.
- A rule cannot be tried on a task without running it, and a run that did nothing is not logged at all.
- The automations prototype brought in by pull request #2 (`Rundesk-task-timesheet-admin/lib/automation`) has all of these: conditions on a task's status, priority, assignee, list, tags, due date and title with eq/neq/in/not_in/is_empty/contains/lt/gt, all or any, at most fifteen; `add_comment`, `add_follower`, `set_due_date`, `update_ai_field`; and an event test console.

*To close:* as ClickUp's automations work (conditions "only if…" on a trigger, all or any; the actions above; a test of a rule on a task):
- conditions on a rule's trigger, read from the task as it is when the event fires, refused in words when they cannot be read, and a skipped run logged with each condition's verdict;
- the four actions, a watcher only somebody who may open the task, the comment under the rule's maker;
- a test that says what a rule would do to a task and does nothing;
- the builder's conditions, the actions' pickers, the test on a rule's card, a skipped run in its history.

*Closed, 14 October* (batch 46, `fe5ff16`, and what measuring it found), as the prototype of pull request #2 has them and ClickUp's automations work:
- **Conditions** (`automation-conditions.ts`): a rule's trigger keeps up to fifteen — a task's status, priority, assignee, List, tag, due date or title, each with the operators it takes (is, is not, any of, none of, is set, is not set, contains, before, after) — and acts when all hold, or any one, as it says. They are read from the task as it is when the event fires, and refused in words when they cannot be read. A run that did not act is logged as skipped, with each condition's verdict.
- **Four actions:** add a comment (its `{{task.title}}` filled in, under the rule's maker); add a watcher (only somebody who may open the task); set the due date some days out; fill an AI field (only an AI field).
- **A test** (`POST /workspaces/:id/automations/:id/test`, `automation.manage`): what a rule would do to a task, its conditions' verdicts and its actions, done to nothing and logged nowhere.
- **The builder's** conditions with "all of these" or "any of these", the actions' pickers, the test on a rule's card, and a skipped run in its history, in four locales; two recipes that use them.

Found measuring it, and fixed before it was closed:
- the API did not start (`fe5ff16`): a static import of the AI fields' service closed a module cycle (tasks → automations → AI fields → AI → tasks), and Nest read the AI service's tasks parameter as undefined. It is loaded where the action runs (`fef3efa`);
- testing a rule from its card sent search's name for the hit (`task-<id>`) as the task's id, and every test from the page failed with "A value has an invalid format" (`281a101`);
- the suite's own fixtures: its tag made without the colour the labels route asks; the built rule read by a query the API's rules also match; jsonb's reordered keys compared as text; the card found by a class the page layout shares (`9839fd8`, `e05f725`, `83a6bc1`). The card, its expand button and the builder's name field have test ids now.

Measured:
- `automation-conditions` 9 of 9 on lane 4 at `281a101` and again at `ec66732`. Its unit file, `automation-conditions.test.ts`, 5 of 5.
- Patches `acn-1` to `acn-10` (the API) and `acn-w1` to `acn-w4` (the web), 14 at `ec66732` on lane 4, baseline 9 of 9: each reddens a check it names (`break-report.sh`: 14 reddened). `acn-1`, conditions ignored, is the rule as it stood before: 6 of 9.

- a People field as its people's names, a Task or Relationship field as its tasks', a Formula as its value.

*Closed, 14 October* (batch 47, `ec66732`, and `6efcf8c`), as the item's "To close" says, each of the three a choice on the import page:
- **Docs** (`clickup.ts`, API v3): a Doc in the Space, one of its Folders or one of its Lists comes into the Space (`DocsService.importPageTree`, as Notion's pages come in). Its first page is the Doc's own body, and the Doc's other pages, and their pages, nest under it as ClickUp nests them. The Workspace's own Docs come in, beside the workspace's other Docs, only when asked. A Doc that cannot be read or made is said, and the others come in.
- **Tracked time:** read once a Space (`space_id`), everyone's by `assignee`, 50 people an ask. Each entry comes in as a time entry under whoever tracked it, billable as it was, marked as the run's (`time_entries.import_id`). An entry of somebody the run invited is held by their address (`import_pending_time_entries`, migration `0196`) and is theirs when they accept, on a task the assignee route would put them on. A running timer is not time. A token that may not read others' time brings its owner's own, and the run says so.
- **Goals:** read once a run, those in Goal Folders too, each whole for its Targets. Each comes in with its owner mapped, as a percentage from its Targets (or as ClickUp says it), done at a hundred. Each Target counts from nothing to its target: a number, currency or percentage from its start to its end, down as well as up; true/false as one to do; a tasks Target as its tasks done of its tasks.
- **Fields:** a People field comes in as its people's names, a Task or Relationship field as its tasks', a Formula as its value.
- **The report** says the pages of Docs, the time entries made and held, and the Goals. The run's "not imported" names what is left: Whiteboards, Chat, Dashboards and views; reminders, and Goal Folders (their Goals come in); files in Custom Fields.

Measured:
- `clickup-workspace-import` 20 of 20 on lane 3 at `6efcf8c` and `93890fd`: six checks are new, and the Custom Fields check now reads the People field.
- `clickup.test.ts` 15 of 15: eight new unit tests.
- Patches `cwi-17` to `cwi-30` and `cwi-w1`: 15 on lane 3 at `6efcf8c`, baseline 20 of 20, each reddens a check it names. `cwi-20` did not build there (TypeScript drops a branch's narrowing on `&& false`, as `cem-2` found); re-aimed, it reddens its three checks at `93890fd`.

*Found measuring it, 14 October:* a Space imported a third time into the Space chosen before failed whole — "duplicate key value violates unique constraint `uq_lists_project_name_active`" — as its List in no Folder had the name of the one the first run made there. A List now comes in beside it as "Inbox (2)", the name a person making it would be asked to change it to.

### `found-14-oct/clickup-chat-unimported` — **closed** (feature, medium; found closing `found-14-oct/clickup-docs-time-goals-unimported`; built at the owner's word, 14 October: "sure do it") · reproduced 14 October

**A ClickUp Workspace comes over without its Chat**

*Evidence, 14 October:* the token import's run says "Whiteboards, Chat, Dashboards and views" stay behind (`CLICKUP.notImported`), and nothing reads ClickUp's Chat: a team's channels and their history are left in ClickUp. Rundesk imports Slack's channels into Chat (`SlackImportService`), and ClickUp's not at all.

*To close:* as ClickUp's v3 Chat API answers — which ClickUp calls experimental, so its shape is read first, read only, through the owner's own ClickUp account, with their leave — each channel (not a direct message, as the Slack import leaves those) a Chat channel here: private when it was, with its people; every page of its messages, each at its moment and under its author when they are a member here, else drawn under their name; a thread's replies in its thread; a mention of a member a mention of them. A choice on the import page, on unless turned off.

*Closed, 14 October* (batch 48, `dd78db8`):
- **Its shape, read first:** with the owner's leave, ClickUp's Chat was read through their own ClickUp account, read only and for its shape alone, nothing of what it said kept or copied. A channel is `id`, `name`, `type` (`CHANNEL`, or a direct message's) and `visibility`. A message is `id`, `content` in Markdown (a mention `[@Name](#user_mention#<id>)`, a group's `#user_group_mention#`), `user_id` (`-1` for ClickUp's own posts), `date` in milliseconds and `has_replies`. Messages and a thread's replies come newest first, a page at a time by `next_cursor`, and a message may have no text (a file).
- **The reader** (`clickup.ts`, v3): the Workspace's channels, its messages (the newest 10 000 a channel, as the Slack import takes), each thread's replies, and its members where ClickUp says them. It takes the API's own pages (`data`) and the connector's named ones, and skips a direct message. A channel that cannot be read is said, and the others come in.
- **The writer** (`TreeWriter.writeChat`), as the Slack import writes a channel:
  - a channel takes its own name, or with `-clickup` after it when the workspace has that name, and is private when it was, archived when it was;
  - its members are the importer and every member here it had or heard from;
  - each message keeps its moment and its author when they are a member here, else it goes under the importer, drawn with the name it was written under (`imported_author`);
  - a reply is in its thread, and a mention of a member here is a mention of them, of anyone else their name;
  - a message with no text says it held a file left in ClickUp. A run that fails takes its channels away.
- **The import page** offers Chat on the ClickUp tab, on unless turned off, and the report says the messages. The run's "not imported" now names direct messages, and files and reactions in Chat.

Measured:
- `clickup-workspace-import` 22 of 22 on lane 3 at `dd78db8` and `d91b749`. Two checks are new: the Chat that comes over, read in its rows (a public channel of seven messages over three of the stub's pages with a thread of two replies, a private channel, a direct message that stays behind); and Chat turned off, neither read nor made.
- `clickup.test.ts` 18 of 18: three new unit tests.
- Patches `cwi-31` to `cwi-38` and `cwi-w2`, 9 on lane 3 at `d91b749`, baseline 22 of 22: each reddens the check it names.

*Found building it:* a Workspace's import asks ClickUp a request or two per task, and ClickUp gives a token 100 requests a minute on most plans (1 000 on Business Plus, 10 000 on Enterprise; developer docs, "Rate Limits", through search excerpts). It says how many are left and when the window starts again (`X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, a Unix time). A token run past that has been reported shut out for hours. The importers' client waited a 429 a second at most ten, three times, and failed the task's comments and files after that.
- **Fixed** (`a90d5a6`, `app-http.ts`): once a tool says its window is spent, the next request waits for the reset. A 429 with no `Retry-After` is waited out until the reset, a minute at most a wait, five times.
- **Measured:** `app-import.test.ts` 12 of 12, with two new tests. `cwi-u1` (the window ignored), `cwi-u2` (a 429 waited a moment) and the re-aimed `isi-u9` each redden their test. The re-aimed `isi-29` reddens its check on lane 4 at `a90d5a6`, where `importers-by-sign-in` is 26 of 26 and `clickup-workspace-import` 22 of 22.

### `found-21-oct/timeline-same-dated-rows-swap` — **closed** (product, small; found by rehearsal 22) · reproduced 21 October

**The workspace timeline drew tasks of the same dates in no fixed order, so a read again could swap two rows under the pointer**

*Evidence, 21 October:* rehearsal 22 at `1b3c4a4`, the only failure of its 400 steps (verify 81, browser 6, postgres 313): "Timeline drags move whole days and keep the time", 16 of 17, "the member's shared task {"mayEdit":"true","handles":2}, dragged true: {"start":"2026-10-07T09:00:00.000Z",…} → {"start":"2026-10-07T09:00:00.000Z",…}". The API sent no "was updated" mail for that task, as it does when the member's change is saved, so no change reached it. The suite passed 6 of 6 alone and 6 of 6 after the job's first 94 steps, so it was traced there instead (every mousedown, PATCH and timeline read):
- `getTimelineForWorkspace` ordered by start and due date alone. The member's view-only task and the task shared with them have the same dates.
- They were drawn in one order on one run and the other on the next, and swapped between the first read and the read again that the refused drag of the binned task makes.
- A bar measured before that read is drawn and pressed after it is pressed where the other row now is: the view-only bar, which moves nothing.

*Closed, 21 October:*
- `1ea455e`: the read orders by when each task was made, then its id, so a read again draws each row where it was.
- `0a98704` and `1ea455e`: the suite measures the shared bar once the refusal's read has taken the binned bar away, so it is measured where it is drawn.
- Measured on the rehearsal's checkout, with the refusal's read held and the two rows swapped in it:
  - drawn between the shared bar's box and the press, with no wait (A): rehearsal 22's failure, word for word, the press on the view-only bar (`data-may-edit` false), no PATCH sent;
  - drawn a second later, with the wait (B, B2): 17 of 17.
- No patch is aimed at the order: putting the old order back fails the check only when Postgres's sort swaps the two rows, which no run can make it do.

### `found-22-oct/deploy-stops-at-the-r2-check` — **closed** (deploy, small; found by the first production deploy of `196bf45`) · reproduced 22 October

**`deploy.sh rebuild` ended silently at its R2 check whenever there was nothing to warn about**

*Evidence, 22 October:* the owner's deploy of `196bf45` built and published the web app, rebuilt and restarted the API, applied every migration and reloaded nginx, and then stopped without "✓ Rebuild complete.". The owner's deploy script (`docs/resume-2026-10-13.md` §3) read the exit status and printed its rollback steps. `warn_if_public_domain_on_private_bucket` (batch 51, `09bd80d`) reads the API's log with `line=$(docker logs … | grep -E "…" | tail -1)`. Under the script's `set -euo pipefail` the grep that finds nothing, the usual case, fails the assignment, and the script exits 1 there, saying nothing. Its test ran the function without those options, so it passed.

*Closed, 22 October:*
- `deploy.sh`: the pipeline ends `|| true`.
- `test/deploy/public-domain-warning.test.sh` runs the function under `set -euo pipefail` and requires the rebuild to go on after it: 3 of 5 against the old line (the two cases with nothing to say), 5 of 5 after.
- No other `$(… | grep …)` in `deploy.sh` or `deploy/lib` is without `|| true`.
- The wait in the same check, for the API to say it has started, ran its whole minute on every deploy: `docker logs | grep -q` stopped reading at the first match, and under pipefail the broken pipe failed the line. Measured on a 4.6 MB log, 30 rounds of 2 s. The log is now read once a round and searched as a string; the test's new case, a long log that says the API started, waits 30 rounds against the old lines and none now (6 of 6). Seen in the owner's verified deploy of `2051a24b`, which paused a minute there.

## Closed from the uncounted list, as ClickUp works them (8 to 14 October) — 49

On the owner's word of 8 October ("close all of these properly … close them as they work on clickup"), the
items the triage set aside as features and decisions are closed one by one: as ClickUp works each where its
sources say how, and as Rundesk already works where they are silent. Each moves here from the last section with
its evidence, is reproduced on a lane before it is changed, and is counted as closed.

### `found-6-oct/task-writes-answer-a-refusal-as-not-found` — **closed** (decision, small; found closing `found-5-oct/super-admin-cannot-write-a-task-it-reads`; was not counted, a decision for the owner) · reproduced 8 October

**A task its caller may not open answers 403 with its reason when read, and 404 "Task not found" when changed or moved**

*Measured, 6 October, lane 6:* a plain member's `GET` of a private space's task answered 403 "This space or project is private", and their `PATCH` of it 404 "Task not found". `PATCH /tasks/:id` and `POST /tasks/:id/move` carry no `ResourceMemberGuard`, and the write rule answers a task its caller may not read as not found; this predates the owner's decision of 1 October, which named reads (403 with the reason, for tasks, lists, projects and spaces). Whether writes follow it is the owner's to say. If they do: the write rule answers 403 with the read rule's reason for a task the caller may not open, and 404 for an id naming nothing, paired in a suite. `super-admin-task-writes` takes 403 or 404 with nothing changed, so it pins neither.

*Closed, 8 October* (lane 3), on the owner's word of 8 October to close the uncounted items as ClickUp works them. ClickUp's sources say nothing of what a refused change answers; Rundesk's own rule, the owner's of 1 October, answers a read its caller may not make 403 with the reason, and a change or a move of the same task is refused in the same words now. The write rule (`assertTaskWritable`, `common/permissions/task-write.ts`) asks the read rule's answer (`taskReadAnswer`, `read-access.ts`): a task its caller may not open is 403 in the guard's sentence ("This task is private", "This list is private", "This space or project is private", "This is not shared with you"); somebody of another workspace is 403 "You are not a member of this workspace", where they were told "Workspace not found"; and an id naming nothing is still 404 "Task not found".

Measured on lane 3 with `refused-as-forbidden`'s new section 13: a member's change of a private task, of one in a private list and of one in a private space, and their move of the last; a guest's change of a task not shared with them; a stranger's.
- Before (the API before the change): each 404 "Task not found", the stranger's "Workspace not found"; 12 of 15, with sections 14 and 15 (below).
- After: each 403 in its refusal's words, nothing changed (SQL), and a change of an id naming nothing 404; 15 of 15.

Checks:
- `refused-as-forbidden` 12 → 15 (this and the two below): "a change or a move of a task its caller may not open is refused 403 in the read’s words — a private task, list or space, a guest’s, a stranger’s — and nothing changes (SQL); a change of an id naming nothing is 404".
- Patches `raf-13` (a refused change is 404 again) and `raf-14` (a stranger's is "Workspace not found" again) redden it: 14 and 13 of 15 on lane 3.
- The patches written on the write rule's old lines (`tel-2`, `gte-1`, `gte-2`, `saw-1`–`saw-3`, `tws-1`–`tws-4`) are re-aimed at the new ones; each still reddens its check on lane 3 (`tel-2` 4 of 5, `gte-1` 1 of 6, `gte-2` 5 of 6, `saw-1` 3 of 7, `saw-2` and `saw-3` 6 of 7; `tws-1`–`tws-4` are unit claims, read by the preflight). `guest-task-edits` reads a guest's change of a task not shared with them as 403 "This is not shared with you" now, as its read is refused, and the write rule's unit test a member's change in a private list as 403 "This list is private".

### `found-6-oct/super-admin-outside-makes-what-it-cannot-change` — **closed** (security, small; found closing `found-5-oct/super-admin-cannot-write-a-task-it-reads`; was not counted, a decision for the owner) · reproduced 8 October

**A platform super_admin who is no member of a workspace makes a task there and is refused changing it**

*Measured, 6 October, lane 6:* `admin@rundesk.internal`, with no member row in a signed-up owner's workspace, made a task in its list (`POST /tasks` 201) and opened it (200); `PATCH` of it answered 404 "Workspace not found". The create gate lets a super_admin who is no member through (the read rule by the account's role; `resolveSpaceLevel` answers nothing for a non-member), and the write rule asks membership. An import by such an account passes the importers' guest rule, and its merge answers the same 404. ClickUp has no platform-wide role to compare with. Whether a platform admin outside a workspace may make there, change there, or neither, is the owner's, beside whether a platform admin reaches private locations at all (recorded on `found-5-oct/super-admin-cannot-write-a-task-it-reads`); either way the create gate and the write rule should agree.

*Closed, 8 October* (lane 3). ClickUp has no platform-wide role: a Workspace's owner and admins act in their own Workspace, and its tasks are made by somebody of it. So a platform super_admin who is no member of a workspace neither makes nor changes anything there, and the gates agree:
- the create gate (`assertCanCreateTaskIn`) asks them to be a member of the list's workspace, as the write rule already did;
- the importers (`assertMayImport`) ask it too: they asked only whether the member row they found was a guest's, so a platform admin with no row there imported a project and its tasks;
- each refuses 403 "You are not a member of this workspace", in the write rule's words.

Reading there stays as it was (the read rule, by the account's role). Whether a platform admin reaches private locations at all stays where `found-5-oct/super-admin-cannot-write-a-task-it-reads` recorded it.

Measured on lane 3 with `refused-as-forbidden`'s section 15: the platform's admin, with no member row in a workspace a signed-up user made.
- Before: it made a task there (201, a row written) and was refused changing it, 404 "Workspace not found"; with the create gate closed, an import there was still taken (201, and its job wrote a project there).
- After: made 403, imported 403 (no job row, no project), changed 403, each "You are not a member of this workspace", nothing written; read 200.

Checks:
- `refused-as-forbidden`: "the platform’s admin, no member of a workspace, makes no task there, imports nothing and changes none, each refused 403 “You are not a member of this workspace” with nothing written (SQL) — as before, it may read there".
- Patches `raf-16` (the create gate asks no membership of the platform admin), `raf-17` (nor do the importers) and `raf-14` redden it: 14, 14 and 13 of 15 on lane 3.
- Unit: `import-access.test.ts` "a platform admin who is no member is refused 403 …" (patch `raf-18-…-unit`), and `task-create.test.ts` "refuses a platform super_admin who is no member of the list’s workspace …" (patch `raf-19-…-unit`).

### `found-6-oct/doc-refusals-answer-not-found` — **closed** (decision, small; found reviewing `found-6-oct/an-open-socket-outlives-its-access`; was not counted, a decision for the owner) · reproduced 8 October

**A doc the caller may not open answers 404 "Doc not found", where the owner's rule of 1 October answers 403 with the reason for tasks, lists, projects and spaces**

*Measured, 6 October, lane 2:* a member removed from the workspace, reading the doc they wrote, got 404 "Doc not found". `DocsService.assertDocAccess` answers not-found both to a non-member and to a member a private space refuses ("Not found either way"), since `db1416d` (24 September). If they do: 403 with the reason for a doc the caller may not open, 404 for an id naming nothing, paired in a suite.

*Closed, 8 October* (lane 3). As tasks, lists, projects and spaces are by the owner's rule of 1 October, a doc its caller may not open is refused 403 in the guard's own sentence (`READ_REFUSALS`): somebody of another workspace "You are not a member of this workspace", a guest it is not shared with "This is not shared with you", a member refused the private space it lives in "This space or project is private". An id naming nothing is still 404 "Doc not found". `DocsService.assertDocAccess` is every doc route's one door, so reads, edits, comments, exports, shares and revisions answer alike; and a task's link to a doc its caller may not open (`TasksService.linkDoc`), refused 404 for the same reason, is refused in the door's words too.

Measured on lane 3 with `refused-as-forbidden`'s new section 14: a member's read and change of a doc in a private space; a guest's read of an open space's doc; a stranger's.
- Before: each 404 "Doc not found".
- After: each 403 in its words, the doc unchanged (SQL), an id naming nothing 404, and the member's open doc and the admin's read 200.

Checks:
- `refused-as-forbidden`: "a doc its caller may not open is refused 403 in the read’s words — read or changed by a member refused its space, a guest’s, a stranger’s — and is not changed (SQL); an id naming nothing is 404, and the open doc and the admin’s are read".
- Patch `raf-15` (the door answers "Doc not found" again) reddens it, 14 of 15.
- `workspace-read-access`'s doc checks read the refusal in its words now: "a member cannot open a doc of a space they are refused, nor the page under it (403 “This space or project is private”) — …", "a member cannot edit, comment on, export or template a doc they may not open (403 … each, …)" and "… and linking one is refused (403 “This space or project is private”, no link) — the admin’s name it". Their patches still redden them (`wra-41` 28 of 30, `wra-44` 27, `wra-45` and `wra-51` 29, `wra-48` 29 and `wra-49` 29 of 30, the last re-aimed at the link's new lines).

### `found-30-sep/template-leaves-values-out-silently` — **closed** (visible bug, small; found closing `found-30-sep/template-values-written-unchecked`; was not counted, a decision for the owner) · reproduced 8 October

**A template applied where a field refuses its value leaves that field unset, and nothing says so**

*Evidence, 30 September:* `instantiate` now writes only what each field's route would take and leaves out the rest (words into a Number field, an option a Dropdown lacks). Its answer does not say which were left out, and the create modal's toast says only that the task was made. ClickUp's help centre has nothing on a template's value that its target field refuses.

*To close:* the owner decides whether the person is told. If so, the answer names the fields left out and the modal says so, in four locales; check it with a template applied where a field refuses its value.

### `found-25-sep/view-only-individual-permissions` — **closed** (parity, medium; found closing `guest-guard-reads-the-account-role`; was not counted, a feature) · reproduced 8 October

**ClickUp's four individual permissions for view-only members and guests are not built**

ClickUp (help centre, "Manage individual permissions for view only users", search snippets): view-only members and guests have four individual permissions.
- On by default: time estimates and time tracking.
- Off by default: adding or removing tags, and creating views.
- An owner or admin turns each on or off per person, on the Unlimited plan and above.

Here:
- Time tracking follows reading, with no switch.
- A time estimate asks the task's write rule, so a view-only member cannot set one where ClickUp's default lets them.
- Tags ask the write rule, which matches ClickUp's default.
- Making views is not measured.

*To close:*

- the task's capabilities carry `estimate`, `tags` and `track`, and the list's `privateViews`: the sheet offers the estimate, the tags and the timer and manual entry only as they allow, saying where time tracking is off, and the list page's + View makes a view of one's own where only that is allowed;
- the People tab offers each member's and guest's four switches, as a popover on their row, to those who may change roles (none on a manager's row). Four locales.
`view-writes-by-level` turns Create views on for its view-only member and guest while it measures their own views, and off again for its page.

### `ledger-rows/row-1962` — **closed** (feature, medium; was not counted, a feature) · reproduced 8 October

**Calendar Automations (which tasks sync, to which calendar) — held by §3 parking, which is a 'walkthrough never explains' reason**

*Evidence:* reaudit.md:1962-1991 (P, 'contested' against §3). planner-settings-dialog.tsx:66-73 parks Automations because 'the explanation was never given'. Yet frame 14:32 draws the page: the 'Sync ClickUp tasks to Google Calendar' card, the empty state 'Pick a list, folder, or space…' and '+ Add sync'. calendar-sync.service.ts:71-101: pushTask sends every due-dated, non-archived task to every connection, with no scope table and no off switch.

*To close:* Research ClickUp's Calendar Automations. Add a sync-rule table (scope = list/folder/space, target calendar), make pushTask read it, and add the Automations settings page. The default becomes 'nothing is syncing', as the frame shows.

*Triage, 5 October:* a feature, not a defect (confirmed unbuilt). Calendar Automations is not built: there is no sync-rule storage and no settings page, and on lane 4 every task with a due date is pushed to every calendar connection in its workspace, whatever list it is in. The triage's skeptic reproduced a defect beside it, now counted as `found-5-oct/calendar-push-ignores-who-may-read`. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*Closed, 8 October* (lane 7), on the owner's word of 8 October. ClickUp's help centre ("Google Calendar integration", through search excerpts, 8 October): "Sync tasks to calendar" draws tasks from a Space, Folder, Subfolder or List into a calendar of one's own — tasks cannot be synced to a shared calendar, and nobody else in a workspace reaches a person's calendar through the integration — all the tasks there or only those assigned to you; a task needs a start or a due date to be on the calendar, a date with no time is a day's event, a due date alone begins an hour before it, and the sync runs one way. Frame `14:32` draws the planner's Automations page: "Sync ClickUp tasks to Google Calendar", "Pick a list, folder, or space…", "+ Add sync". Built so:
- a person's syncs (`calendar_sync_rules`, migration `0178_calendar_sync_rules`): a space, folder, project or list they may open, one of their own connected calendars (`user_calendar_accounts`), and all the tasks there or only theirs. `GET`/`POST /workspaces/:id/calendar-sync/rules`, `DELETE …/rules/:ruleId`, and `GET …/places`: the spaces, folders, projects and lists they may open, in the sidebar's order, which the page offers and a new sync is checked against. A place they may not open is refused 403, saying so; one that is not there is 404; a colleague's calendar is not found; the same place twice to one calendar is 409; and each person is shown their own syncs alone;
- the push (`CalendarSyncRulesService.syncTask`, behind `CalendarSyncService.pushTask`): a task goes to the calendar of every sync of its list, project, folder or space whose owner may open it now — the read rule and the membership, asked at every push (`calendar-owner.ts`, the one statement of it, which a task's Google Meet and Zoom still ask) — and, where the sync takes only its owner's tasks, to whom it is assigned. Its event is the task's name, its description as text with the way back to the task, at ClickUp's times; the event it became (`calendar_sync_events`) is changed rather than written twice, and nothing is written when nothing it shows has changed. It comes off when the task is archived, its dates are cleared, it is moved out, unassigned from a sync of only its owner's, no longer its owner's to open — their access gone, or they have left — or the sync is removed. A new sync writes the tasks already there; one calendar's writes go one at a time;
- every task write that changes an event pushes it: a task made with a start or due date; a change of its name, description, dates or their times, of whether it is archived, or of its list; a move; an assignment either way; a restore, from Archived or from the Trash;
- NOTHING SYNCS UNTIL A SYNC IS ADDED. The workspace's connected calendars take no task: every dated task of the workspace was written into every one of them, with no table saying where and no switch to stop it. The App Center's calendar panel says where tasks are synced now (four locales);
- the planner's settings have the Automations page (`planner-sync-page.tsx`, `/calendar?settings=automations`): the syncs, each naming its place, its calendar and which tasks, with Remove; + Add sync, with the place, the calendar and All tasks or Only tasks assigned to me; and with no calendar connected, the way to Accounts. Four locales.

Measured on lane 7:
- Before (batch 21's build): `calendar-sync-rules` 0 of 12 — the routes answered 404, and the push wrote to the workspace's connected Google Calendar ("gcal:No access token for gcal") — `calendar-push-reach` 0 of 10 (its pushes stage syncs now, and there was no table for them), `planner-settings` 18 of 20 (the nav's six pages, and their order).
- After: 12 of 12, 10 of 10 and 20 of 20; beside them, all passing: connected-calendars 11, calendar-accounts 37, calendar-pull-access 3, meetings-connect-calendar 6, personal-calendar-connect 6, planner-blocks 19, people-calendar-access 8, planner-upcoming-meeting 8, rail-reorder 13, planner-onboarding 12, trash-rules 4.

Checks (`calendar-sync-rules`, 12): "nothing syncs until a sync is added: …", "the member adds a sync of a folder on the Automations page — …", "the tasks already in the folder are written to that calendar once the sync is made: …", "a task made there afterwards with a due day and no time is that day’s event", "renaming a task and moving its due time changes its event — …", "a task in a place no sync holds is not written; …", "a task whose due date is cleared comes off the calendar, and so does an archived one", "a sync of only the tasks assigned to its owner takes a task once they are assigned it, and gives it up when they are not", "a sync takes only what its owner may open: …", "a place the member may not open is refused, saying so — …", "removing the sync on the page takes its events off the calendar, …", "once the member has left the workspace their sync writes nothing more — …". `calendar-push-reach`'s four push checks stage a sync for the keeper and one for the admin and ask the same rule of each; `planner-settings` "the nav offers exactly the six pages that do something", and their order with Automations last. Unit: `calendar-sync-rules.service.test.ts`, 15 (when an event is, what it shows, which calendars a task goes to); `calendar-sync.service.test.ts`'s push test asks the syncs.
- Patches `csr-1` to `csr-15` (the API), `csr-w1` to `csr-w5` (the web) and the unit claims `csr-16` and `csr-17` redden their checks: 10, 10, 11, 10, 11, 11, 11, 7, 11, 10, 10, 10, 10, 11 and 11 of 12 on lane 1, and 2, 3, 6, 10 and 11 of 12 on lane 2; the unit claims redden their tests; `cpr-1`, `cpr-2`, `cpr-3` and `cpr-7` re-aimed at `calendar-owner.ts` and at the push checks' new words, 6, 7, 6 and 9 of 10; `planner-settings-1` at the nav's six, 18 of 20.

### `resume-defects/s4-clip-link` — **closed** (feature, large; was not counted, a feature) · reproduced 8 October

**Section 4: 'A pasted clip link renders as the clip' is still unbuilt. There is no clips table, no per-clip route and no paste handling**

*Evidence:* No clips table: I grepped packages/db/src/schema for a pgTable named with 'clip', and packages/db/src/migrations for CREATE TABLE with clip, and found nothing. A clip is a storage object. clips.service.ts:21-23 builds the prefix `workspaces/<id>/clips/`, :37 builds the key, and :50-80 lists the clips by listing storage objects, using the storage key as `id` and title and duration from object metadata. The routes are only the library /app/$workspaceId/clips (routeTree.gen.ts:419-423, 591); there is no per-clip route. For paste handling, the comment composer has no onPaste or unfurl: grep of apps/web/src finds unfurl only in chat (chat-message-body.tsx:124-169, 315-328), which unfurls task URLs and OG metadata, not clips. Copy link signs the storage object (clip-publish.ts:111-117), so a pasted link carries no clip identity and no title. The ledger entry is docs/video2-reaudit.md:1307-1330 (status M), with the row at 1532. ClickUp research: clip URLs are stable, unguessable public links (see resume-7).

*To close:* The order is forced. First, a `clips` table (id, workspace_id, storage_key unique, title, duration_seconds, created_by, share_token, created_at), backfilled from the existing storage prefix, with list() reading the table. Second, a stable app route that resolves a token to a freshly signed playback URL, shared with resume-7. Third, paste handling in the comment composer (and chat) that recognises the route, stores a clip reference on the comment rather than a bare URL, and renders the existing comment-video card (task-detail-sheet.tsx:5732-5770) with its processing state. Checks: paste a copied clip link and assert the card shows the clip's title and plays; paste a foreign URL and assert it stays a link. Break patches: the route ignores the token; the paste handler falls back to plain text.


*Update, 30 September:* the per-clip route this row says is missing now exists, from `resume-defects/resume-7`. `/clips/<token>` and `GET /public/clips/:token` give a clip's title, length, a playable URL and who it opens for, and that is what a pasted link would read to render the clip. What is still missing is the paste itself, turning a clip link into the clip in a description, a comment or a doc, and the clips table that `clip_links` would join or be absorbed into.

*Triage, 5 October:* a feature, not a defect (confirmed unbuilt). Still unbuilt: a pasted /clips/<token> link stays a bare URL in the composer, is stored as plain text, and renders as plain text with no player and no title, although the per-clip route and public endpoint now exist. The triage's skeptic reproduced a defect beside it, now counted as `found-5-oct/comment-links-not-links`. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*Closed, 8 October* (lane 7), on the owner's word of 8 October, with `ledger-rows/row-1307`. ClickUp embeds a clip's link where it is shared: "Clip links auto-embed in Chat for instant viewing", and a clip embedded in a task's description plays there (its help centre, through search excerpts). The pieces this item waited on are built: a clip's stable link and its identity are `clip_links` (`resume-defects/resume-7`), a token per clip that `/clips/<token>` and `GET /public/clips/:token` resolve, signing the clip again on every view, which is the identity a `clips` table was to give. What was left was the paste. Built so:
- `clip-links.ts` reads the clips a piece of text links to: this site's own `/clips/<token>` (an absolute address on this origin, or the path alone), a token of the shape `ClipsService` makes (24 random bytes, base64url) and nothing else, each once, in order, at most three; the same path on another site is somebody else's page and stays a link;
- `ClipEmbed` draws each under the text as the clip — its title, a player and its length, and the link to its own page — from what the link itself opens (`GET /public/clips/:token`), so it opens for exactly whom the link opens: anyone where its workspace allows public links, its members where it does not. A clip the reader may not watch, or a deleted one, is said in words (four locales), not drawn as a player that fails; a signature that lapses under an open card is asked for again once;
- under a chat message (not in the edit history), a task's comment, a reply and a thread's root and replies, and a task's description — drawn outside the area that opens the description's editor, so pressing play plays.

Measured on lane 7 with `clip-link-embeds`, two workspaces of the run's own (one as every workspace starts, one keeping its links to its members) and three clips uploaded as the app uploads one (presign, then a PUT to the lane's store):
- Before (batch 23's bundle): 1 of 6 — the link drawn as a bare address everywhere; only "the same path on another site stays a link" passed.
- After: 6 of 6.

Checks (`clip-link-embeds`, 6): "a clip’s link posted in a chat channel is drawn as the clip under the message: its title, its length, and a player whose address plays from the store", "and the same link in a task’s comment is drawn as the clip under the comment", "the same path on another site stays a link and is drawn as no clip, nor is an address of another shape", "and in a task’s description, drawn under it — pressing its player plays it and opens no editor", "a clip its link does not open for the reader — one its workspace keeps to its members, read by somebody who is not one — is said, not drawn as a player, while the open workspace’s clip plays for them", "a deleted clip’s link is said to be unavailable, not drawn as a player that fails". Unit: `clip-links.test.ts`, 3.

### `found-23-sep/connected-search-per-person` — **closed** (feature, medium; was not counted, a feature) · reproduced 12 October

**Each member should search their OWN mail and files; today one person's connection is the workspace's only one**

*Evidence:* `workspace_integration_connections` is unique on (workspace, provider), so a second member connecting Google replaces the first's grant — and since 23 September a grant answers only the person who connected it, so everyone else's Gmail, Drive and SharePoint tabs say "Connected with someone else's account". The frame (§V2-11 `19:07`, "meri Gmail pe jaa ke") is a person searching their own mailbox.

*To close:* research ClickUp's Connected Search — which apps each person connects for themselves and which an admin connects for the workspace, and what a member sees of the latter — then store per-person grants beside the workspace one (the calendar accounts already do: `user_calendar_accounts`), connect from the person's own settings, and search with the searcher's own grant. A suite per source: two members, each finding only their own.

*Triage, 5 October:* a feature, not a defect (confirmed unbuilt). Connected search allows one grant per workspace and provider, and that grant answers only the person who connected it. Per-person Gmail, Drive and SharePoint grants are unbuilt. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*Closed, 12 October* (lane 8), as ClickUp works it. ClickUp (help centre, "Connected Search", through search excerpts, 12 October): an app is connected two ways. A personal connection is anybody's but a guest's, made for themselves, and its results — their private files and mail too — are theirs alone; a Workspace connection is an owner's or admin's, and through it every member finds what the connected account shares with the whole organisation, and nothing private. Gmail is personal only. Guests do not use Connected Search. Built so:
- one's own Google Drive, Gmail or SharePoint (`user_search_connections`, migration 0183): `POST /workspaces/:id/search/connect/:provider` starts the consent, its callback keeps the grant for that person alone — the workspace's connection untouched — and comes back to search; `DELETE …/search/connections/:provider` takes it away; a guest is refused in words (403);
- whose connection answers: one's own first, then the workspace's — Drive asked only for what is shared with the whole organisation (`anyoneCanFind`, `anyoneWithLink`, `domainCanFind`, `domainWithLink`), SharePoint without anybody's OneDrive; a workspace Gmail connected before this answers its connector alone; a guest is answered by none (`federatedCredential`);
- a source says whose it is (`listSources`: `heldBy` you, the workspace, or nobody, and whether this person may connect their own), and the search palette says it — the workspace's, shared things only, with Connect your own; your own, with Disconnect; or not connected, with the offer — and App Center's Connect only for an admin, never for Gmail;
- the lanes and CI answer Drive, Gmail and Graph search, and Google's consent and profile, from the calendar stub (`GOOGLE_DRIVE_API_URL`, `GMAIL_API_URL`, `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_API_URL`, `GOOGLE_USERINFO_URL`), so a search reaches a source that holds what the suite put there.

Measured: before (main's lane 4, the tree before it): `connected-search` 0 passed, 2 failed, 2 of 11 run — the personal connect route 404, and the workspace's Drive answered everybody with its connector's private files. After (lane 8): 11 of 11 (8 of 11 on the way: the phrase searched was not in the shared file's name, and the connect route answers 201); `search-sources`, re-aimed, 11 of 11; unit `search.service.test.ts` and `drive-scope.test.ts`, 71 of 71. A guard was misplaced on the way: the new route took the calendar route's decorators, leaving the disconnect and the calendar route unguarded — each route has its own now.

Checks (`connected-search`, 11): "nothing connected: Drive, Gmail and SharePoint say not connected, and each member may connect their own", "through the workspace’s Drive a member finds what is shared with the whole organization and not the connector’s private file — Drive was asked for the shared ones alone", "SharePoint through the workspace finds the organisation’s sites and no one’s OneDrive", "a mailbox is personal: the Gmail Olga connected for the workspace is searched for her alone, and for Max it is not connected", "and through the workspace’s Drive its connector finds the shared files too, not her own private ones", "a member connects their own Gmail: the consent comes back to search, and her own connection is kept — the workspace’s untouched (read by SQL)", "her mail is searched for her alone: she finds it, Max does not, and her source says it is her own", "with her own Drive connected, Mia’s search reaches her private files — Drive asked for everything she may see — and Max’s still reaches only the workspace’s shared ones", "a guest uses no Connected Search: the workspace’s Drive finds them nothing, connecting their own is refused in words (403), and their sources say so", "the palette tells Max his Drive results are the workspace’s, shared things only, and offers to connect his own — and that his Gmail is not connected, with the same offer", "Mia’s palette says her Gmail is her own and offers to disconnect it; disconnected, it is gone (read by SQL) and her mail is searched no more".

Built so:

- the Button type (migration 0184): its words, no value (refused, 400), and `POST …/custom-fields/:fieldId/press`, which asks the task's write rule and runs the automations whose trigger is `button.clicked` for that field — a rule must name a Button of the workspace (400) — and says how many ran; the automation builder offers "A button is pressed" with the workspace's Buttons;
- the Relationship is the `tasks` type with `config.listId` — a list its maker may open, kept once made (400) — and `config.rollups`, fields that list's tasks have; a value outside the list is refused (400); the field's read gives each rollup's value on each related task the reader may open; the sheet's picker searches that list alone (`GET /tasks/workspace/:id?listId=`), and draws the rollups under each related task;
- the task sheet's field form offers the AI fields (with their instruction, language and fill settings), a Button's words, a Relationship's list and rollups; an AI field carries ✦ Generate, a Button presses and says what ran;
- the lanes' model stub answers each kind in the product's own words, a Dropdown with the first option its prompt lists.

- Add credits buys packs of 10,000 through the payment provider's checkout (`POST /:workspaceId/billing/ai-credits/checkout`, `workspace.billing`): one to a hundred packs (400 otherwise, in words); a server with no payment provider says so (400); a purchase counts only once its checkout is paid (`checkout.session.completed`).

### `found-9-oct/task-email-sends-from-the-server` — **closed** (feature, large; was not counted, a feature) · reproduced 12 October

**A task's email is sent from the server's address, "via Rundesk"; ClickUp sends it from the person's own mailbox**

*Evidence, 9 October:* ClickUp's Email ClickApp sends from the person's connected email account — Gmail, Outlook, or another over IMAP — with their signature, saved templates and a time to send (help centre, "Use Email in ClickUp", through search excerpts). Rundesk sends a task's email from the server's own address, named "<the writer> via Rundesk", its answers coming back to an address of its own (`comment-email.service.ts`), with no signature, template or send time.

*To close:* connect a mailbox per person (each provider's OAuth app, the owner's to register), send from it and read its answers from it; signatures, templates and a send time on the Email form.

*Closed, 12 October* (lane 8), as ClickUp works it. ClickUp (help centre, "Use Email in ClickUp", "Schedule comments and emails"; read through search excerpts, 9 and 12 October): the comment box's From links an email account — Gmail or Outlook, signed in at the provider — under a sender name, and its owner chooses the teammates who may send from it too; the email goes from that mailbox and its answers are read from it into the task; on Business and above a person keeps signatures and the workspace has templates; Free Forever has one account of 100 uses, Unlimited (Pro here) one with no cap and scheduling, Business two; the arrow beside Send sends later, and the task lists it until then, to be sent now or cancelled. Built so:
- a mailbox is linked through the provider's own consent asking to send and read mail (Google's `gmail.send` and `gmail.readonly`; Microsoft's `Mail.ReadWrite` and `Mail.Send` — a draft is how Graph threads an answer), kept as its linker's (`email_accounts`, migration 0186) under a sender name they choose; a guest links none (403, in words), only Gmail and Outlook are linked to send from (400), and a plan's number of mailboxes is refused in words before the provider is asked;
- From offers a person their own mailboxes and those shared with them — shared by their linker alone (403 for anybody else) — and the server's address beside them, which is where it differs: ClickUp has no server address, and a workspace with no mailbox linked still sends a task's email as it did on 9 October;
- an email from a mailbox goes through that provider (Gmail's `messages.send`; Graph's draft, then send), file and all, and the server's own mail sends nothing; it is kept as the task's email with the mailbox and its thread, and takes one use;
- its answers are read from that thread every two minutes (`EMAIL_REPLY_POLL_SECONDS`), each landing in the task once, under the email, without the quote of what it answers; answering one by email goes from the same mailbox, in the same thread, naming the answer it answers;
- a grant the provider refuses is said in its words (502) and the mailbox marked to link again; linked again it is the same mailbox;
- a person keeps signatures, one the default, theirs alone; templates are shared with everybody or kept by their maker, changed only by their maker or an owner or admin — both on Business and above (403, in words, below);
- the arrow beside Send sends in an hour, tomorrow at nine, next Monday at nine or at a time chosen; the email is kept, listed on the task for its writer alone, sent from the mailbox at its time (every `TASK_EMAIL_SCHEDULE_SECONDS`), cancelled or sent now from the list; Free does not schedule (403);
- the Email settings page (`/app/:workspaceId/email`, from the composer's From menu) lists the workspace's mailboxes to whoever may manage them, changes a sender name and links Gmail or Outlook; a refused consent is said on return.

Measured: before (lane 8 on wt-b35 at `8490475`, the tree before it): `POST /workspaces/:id/email-accounts/connect/gmail` was a 404 and a task's email went from the server's address alone. After: lane 8, 19 of 19 (on the way: a fill with no timeout hung the suite eleven minutes — the suite now sets a page timeout and opens the comments tab first; linking a mailbox again was refused by the room check and is now allowed to its owner; the owner-or-admin rule named roles that do not exist and now asks `isAdminRole`; the suite closed its stack by a `stop` it does not have, so every run sat until `timeout` killed it — `found-12-oct/suites-stop-a-stack-with-no-stop` — and exits in 28 seconds now; under the break runs' load it threw at three steps — the Email row pressed while it was still checking, or left outside the window, the arrow's In 1 hour with no form under it, the settings page opened while Link Gmail was still on its way to Google — and passed an undefined id to SQL where a send went unscheduled; each step now waits or reads null, so what fails is its check; and its refused grant was staged for the mailbox's next call of any kind, which the two-second poll for answers could take first, so the send was refused 409 before Google was asked — the stub stages it on the mailbox's writes now, `on: "write"`); unit `mail-message.test.ts`, 6. ### `ledger-rows/row-2294` — **closed** (feature, large; was not counted, a feature; triage, 5 October; was: open, large) · reproduced 13 October

**The AI acts inside a connected app — absent**

*Evidence:* reaudit.md:2294-2321 (M). COMMAND_TOOLS (ai-command.ts:179-246, plus create_list/create_folder at :118-123 and :265) are all internal. ai-categories.ts:62-78 marks externalActions/externalSearches unsupported with reasons. Parts that exist: calendar-sync's Google event upsert, and the Gmail/SharePoint search providers. The §5 note that AiService injects SearchService and never calls it is FIXED: it was removed (ai.service.ts:915-921).

*To close:* Add connector tools, e.g. book a meeting via calendar-sync, and search/send via Gmail. Measure them on a model-stub lane with provider stubs.

*Triage, 5 October:* a feature, not a defect (confirmed unbuilt). The AI cannot act in or search a connected app. Every AI tool acts on Rundesk's own data, and the AI value report marks both external categories as unsupported. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*Closed, 13 October* (lane 10), as ClickUp works it. ClickUp's AI acts through a person's own connections, as that person (help centre, "Use Gmail tools with ClickUp AI" and "Google Calendar integration"; AlternativeTo, July 2025, "connection between Brain and Google Calendar"; read through search excerpts, 12 and 13 October): with Google Calendar it creates an event — a title (the one thing it needs), a start, a duration, a description, a location and attendees — and drafts the invite for the person to approve; with Gmail it creates drafts and searches them; Connected Search lets it read what their apps hold. Here, on the AI page's Commands tab, where every change is previewed and written only once confirmed (`ai-connected.ts`):
- `create_calendar_event`: an event in the asker's own calendar — the default one their planner writes to, Google or Outlook — at the time they meant in their own zone (`users.timezone`), inviting whom it names: Google is asked to send the invitations (`sendUpdates=all`), Graph sends them with the event. The preview draws the title, the time in their zone, the attendees and the place;
- `draft_email`: a draft left in the Drafts of a mailbox the asker linked themselves (`found-9-oct/task-email-sends-from-the-server`), never one shared with them, and never sent from here. Gmail is now asked for `gmail.compose` when a mailbox is linked, and a mailbox linked before that is told to be linked again rather than refused at Google;
- `search_connected_apps` (read-only): the asker's own Drive, Gmail and SharePoint, searched as Connected Search searches them for that person (`found-23-sep/connected-search-per-person`); what it found is drawn under the plan, linked;
- refused in words where the asker has nothing connected — where to connect a calendar, link a mailbox or connect a search source — and, at the confirm, in the provider's terms ("Google Calendar refused the grant…: connect it again"). The Commands tab said a refusal by its code (`reconnect`, `name_taken`) and says its sentence now. The executor checks again everything an action carries — its workspace, its times, its addresses — because an action comes back in the body of `/ai/command/execute`;
- §V2-11's last two tiles, External app actions and External app searches, count the command turns that reached a connected app (`command.connected_action`, `command.connected_search`) and are no longer marked unsupported; the App Center's MCP panel says what the AI still cannot do, which is call a server a workspace registers.

Measured: before (`fc287a9`; lane 9 with a model, lane 8 without), `ai-connected-apps` 0 of 11 on both — Gmail was asked to send and read, never to leave drafts; the tool calls a model would make were not tools, so the Commands tab drew no event and no draft; `/ai/command/execute` answered an event or a draft action `201` with no result at all; and the two tiles were still marked unsupported. After: lane 10 (a model) 11 of 11, lane 4 (none) 11 of 11. Units `ai-connected.test.ts` 15 and `ai-categories.test.ts` 10 (108 of 108 with their neighbours); `check-model-stub` 14 cases and 14 mutations, `check-calendar-stub` with its two new cases and 12 mutations. Its neighbours pass on lanes 4 and 10, 13 of 13: `ai-action-categories` 29, `app-catalogue` 26, `task-email-accounts` 19, `ai-create-containers` 33, `create-ai-results` 2, `create-menu-ai` 24, `comment-email` 18, `calendar-accounts` 37, `personal-calendar-connect` 6, `connected-search` 11, `ai-generate-fields` 4 and `ai-model-picker` 32.

*Closed, 13 October* (lane 8), as ClickUp works it. ClickUp's Imports (help centre and ClickUp's own pages, read through search excerpts, 12 and 13 October): its Spreadsheets Importer takes .xls, .xlsx, .csv, .json, .tsv and .txt; its Docs import takes Word, HTML and Markdown; Confluence comes in from the space's HTML export; Slack from its export, the public channels with their threads and reactions and the newest 10 000 messages a channel; Basecamp by signing in to it, its projects as Spaces of lists or as Folders in one Space, its to-dos as tasks with their notes, assignees and comments; Monday's boards as Folders and Lists. Here, on the Imports page, a tab for each row of frame `12:08`'s submenu and no box of tools it cannot import:
- **Spreadsheet files** read the six. A workbook is uploaded as the file it is — to the store, under its importer's own key (`import-files.ts`), because the API takes 1 MiB of JSON and a workbook's bytes do not survive being read as text — and read by the server with no dependency: a zip reader (`zip-read.ts`: the central directory, deflate through zlib, Zip64, a CRC and the declared size checked, a bomb stopped while it inflates), an XML scanner that expands no entity a document defines (`xml-scan.ts`), the .xlsx reader (shared strings, styles' dates, the 1904 system, the first visible sheet) and the .xls reader (the compound file's FAT and mini stream, BIFF8's shared strings, numbers, RKs, formulas' results and dates). A JSON file is a list of tasks. Monday's "Export board to Excel" is not one table — the board's name, then each group's name, its column names again, its items and a row of sums — so it is read as the board: each item keeps its group, which becomes its list, the board's name names the import, and the rows of Monday's own are left out and counted (`readExportLayout`). Wrike's export lists a task once for every folder it is in, under one Key: it is made once. "Working on it", Monday's own, is In progress.
- **Document files**: Word (.docx: headings by style and outline level, bold, italic, strike, links by relationship and by HYPERLINK field, numbered and bulleted lists by level, tables, a deleted revision left out), HTML (a tolerant tree: its `<title>` the title, a first `<h1>` saying the same not said twice), Markdown and text. A guest may import a document where they may make one.
- **Confluence**: the space's HTML export, its page tree read from `index.html`'s "Available Pages", each page's words from `#main-content` and nothing around them; one Doc named for the space with its pages nested inside as Confluence nests them, and a page the tree names and the zip lacks named, not made.

### `ledger-rows/row-745` — **closed** (feature, large; was not counted, a feature; triage, 5 October; was: open, medium) · reproduced 13 October

**@ picker Brain section and Agents — still absent**

*Evidence:* reaudit.md:745 says Brain and Agents are 'blocked rather than pending'. task-detail-sheet.tsx:299-305: MentionTab is 'people'|'tasks'|'docs'|'whiteboards'|'locations'|'channels', and the comment refuses Brain/Agents because 'The Brain² hub is a recorded decision'. The AI service and dock exist (see row-743), so an @Brain mention that asks the AI in the thread has something to call. Agents have nothing: no agents schema or module.

*To close:* @Brain: research how ClickUp's @Brain answers in a comment thread, then build it on ai.service + comment create, measured on a model-stub lane. Agents: wait for row-852's Super Agents.

*Triage, 5 October:* a feature, not a defect (confirmed unbuilt). The @ picker has six sections and no Brain or Agents section. @Brain could be built on the existing AI service, but Agents cannot be built until Super Agents (row-852) exists. Evidence: `docs/triage-2026-10-05.md`.

*13 October:* the Agents half is built with `ledger-rows/row-852`: the comment @ picker has an Agents tab listing the agents the reader may use, and Chat's picker an Agents section, each inserting a mention the agent answers in the thread (`super-agents.mjs`, `sa-29`, `sa-30`). The Brain section — @Brain answering in a comment thread — is what is left.

*Closed, 13 October (batch 40b), as ClickUp's @Brain works.* The research is ClickUp's help on @mentioning Brain and on using Brain on task comments. @Brain in a comment answers right away, in that comment's thread. By default it draws only on what is public in the workspace. It reads a private item only when it was asked inside one, or when the prompt links to one. Its reply is read by everybody who can see the task, including people the private data it drew on would refuse. Each new question names it again. Built that way:
- **The picker.** The @ picker opens with frame `04:00`'s Brain section, "Brain² — Ask, Build, Create", above the people, and picking it writes `@Brain`. Its Agents section now ends in "+ Create Agent", which opens a new Super Agent.
- **The answer.** A comment naming `@Brain`, in any case, is answered by Brain's own account. That account is an agent's, so it is on no roster, never notified, and follows nothing. The answer goes in the comment's thread and is posted where its asker may comment (`brain-comments.ts`).
- **What Brain reads.** It reads the task, the thread, and the workspace knowledge its asker may read. Of that it keeps only what has no private or personal space, private folder, or private or Personal List above it. Two exceptions: what is in the task's own list, and what the comment links (`?task=<id>`, `/docs/<id>`).
- **What starts it.** Brain's own words start nothing. Where no model answers, the picker's Brain row says why it is greyed out, and a posted @Brain says it will not be answered.

`brain-comments-and-decks.mjs` checks this, with the model stub and without one. The stub signs each answer with the task it was asked on and the knowledge it was given, so the suite reads what Brain was allowed to know from its words. Building it also fixed three things:
- **The stub's prompt reading.** The stub read a system prompt sent as text blocks as its JSON, its lines escaped into one. It now reads the words, and `check-model-stub.mjs` holds it to that.
- **Agents following tasks.** An agent's account followed every task it commented on (`NotificationsService.autoFollowEnabled`). It now follows none.
- **Strings that print their braces.** `found-13-oct/single-brace-placeholders-print-themselves`.

The ai_usage metering exists (reaudit.md:6558-6564). Only the allowance and reset are missing, which the frames never give.

*To close:* Rotating placeholder: built 29 September (`commit-log/log-4ad25f6-1`). Credit meter: allowance and reset from ClickUp research, reading ai_usage.
